description: Original Mavic 3 dual-camera aircraft featuring a 4/3 CMOS 20 MP Hasselblad wide camera (24 mm equivalent f/2.8-f/11) and a 1/2-inch CMOS telephoto camera with up to 28x hybrid zoom. Standard Mavic 3 has 8 GB internal storage and does not inherit Cine-only Apple ProRes recording or internal 1 TB SSD. Aircraft identity remains separate from Fly More/Cine bundles, controllers and batteries.
flightTime: Up to 46 min at 32.4 km/h, sea-level/no-wind equivalent; Brake/photo, to forced low-battery landing
chargingTime: Approximately 96 min with DJI 65W portable charger; charge-state interval unspecified

handType: Compatible with off-the-shelf 5 mm and 10 mm laparoscopic instruments and scopes
dof: Multi-arm laparoscopic assistance system with gravity-defying holding and intelligent scope control
description: Maestro is Moon Surgical’s robotic-assisted laparoscopy platform designed to augment surgical teams. The system features multi-arm patient-side assistance with gravity-defying arms that hold instruments steadily without clutching or foot pedals, and ScoPilot intelligent scope control allowing the surgeon to position the laparoscope directly using held instruments. Maestro integrates into existing clinical workflows and supports commercially available 5 mm to 10 mm laparoscopic instruments and scopes. Commercial availability covers the US, EU, and UK following regulatory clearances.
driveMode: Surgeon-controlled bedside assistance arms with ScoPilot scope navigation; not autonomous surgery

description: IP67-rated tracked unmanned ground-vehicle chassis with dual 1,500 W motors and reinforced suspension. It crosses 18 cm obstacles and climbs 30-degree slopes. It has CAN interfaces plus ROS and Autoware support for research and field robots. Announced in November 2021.
Lightweight pneumatic powered knee orthosis registered as an FDA Class I device for knee pain from osteoarthritis, instability or weak quadriceps. It reduces knee load by unloading the quadriceps.

Fixed-wing eVTOL home-delivery drone. It hovers at about 300 ft while a tethered, thruster-guided droid lowers packages onto a target about one meter across. It docks and recharges autonomously and has a 10-mile service radius.

Fully automated massage table that uses two robotic arms. It builds a 3D body scan from over one million data points to personalize each session, and is deployed at Equinox clubs, hotels and Massage Envy locations.

Indoor security robot designed by fuseproject, with around 60 sensors (lidar, depth, thermal, 360-degree cameras), a badge reader and two-way video. It runs autonomously with remote human operators supervising.
First miniaturized robotic-assisted surgery device, with a tray-to-table design that needs no dedicated OR layout. FDA De Novo-authorized for colectomy in 2024.
Mobile manipulator with a 7-DOF arm, telescoping torso lift, RGB-D head camera and 2D laser scanner. Introduced for warehouse and research use; its arm carries 6 kg at full extension.
Autonomous mobile base for moving warehouse material, with lidar and a 3D camera for navigation and obstacle avoidance. Larger 500 and 1500 kg variants also exist.

Autonomous smoothie kiosk where a robotic arm portions fresh ingredients, blends and dispenses custom drinks. Makes up to 45 blends per hour. The first commercial kiosk launched in March 2019; deployed with Jamba and at universities.

Collaborative pipe and roll-welding robot from Vancouver. A long-reach manipulator carries a three-axis arm that follows the operator's hand, including the weave motion. It welds flanges, tees, elbows and reducers. The spec sheet gives a 4 x 4 ft footprint, a 15 ft (4.5 m) reach, GMAW/FCAW/MCAW processes and roughly 3500 lb. It launched at FabTech 2017.

Dual-torch version of the Spool Welding Robot that uses Lincoln Electric's twin-wire GMAW-P HyperFill process for fill and cap passes and STT on the root. It handles carbon-steel pipe and vessels 0.5 to 2.5 in thick and as small as 6 in in diameter. It was unveiled at FabTech 2021.

Fully autonomous TIPTIG (hot-wire TIG) pipe-welding system that welds with no operator intervention. Novarc claims up to 4 lb/h deposition and up to 300% faster travel than conventional TIG. It has a 4 x 4 ft footprint and supports up to four positioners. It was unveiled at Schweissen & Schneiden in September 2025.

Second-generation robotic digital microscope (exoscope) on a robotic arm from Toronto-based Synaptive. It has instrument tracking, automatic focus and hands-free control, and works with Synaptive's BrightMatter neurosurgery platform. It was released in October 2017.

Configurable medical cobot platform from Cobionix in Kitchener, Ontario, designed for patient-facing tasks such as diagnostic ultrasound. It currently runs ultrasound by teleoperation, and fully autonomous ultrasound is in development. Clinical tasks are reconfigured through tool changes and over-the-air software updates. Launch was planned for the UK at the end of 2025, then Canada in 2026 and the US in mid-2026.

Self-driving passenger mobility pod for airport terminals from Vancouver-based A&K Robotics. Riders pick a destination and Cruz navigates among pedestrians using 360-degree 3D sensing, managed through the CruzFleet cloud software. It was tested at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport in 2022 and has since been deployed with operators including Vancouver International Airport (YVR).

Industrial multirotor UAV from Saskatoon-based Draganfly. It flies automated missions or manual flights and takes interchangeable delivery, imaging and LiDAR payloads. Draganfly states a 67 lb payload lift capacity and up to 55 minutes of flight time. It launched in June 2022.

Weather-resistant, high-endurance multirotor UAV with drop and winch-down delivery systems. It carries up to 26 lb of payload and has a triple-redundant-IMU, Blue UAS certified autopilot. It launched in June 2022 alongside the Heavy Lift drone.

Compact, transportable surveillance UAV for military and law enforcement, derived from the Commander 3XL. It has quick-release payloads and optional NVIDIA Jetson Orin onboard computing. Draganfly states up to 45 minutes of flight time and a 5 lb payload. It launched in September 2024.

NDAA-compliant modular FPV drone system for government and defence, with arm assemblies that swap between sizes in minutes. It launched in May 2024 as the FlexForce Modular FPV System. The current page lists 5-, 7-, 10- and 13-inch configurations, 450 g to 3 kg of payload and speeds up to 90 mph.

Long-endurance autonomous underwater vehicle powered by a hydrogen fuel cell, from Burnaby, BC; it was formerly called Solus-LR. The manufacturer page gives 8.5 m length, 1 m diameter, 3700 kg displacement, a 2000 km submerged range, 15-day endurance, a 500-litre flooded payload bay and 2000 m operating depth. Solus-LR demonstration missions were completed in July 2022.

Extra-large uncrewed underwater vehicle for subsea surveillance, powered by a hydrogen fuel-cell air-independent propulsion system; it was formerly called Solus-XR. The manufacturer states over 45 days of submerged endurance, a 5000 km range, modular 2500-litre payload bays, an 8-knot speed and a size that fits a 40 ft ISO container. Sea trials began in 2023.

Power-line inspection robot that travels along high-voltage transmission lines. It was developed by Hydro-Québec's research institute, which earlier built LineScout. In 2018, Hydro-Québec's product arm MIR Innovations was promoting it as a finished product alongside the LineDrone corrosion sensor.

Autonomous mobile UV-light disinfection robot from Canadian custom-robotics firm AIS, adapted from the company's agricultural robot platform with NGen funding. It is aimed at hospitals, hotels and malls. It launched in July 2021.

Turnkey robotic sanding cell from Montreal-based Vention, built on a FANUC CRX-30iA cobot with a laser panel-measurement system and a PushCorp sanding tool. It was developed with 3M for cabinet-making and woodworking. It launched in February 2025 as part of Vention's Rapid Series.

MAV (Multi-Sensing Autonomous Vehicle) is NEURA's autonomous mobile robot family, first shown at Automatica 2022. It comes as MAV 500 (500 kg payload, 12 h uptime), MAV 1500 (1500 kg, 10 h) and MAV+ (500-1000 kg). All versions run at 1.5 m/s.

Lynx is Husarion's outdoor wheeled robot platform (v1.0). It has a 720 Wh hot-swappable battery, a 65 kg payload, 90% grade climbing with 36 kg of cargo, and IP54 or IP66 sealing. It won the Best Radiation Mapping Award at EnRicH 2025.

Myoelectric powered arm orthosis that reads surface EMG signals to drive the elbow and, on the Motion G version, the grasp. Built for people with arm paralysis after stroke, spinal cord or nerve injury. Comes in Motion E, W and G versions.

Eve is Wandercraft's self-balancing personal exoskeleton for adults with spinal cord injury. It walks hands-free, without crutches, using 12 motors. It is FDA-cleared, available by prescription and used with a trained companion. It went on sale in the US on 17 September 2026, with other regions to follow.
Two-wheeled-leg autonomous security patrol robot for large outdoor sites, offered as robotics-as-a-service. It works in all weather, uses thermal, RGB and infrared cameras and charges itself.

Second-generation Ascento Guard patrol robot. It has better night vision, a thermal camera with 160% higher resolution, longer person-detection range, a brighter spotlight and a 4:1 charge ratio. It balances and rights itself on and off road.
Heavy-duty AMR from Ankara-based Milvus Robotics. It navigates without fixed infrastructure using 360° LiDAR and has a 30 cm-high low-profile chassis. It was introduced in 2021 as the SEIT1500-S.

Seventh-generation FDA-cleared personal exoskeleton for people with T7-L5 spinal cord injuries. It has crutch-button control, several walking speeds, stair activation and tracking in the MyReWalk app. US sales began in April 2025.
AI-augmented powered back exoskeleton that gives up to 38 kg of dynamic lift assistance. It is aimed at logistics, industry, construction and nursing.
Powered, IP54-rated lifting exoskeleton for nursing and patient handling. Its motors give about 30 kg (66 lb) of lifting support. It went on sale in December 2023.
Powered exoskeleton revealed at CES 2025. It gives up to 80 lb (about 36 kg) of dynamic lift assistance plus walking support, with AI-personalised assistance and over-the-air updates.

handType: none
terrain: Indoor business premises: front of house, back of house and storage areas
description: Ring Rover Cam is Ring's autonomous indoor security robot for businesses, announced on 10 November 2026. Its AI Pilot system maps the premises, suggests patrol points and navigates around obstacles on its own. An adjustable periscope mast camera streams and records video at up to 4K. It also has a built-in siren and light tower, two-way audio and continuous person-motion detection. Sleep Mode retracts the periscope and mutes the microphone. Scheduled patrols require a compatible Ring Protect plan. US preorders open on 16 December 2026 at 999.99 USD. Amazon publishes no battery life, speed, mass, dimensions or drive details.
driveMode: Autonomous indoor patrol robot with adjustable periscope mast camera

description: Mid-size 2026-model-year agricultural drone from XAG for spraying, spreading and aerial survey, with a 55 kg maximum payload, 42 L/min maximum spray flow and a 90 L granule box. Unveiled together with the P200 at XAG's annual conference in November 2025.

Electric four-wheel-drive agricultural rover from XAG for precision spraying in orchards and greenhouses, with a 120 L tank, dual centrifugal atomizers and remote-controlled or autonomous route operation. It is 80 cm wide, travels at up to 1.5 m/s and was launched in 2025 as part of XAG's R Series.

Six-wheel electric agricultural rover from XAG for targeted spraying in orchards and greenhouses, with a 240 L tank and four pumps feeding four centrifugal atomizers at up to 16 L/min. It has a 130 kg curb weight and 1.5 m/s top speed; launched in 2025 as part of XAG's R Series.

Heavy-lift agricultural drone from DJI with a 100 kg operating payload for spraying, spreading and lifting tasks, and a maximum takeoff weight of up to 177 kg depending on configuration (175 kg standard 2-nozzle). It uses a coaxial twin-rotor layout with 62-inch propellers and combines LiDAR, millimeter-wave radar and a vision system for obstacle avoidance; launched in China in November 2024.

Agricultural drone from DJI with a 70 kg operating payload for spraying, spreading and lifting, equipped with DJI's Safety System 3.0. It weighs 52 kg with a DB1580 battery and measures 3200 x 3520 x 960 mm unfolded; launched in China in November 2024.

Agricultural drone from DJI for high-flow spraying, spreading and lifting/transport work, with an onboard battery heat sink to keep performance stable in high temperatures. It weighs 45 kg with battery in its standard two-nozzle, 50 L tank configuration; launched globally in 2026.

China-market heavy-lift agricultural drone from DJI rated for payloads of up to 200 kg, with support for up to four batteries and two-aircraft coordinated lifting of up to 360 kg. Launched in April 2026 with kits priced from 99,999 CNY.

DJI's first delivery drone, carrying 30 kg in dual-battery mode or 40 kg with a single battery, with a 95 kg maximum takeoff weight, IP55 rating and cargo-box or winch payload options. Announced in China in August 2023 and rolled out globally in January 2024.

Heavy-lift delivery drone from DJI with up to 80 kg payload in single-battery emergency mode (65 kg in normal dual-battery mode) and a 149.9 kg maximum takeoff weight, with interchangeable lifting and winch systems. It is IP55-rated and launched globally, excluding the U.S., in December 2025.

China-market heavy-lift logistics drone from DJI with a 200 kg payload, support for up to four batteries and dual- or quad-aircraft coordinated lifting. It shares its airframe with the DJI T200 and was launched in April 2026.

Flagship enterprise drone platform from DJI with up to 59 minutes of flight time, up to 6 kg payload capacity, and a built-in rotating LiDAR plus mmWave radar that can detect obstacles down to power lines. Aimed at emergency response, power-line inspection, mapping and construction work; launched in June 2025.

DJI's first eVTOL cargo drone, a lift-and-cruise design that takes off vertically and transitions to fixed-wing flight, with a claimed 50 kg (110 lb) payload and 150 km (93 mi) maximum range. Unveiled in July 2026 after high-altitude test flights at Mount Everest that reached 8,861 m.

Indoor-outdoor delivery robot from Chengdu Yuefan Innovation Technology, first shown at WRC 2026, that unloads parcels by itself at each door and confirms delivery by scanning the household barcode. It handles food, express parcels and emergency supplies and integrates with gates, elevators and access-control systems; Yuefan's delivery robots operate in thousands of buildings in China.

Guardian GT is a teleoperated force-multiplying robot from Sarcos (now Palladyne AI) of Salt Lake City, unveiled in 2017, with two hydraulic 7-DoF arms about 2.1 m long on a tracked base. Operators control it with force-reflective controls to lift up to 454 kg (1,000 lb); it has been discontinued.

Guardian S is a teleoperated snake-like inspection robot from Sarcos (now Palladyne AI), introduced in 2017 for industrial inspection, hazmat, search-and-rescue and bomb-squad support. It carries six 4K cameras for a 360-degree view, can climb stairs and magnetically scale metal surfaces, and is IP65-rated; it has been discontinued.

description: Aquanaut is an all-electric, untethered subsea vehicle from Houston-based Nauticus Robotics, first shown in 2019, that transforms from an AUV for long-distance survey into a half-humanoid ROV form with two manipulator arms. The current Aquanaut 2.1 configuration of the Mk2 platform offers autonomous transit, survey and inspection with up to 72 hours endurance and depth ratings up to 3,000 m.

Harvey is an autonomous mobile robot from Harvest Automation that locates, picks up and spaces potted plants in nurseries and greenhouses, working alone or in fleets. First delivered to customers in 2012, it uses a forward-looking laser range finder and boundary sensors, carries up to 10 kg and was priced at about 30,000 USD per robot.

QB is an early self-balancing telepresence robot from Anybots of Mountain View, California, shown in 2009 and offered for sale on the company's website from May 2010. It has a height-adjustable mast up to 1.83 m with a head carrying a display, two cameras, microphones and a laser pointer, balances on two wheels and runs 6 to 8 hours on lithium-ion batteries.

PackBot is a man-portable tracked robot for bomb disposal, surveillance, CBRN/hazmat detection and other dangerous missions, originally developed by iRobot in 2000 and now made by Teledyne FLIR; more than 4,000 have been delivered. The current PackBot 510 climbs stairs, is deployable by one person in under two minutes, and its manipulator lifts up to 20 kg.

Kobra is a heavy-payload tracked unmanned ground vehicle for EOD, reconnaissance, CBRN detection and nuclear maintenance, originally developed by iRobot (2011) and now sold by Teledyne FLIR as Kobra 725. Its manipulator lifts up to 150 kg with 350 cm vertical reach, and it climbs stairs and carries up to 68 kg of sensor payloads.

SUGV 325 is a single-person-lift modular unmanned ground robot from Teledyne FLIR Defense for EOD, reconnaissance and remote inspection, launched in 2024. It weighs about 9.1 kg in its lightest configuration, uses articulating flippers to climb stairs, carries HD visible, LWIR and 360-degree cameras, can lift 9.1 kg with its optional 5-DoF manipulator and runs up to eight hours.

Proteus is Amazon Robotics' first fully autonomous mobile robot, unveiled in 2022, which drives under and moves GoCarts of packages through Amazon fulfillment facilities in spaces shared with workers. It uses cameras and lidar for navigation, signals its intent with light and sound, and complies with the R15.08 industrial mobile robot safety standard.

VGo is a telepresence robot created by VGo Communications (later part of Vecna Robotics) that lets a remote user see, hear, talk and drive around an office, school or hospital over Wi-Fi or optional 4G LTE. Unveiled in 2010 and shipping from 2011 at about 6,000 USD, it is 1.22 m tall, weighs 8.2 kg and runs 6 to 12 hours per charge; it has been discontinued.

Wave Glider is an autonomous unmanned surface vehicle from Liquid Robotics (a Boeing company) that converts wave motion into propulsion and uses solar panels to power its computers and sensors, allowing months-long ocean missions without fuel. First developed in 2007, it consists of a surface float connected by an umbilical to a submerged wing glider and carries sensors for marine science, commercial and defense data collection.

description: The Saildrone Explorer is a 7 m wind- and solar-powered uncrewed surface vehicle from Alameda, California-based Saildrone for meteorological and oceanographic data collection, operating for up to 12 months at sea without a support vessel. It carries sensors for wind, air and sea temperature, CO2, chlorophyll, currents, seafloor depth and fish biomass, and has been used inside hurricanes; Saildrone vehicles have operated since 2015.

maxRuntime: 100 days
description: Voyager is a 10 m (33 ft) uncrewed surface vehicle from Saildrone, announced in March 2023, for near-shore bathymetry, coastal surveillance and maritime security missions. It uses an electric motor with wind-assisted propulsion, maps at 5 knots, carries radar, a PTZ infrared camera and seafloor-mapping sonar, and can run up to 100 days between service stops.

Surveyor is Saildrone's largest-production uncrewed surface vehicle class, launched in January 2021 for autonomous deep-water seabed mapping and long-range maritime ISR. The 20 m (65 ft) vessel combines wind and diesel propulsion, maps at 6 knots and carries radar, EO/IR, AIS and deep-water multibeam payloads; a lighter new-generation version was unveiled in March 2024.

Sparrow is an Amazon Robotics robotic arm system introduced in November 2022 that picks individual products from containers and places them into totes in Amazon fulfillment centers. It uses computer vision and AI with suction end-effectors to identify and handle millions of diverse items before they are packed.

Cardinal is an Amazon Robotics arm announced in 2022 that uses AI and computer vision to select a single package from a pile, lift it with suction, read the label and place it in the correct cart for outbound trucks. It handles packages up to 50 lb and works together with the Proteus autonomous mobile robot, which moves the filled carts.

Vulcan is Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch, unveiled in May 2025, which picks and stows items in the highest and lowest rows of inventory pods using force-sensing end-of-arm tooling and a camera-plus-suction picking arm. Amazon says it can handle about 75% of item types stored in its fulfillment centers at speeds comparable to employees and is deployed in Spokane, Washington and Hamburg, Germany.

Titan is an Amazon Robotics mobile drive unit introduced in November 2023 that lifts up to 2,500 lb, twice as much as the Hercules drive, to bring pods of heavy and bulky items to employees in fulfillment centers. It navigates a restricted robotics floor using computer vision and floor markers.

Blue Jay is a multi-arm robotic workcell from Amazon Robotics, introduced in October 2025, that coordinates several robotic arms to pick, stow and consolidate items in one station, handling about 75% of item types stored at Amazon sites. It was tested at a facility in South Carolina to support Same-Day sites; Amazon stated in a February 2026 update that it was no longer utilizing Blue Jay in operations.

Sequoia is an Amazon robotic inventory system announced in October 2023 and first deployed in Houston, Texas, in which mobile robots move totes to a containerized storage system and to ergonomic employee workstations. Amazon says it lets fulfillment centers identify and store inventory up to 75% faster.

maxRuntime: 18 hours
description: Carter is a collaborative mobile robot from Robust.AI, the company co-founded by Rodney Brooks, for warehouse picking and material transport alongside workers. Unveiled as a concept in June 2022 and launched as Carter Pro in October 2024 with active and passive force sensing for tactile interaction, it carries 100 kg on configurable shelving, has 360-degree camera vision, a touchscreen and barcode scanner, and runs up to 18 hours.

The RPD 35 is an autonomous pile-driving robot from San Francisco-based Built Robotics for utility-scale solar farm foundations, launched in March 2023. It carries up to 224 piles (maximum payload 34,000 lb), supports piles up to 19 ft long and works with the RPS 25 surveying robot, which positions piles within 1.0 degree of plumb and 15 mm of design elevation, in fleets operating up to 24 hours a day.

Stretch Gen 2 is the second generation of Boston Dynamics' autonomous mobile trailer-unloading robot, unveiled on November 3, 2026. It adds automotive-grade connectors, an upgraded vacuum gripper, continuous-rotation joints, 81% less internal cabling and faster serviceability, unloads up to 1,000 cases per hour with multipick, runs two shifts per battery and fast-charges to 90% in about 75 minutes.
throughput: up to 1000 cases/hour

description: Atalante X is a self-balancing lower-limb rehabilitation exoskeleton from Wandercraft of Paris, launched in 2022 as the next generation of the Atalante exoskeleton first announced in 2019. With 12 actuated degrees of freedom and dynamic walking algorithms, it lets patients with severe gait impairment stand and walk hands-free, including multidirectional gait and turns.

Elios is a collision-tolerant inspection drone from Swiss company Flyability, introduced in 2016, enclosed in a protective carbon-fiber cage so it can fly inside boilers, tanks, tunnels and other confined spaces. It carries a Full HD and a thermal camera, flies about 10 minutes per battery and sold for around 25,000 USD; Flyability's current model is the Elios 3.

SpeedyBot (Feimaotui) is an indoor-outdoor last-mile delivery robot from Suzhou-based CSJBot (Pangolin Robot / Alpha Robotics), launched in December 2024 for takeout and parcel delivery. It uses multi-line 3D lidar, a four-wheel-drive four-wheel-steer chassis and an 80 L compartment, rides elevators autonomously, and is offered as Pro, Ultra and Omni versions, the Omni adding a 6-DOF arm for pressing elevator buttons and handling items.

The Oxbot (Chinese: 熊猫, Panda) F-series are factory material-transport AMRs from CSJBot (Pangolin Robot), launched in January 2025 (originally marketed as the Niumowang F500, since respecced into the current F150/300/600 line). The F150, F300 and F600 carry 150, 300 and 600 kg respectively, navigate with 40 m lidar SLAM plus two RGBD cameras, pass gates and ride elevators autonomously, and have a 13.3-inch touchscreen.

CatCop (Heimao Jingzhang, 'Black Cat Sheriff') is an autonomous security patrol robot from CSJBot (Pangolin Robot) for residential communities, parks and parking garages. It uses a 16-line lidar with 70 m range, a 30x optical-zoom PTZ camera, a thermal camera and starlight night vision, offers face recognition and an SOS button, and returns to its charger automatically.

Special Forces T1 (Tezhongbing T1) is a security patrol robot from CSJBot (Pangolin Robot) with a telescopic camera mast adjustable from 1350 to 1750 mm, a 360-degree PTZ camera, panoramic cameras, infrared night vision and 60 m lidar. It patrols indoors and outdoors on a four-wheel differential chassis, is rated IP54 and recharges automatically.

Timo (sold in China as Xiaoyu, 'Little Fish') is a reception and guide robot from CSJBot for schools, nursing homes, retail stores and exhibition halls. It has a 13.3-inch touchscreen, 6 degrees of freedom, 40 m laser SLAM navigation, face recognition and voice Q&A, and recharges automatically.

Fairy (sold in China as Jingling, 'Elf') is a mobile digital-signage and reception robot from CSJBot for exhibition halls, airports, banks and government service halls. It carries a 23.8-inch touchscreen on a 'swan-neck' body, a 5 MP camera for face recognition and 40 m lidar SLAM navigation, and offers an open API for custom services.

Renwoxing is an autonomous mobile convenience-store vehicle from CSJBot (Pangolin Robot) for scenic areas, malls, residential communities and industrial parks. It has a 1108 L cargo box with 300 kg capacity, uses two 16-line and one 32-line lidar, stereo and surround cameras, RTK-GPS and an NVIDIA Xavier computer for L4-level driving, and connects over 5G.

Yunji Technology's embodied-AI single-arm collaborative robot is a mobile manipulator for hotels, launched in July 2026 and used for tasks such as running hotel laundry rooms. It has a lifting body adjustable from 38 to 78 cm, a six-axis arm with 110 cm reach, vision sensors on the body, base and wrist, an onboard NVIDIA Orin computer and swappable grippers for cleaning, sorting and delivery tasks.

Yunji Technology's noodle-cooking robot is an automated noodle station for hotel dining areas that cooks noodles, rice noodles and wontons with customizable toppings. Guests place a bowl to order and the robot handles the process from portioning to serving, with a peak output of 66 bowls per hour; it was deployed at BTG Homeinns hotels in late 2025.
throughput: 66 bowls per hour (peak)

description: The Waterproof Ant is a 2-ton autonomous pallet forklift from Shenzhen Reeman, launched in October 2026 for moving pallets between factory buildings over open roads in rain. It has a whole-vehicle waterproof design, a top-mounted 48-channel lidar (IP67-tested, 150 m range), laser SLAM navigation, 3D-vision pallet recognition and automatic charging; Reeman quotes a reference price of about USD 14,000.

YIMA (YBOT20P) is an outdoor material-delivery robot from Shenzhen Reeman for factory roads, warehouses, connected buildings and residential parcel delivery. It carries 100 kg, navigates with dual-laser SLAM (360-degree top lidar up to 100 m plus a 230-degree front lidar), climbs 10% grades, runs 10-15 hours and can integrate with elevators and automatic doors; it is specified for dry paved roads, not rain.

Geely's 7 kW underbody AGV charging robot is an automatic EV charging robot unveiled at the Geely AI Smart Charging launch in September 2026 for residential communities and private parking spaces. The low-profile AGV drives under a parked car, aligns automatically with an underbody charging port and charges overnight; Geely said its three charging robots would launch in the near term.

Geely's 20 kW automatic charging robot is a compact robotic EV charger unveiled in September 2026 for shopping districts, office parks and public car parks with medium dwell times. It automates plug-in charging without driver involvement while limiting the load added to the local commercial power grid; it is one of three automatic charging robots Geely announced alongside its AI Smart Charging technology.

Geely's 1.5 MW ultra-fast charging robot is a robotic-arm megawatt EV charger unveiled in September 2026 for expressway service areas. A fully automatic arm with multimodal perception locates the charging port and connects the heavy liquid-cooled cable so drivers need not leave the car; it is the top model of the three automatic charging robots Geely announced.

PathFynder is UBTECH's autonomous smart wheelchair robot for elder-care facilities, parks and hospitals, launched in August 2022. It combines joystick driving with autonomous indoor-outdoor navigation, an RGBD camera for obstacle, step and curb detection, automatic braking and lane-keeping, and a removable lithium battery rated for at least 15 km.

Wassi is UBTECH's walking-assist and gait-training robot for rehabilitation and elder care, launched in August 2022. It drives itself to the user and back to its charger, electrically adjusts its handles (660-930 mm) and seat, offers touchscreen-guided training modes with real-time vital-sign monitoring and an emergency button, and has a seat rated for 100 kg.

Jingjie S1 is a compact autonomous outdoor sweeping robot from Guangzhou Saite Intelligence, launched on April 1, 2026 at 99,000 CNY (or 2,999 CNY per month rental) for residential estates, campuses and business parks. It plans routes and avoids obstacles with a 16-line lidar, automatically bags and drops collected waste, sprays water to suppress dust, sweeps up to 1350 mm wide at over 4,700 m² per hour and refills and recharges automatically.

Jingjie S5 (Zhisaijie S5) is an L4 small autonomous street-sweeping robot from Guangzhou Saite Intelligence, premiered at CCE 2025 in Shanghai for sidewalks, back alleys and municipal sanitation. It passes 1.1 m-wide lanes, automatically bags and drops waste, uses a blower to assist sweeping, recognizes traffic lights and sweeps up to 1300 mm wide; flagship versions carry a 32-line lidar.

Youxiaomei M7 is the seventh-generation hotel and office-building delivery robot from Shenzhen-based UDI (Excelland Robotics), launched at the 2026 Shanghai hotel expo on March 31, 2026. A movable divider switches it between two compartments (30 L + 25 L) and one 50 L compartment, it charges wirelessly, and upward- and downward-facing RGBD cameras provide stereo obstacle avoidance; it passes 62 cm corridors.

Youxiaomei MX is an embodied-AI indoor delivery robot from UDI (Excelland Robotics), launched on March 31, 2026 at the Meadin hotel development forum in Shanghai. A six-axis arm with gripper and 626 mm reach presses elevator buttons between 70 and 140 cm, so it rides elevators without IoT retrofits, and it can hand over items or knock on doors; it carries 10 kg in a 28 L compartment and navigates with fused VSLAM and laser SLAM.

Puductor 2 is Pudu Robotics' second-generation autonomous disinfection robot, launched in November 2020 for hospitals, schools, airports, transit stations and other public spaces during the COVID-19 pandemic. It combines ultrasonic dry-mist spraying from a 15 L disinfectant tank (four adjustable atomization levels) with a Philips UV-C lamp rated at 180 µW/cm² at 1 m behind a motorized shutter, and can be assigned tasks remotely.

The Cainiao Autonomous Vehicle GT Pro is an L4 driverless parcel-delivery vehicle for public roads from Alibaba's logistics arm Cainiao, launched in January 2025 as the first major upgrade of the 2024 Cainiao GT. It measures 3694 x 1299 x 2200 mm, carries 600-800 parcels in 5 m³ of cargo space with a 180 km range, and fuses one lidar with eleven HD cameras.

Cainiao's self-developed climbing robot is a rack-climbing bin-retrieval robot for automated warehouses, launched in April 2026 and upgraded at CeMAT Asia in November 2026. It climbs onto racks and retrieves totes from four sides, supports double-deep storage, and is used in cross-border e-commerce, fashion, electronics, FMCG, healthcare and automotive warehouses, with an international version for EU and US standards.

The Cainiao GT is an L4 autonomous parcel-delivery vehicle from Alibaba's logistics arm Cainiao, introduced in 2024 for public-road deliveries; by December 2024 it was operating in more than 30 counties and cities across over 10 Chinese provinces. It was succeeded by the larger GT Pro in January 2025.

Hussar Pro is a factory and warehouse delivery robot from Shenzhen Reeman for frequent in-plant transport of parts, tools, bins and work-in-progress. It carries 80 kg, positions and avoids obstacles with lidar plus a 3D vision system, runs on a lithium iron phosphate battery with automatic return to its charger, and supports remote scheduling and route planning.

The Z10 Pro is a 2.5-ton heavy-load L4 driverless urban logistics van from Zelos (Jiushi Intelligent), launched at the China International Fair for Investment and Trade in September 2026. Zelos lists a 2,500 kg payload, 12.5 m³ cargo box, 55.91 kWh battery and up to 300 km unladen range; a refrigerated Z10 Pro variant is also offered.

Rhino (RBOT30F) is an autonomous stacker forklift from Shenzhen Reeman, introduced in December 2024 for pallet handling in factories, warehouses and distribution centers. It is rated for 1,500 kg with a 2.5 m lift height and navigates by reflector-free laser SLAM with positioning accuracy of up to 10 mm, and the current 3.0 version adds 360-degree stereoscopic obstacle avoidance and elevator use; Reeman quotes a reference price of about USD 11,000.

X-ant is a 2-ton autonomous pallet forklift from Shenzhen Reeman, launched in April 2026 for narrow-aisle warehouses and factories up to 40,000 m² with EU and US pallets. It has 550 mm fork width, a 1448 mm turning radius, PLC plus industrial-PC control, marker-free laser SLAM navigation, and solid-state TOF lidar, multi-line lidar and 3D vision for 360-degree obstacle detection up to 50 m.

Hammer 2.0 is a forward-moving autonomous counterbalanced forklift from Shenzhen Reeman, launched in October 2025 for cross-shaped (field-shaped) pallets. It lifts 1.2 tons to 2.5 m, navigates by reflector-free laser SLAM with ±10 mm positioning, detects obstacles with lidar, ultrasonic sensors and 3D vision, turns within 1.13 m and supports quick battery swaps and automatic charging.

Promobot V.4 is the fourth-generation autonomous service robot from Russian company Promobot, presented at CES in January 2018 and used as a consultant, concierge, promoter and tour guide. It recognizes faces, holds conversations, navigates while avoiding obstacles, and can be fitted with a touchscreen, document scanner, card dispenser, printers and a payment terminal.

The Blueye X7 is an inspection-class underwater ROV from Norway's Blueye Robotics with seven thrusters, seven guest ports for payloads such as manipulators and sonars, a 4K camera and an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX for AI processing. It is rated to 500 m depth, weighs 20 kg in air and runs on dual batteries or optional topside power; it was launched in May 2026 as the company's new flagship.

The Blueye X3 Ultra is an upgraded portable mini-ROV from Blueye Robotics with a 4K HDR camera, onboard Jetson Orin NX AI processing, a new IMU and three guest ports for external equipment. It is rated to 305 m, moves at 1.5 m/s and weighs 8.6 kg; it was launched in May 2026 alongside the X7.

The Blueye X3 is a professional underwater drone (mini-ROV) from Blueye Robotics with three guest ports for grippers, sonars and positioning systems, four 350 W thrusters and a 305 m depth rating. It weighs 8.6 kg, runs about 2 hours on the standard battery or 5 hours on the high-capacity battery and was launched in June 2021; a recommended professional kit starts at 30,788 USD excluding VAT.

The Blueye Pro is a professional underwater drone from Blueye Robotics with a tilting Full HD camera, 3300-lumen LED lights and a 305 m depth rating, introduced in January 2020. It weighs 8.6 kg, travels at 1.5 m/s and runs 2 or 5 hours depending on battery; it has since been replaced by the Blueye X1 and X3.

The Brokk 110+ is a compact electric, remote-controlled demolition robot from Swedish maker Brokk, launched in January 2026 as the SmartPower+ successor to the Brokk 110. It weighs 990 kg, delivers 19.5 kW, fits in elevators and on car trailers, and reaches 4.3 m vertically with a breaker.

The Brokk 130+ is a compact-class remote-controlled demolition robot from Brokk, unveiled in April 2025 with the SmartPower+ platform. It weighs 990 kg, delivers 20.2 kW for a stated productivity of 3.1 m³/h and reaches 4.3 m vertically with a breaker.

The Brokk 170+ is a 1,600 kg electric remote-controlled demolition robot with 24 kW of power, introduced with Brokk's SmartPower+ generation at World of Concrete in January 2024. Brokk states IP65-equivalent dust and water protection for the new generation and a vertical reach of 4.8 m including breaker.

The Brokk 900 is Brokk's largest remote-controlled demolition robot, introduced in March 2021 for heavy demolition, mining and process-industry work. It weighs 11,400 kg, delivers 71 kW and reaches 9.1 m vertically with a breaker.

The R5 Pro is a grid-running bin-handling robot from Norway's AutoStore, introduced in October 2023 as a version of its Red Line R5 robot for large-scale, multishift e-commerce operations. AutoStore says it improves productivity per robot during extended operation, optimizes space use and lowers total cost of ownership in its cube storage systems.

The R5+ is an AutoStore Red Line robot that runs on top of the storage grid to dig, carry and deliver bins to workstations, announced in January 2022. Unlike the standard R5 it handles all three AutoStore bin sizes including the tallest 425 mm bin, in grids up to 14 levels high.

The B1 is the robot of AutoStore's Black Line, a module line for high-throughput cube storage systems introduced in January 2019. It is a slimmer, lighter grid robot with a cavity design, a direct-drive motor and exchangeable BattPack lithium-ion batteries, and can work alongside Red Line modules.

Hercules is the Amazon Robotics drive unit that slides under four-sided inventory pods and carries them to employees at ergonomic pick stations in Amazon fulfillment centers. It lifts up to 1,250 lb (567 kg), reads floor-grid markers and uses a forward-facing 3D camera to tell people, pods and robots apart, and takes direction from central planning software; the first Hercules model was deployed in 2017 and it is Amazon's most broadly deployed robot. It is used in-house and not sold.

Robin was the first robotic arm deployed by Amazon Robotics; it picks packages from conveyors and places them onto mobile drive units for outbound sortation and diverts damaged packages. It uses visual-perception algorithms to segment, identify and locate packages, rolled out in 2020, and Amazon reports more than 1,000 Robin arms sorting over 2 billion packages.

The MK30 is Amazon Prime Air's delivery drone, launched in November 2024 in the West Valley Phoenix area and College Station, Texas, for items weighing 5 lb (2.3 kg) or less delivered in 60 minutes or less. Amazon says it flies twice as far as its previous drones at roughly half the perceived noise, can operate in light rain, and uses a camera-based perception system with redundant flight-critical systems to detect and avoid obstacles and aircraft.

OTTAVA is a soft-tissue robotic surgical system from Johnson & Johnson MedTech whose four robotic arms are integrated into the operating-room table, which the company says takes 30-50% less space than boom- and cart-mounted systems and supports synchronized table-and-arm motion. It received FDA De Novo marketing authorization on July 22, 2026 for upper-abdominal and general procedures including gastric bypass, gastrectomy, cholecystectomy and hiatal hernia repair.

VELYS Spine is an active robotic-assisted and navigation system from DePuy Synthes, the orthopaedics business of Johnson & Johnson MedTech, developed with eCential Robotics for planning and instrumenting spinal fusion procedures in the cervical, thoracolumbar and sacroiliac spine. It received FDA 510(k) clearance and launched in the United States in August 2024.

The VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution is a table-mounted robotic system from DePuy Synthes (Johnson & Johnson MedTech) for total knee replacement with the ATTUNE Total Knee System. It received FDA 510(k) clearance in January 2021 and was launched later that year.

TMINI is a miniature, handheld, wireless robotic system from THINK Surgical (Fremont, California) for total knee replacement that uses CT-based 3D planning and overhead active tracking, and is an open-implant platform cleared for use with implants from several manufacturers. It received FDA 510(k) clearance on May 30, 2023, with first clinical cases performed in September 2023.

HYDROS is PROCEPT BioRobotics' next-generation robotic platform for Aquablation therapy, a heat-free robotic waterjet resection of prostate tissue to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia. It adds FirstAssist AI ultrasound-based treatment planning, integrated digital cystoscopy and dual HD touchscreens to robotic waterjet resection, and received FDA clearance in August 2024.

The AquaBeam Robotic System from PROCEPT BioRobotics is an image-guided surgical robot that combines real-time ultrasound and cystoscopy, surgeon-defined treatment planning and robotic heat-free waterjet resection (Aquablation therapy) to remove prostate tissue in benign prostatic hyperplasia. It received FDA De Novo authorization in December 2017 and was succeeded by the HYDROS system in 2024.

ExcelsiusGPS is a robotic navigation platform from Globus Medical that combines a rigid robotic arm with full navigation for spine and cranial procedures such as pedicle-screw trajectory guidance. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K171651) in August 2017.

ExcelsiusFlex is a robotic navigation system from Globus Medical for total knee arthroplasty that supports both imageless and CT-based registration. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K240721) in June 2024.

Senhance was a laparoscopic robotic surgery system with separate arm carts and an open surgeon console, developed by TransEnterix (renamed Asensus Surgical in 2021, acquired by KARL STORZ in 2024). It received its first FDA 510(k) clearance in October 2017, but KARL STORZ announced in June 2026 that it is discontinuing the Senhance line as part of fully integrating Asensus.

Mazor X Stealth Edition is Medtronic's robotic guidance system for spine surgery, combining the Mazor X robotic arm (originally from Mazor Robotics) with Medtronic StealthStation navigation for planning and guiding implant trajectories. The Mazor X received FDA clearance in 2017 and the Stealth Edition (K182077) was cleared in November 2018.

Yomi is a robotic guidance system from Neocis (Miami, Florida) for dental implant surgery that physically guides the surgeon's drill to a pre-planned implant position and angle. It was first cleared by the FDA in December 2016 (K161399) as the Neocis Guidance System and was later marketed as the Yomi Robotic System.
Yomi S is a newer version of Neocis' robotic system for dental implant surgery, listed alongside the original Yomi on the company's site. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K252376) in October 2025.

CorPath GRX was a robotic system from Corindus (Waltham, Massachusetts; acquired by Siemens Healthineers in 2019) that let interventional cardiologists advance and manipulate guidewires, balloons and stents from a shielded radiation-protected cockpit during percutaneous coronary and vascular interventions. It received FDA 510(k) clearance in October 2016, but Siemens Healthineers discontinued its cardiovascular surgical robotics program in 2023.

The CorPath 200 was Corindus' first robotic-assisted system for percutaneous coronary intervention, letting the physician control guidewire and balloon/stent catheters from a radiation-shielded interventional cockpit. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K120834) in July 2012 and was succeeded by the CorPath GRX in 2016.

The Galaxy System is a robotic bronchoscopy platform from Noah Medical (San Carlos, California) for peripheral lung-lesion biopsy, combining a single-use robotic bronchoscope with onboard tomosynthesis imaging, augmented fluoroscopy and tool-in-lesion confirmation. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K223144) in March 2023.

Genesis RMN is a robotic magnetic navigation system from Stereotaxis (St. Louis, Missouri) whose permanent magnets are mounted on flexible robotic arms to steer magnetic catheters remotely during cardiac electrophysiology ablation procedures. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K193147) in March 2020.

GenesisX is a semi-mobile robotic magnetic navigation system from Stereotaxis that combines the Genesis platform's responsiveness with a smaller form factor that can be installed in a cath lab over a weekend and shields its magnetic fields in its base when parked. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K251792) in November 2025.

The ARTAS System was an image-guided robotic system from Restoration Robotics (Sunnyvale, California) that harvested individual hair follicular units for hair restoration procedures. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K103428) in April 2011. Restoration Robotics merged into Venus Concept in 2019, and the product line continues today as ARTAS iX.

CyberKnife is Accuray's robotic radiosurgery system, a compact linear accelerator mounted on a robotic arm with integrated image guidance that tracks moving tumors and aims the beam for stereotactic radiosurgery and SBRT anywhere in the body. The first CyberKnife system received FDA 510(k) clearance (K984563) in July 1999; current models are the CyberKnife S7 and M6.

The mBôs TKA System is a robotic system for total knee arthroplasty from Monogram Technologies (Austin, Texas), now a Zimmer Biomet company, designed to make precise bone cuts for personalized knee implants. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K242121) in March 2025.

MARS (Magnetic-Assisted Robotic Surgery) is a robotic arm system from Levita Magnetics that works with the company's Magnetic Surgical System to move an internal magnetic grasper from outside the body, acting as a surgeon-controlled third arm that maintains exposure of anatomy in laparoscopic surgery without an extra incision. Its surgeon-controlled arm received FDA 510(k) clearance (K223673) in August 2023.

LIBERTY is a single-use, remotely operated endovascular robotic system from Microbot Medical for peripheral vascular interventions, consisting of a compact robotic drive, remote control and mounting arm that let physicians navigate guidewires and catheters from across the room. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K243789) in September 2025.

TSolution One is an active orthopedic surgical robot from THINK Surgical (Fremont, California) that autonomously mills bone to a CT-based preoperative plan for total hip arthroplasty. It received FDA 510(k) clearance (K150741) for hip procedures in October 2015 and preceded the company's handheld TMINI system.

Scoop is a robotic trailer and container unloader from Berkshire Grey that combines selective picking and pulling with conveyor-enabled floor induction to bulk-unload structured, unstructured and floor-loaded parcels, with a manual mode for non-conveyable exceptions. It was launched on February 3, 2026, when FedEx announced deployment of the system during 2026 after a multi-year collaboration.

FoxBot Mk3 is the third-generation FoxBot ATL autonomous forklift from Fox Robotics (Austin, Texas), a standard three-wheel counterbalance electric forklift fitted with cameras, LiDAR and AI perception to load and unload pallets from trailers at warehouse docks. Released in March 2025, it added autonomous trailer loading, auto-adjusting fork tines, an expanded sensor suite and more software integrations, and handles single or double-stacked pallets.

Brightpick Autopicker is an autonomous mobile picking robot that picks items from storage totes in standard shelving aisles and consolidates orders on board, aimed at e-commerce and grocery fulfillment. Brightpick, headquartered near Cincinnati, Ohio, announced it on February 14, 2023 as a commercially available autonomous mobile picking robot.

Autopicker 2.0 is the second-generation multi-purpose warehouse robot from Brightpick, unveiled on June 24, 2025 with redesigned hardware and Intuition software adding physical AI and picking-in-motion. Brightpick states it averages 70-80 picks per hour, with about 40% faster picking and 20% faster travel than the first model, and it is offered as robots-as-a-service starting at 1,900 USD per robot per month.

Brightpick Giraffe is an autonomous mobile robot for Brightpick's warehouse picking system, unveiled in February 2025, that can reach storage up to 20 ft (6 m) high. Brightpick says it lets users achieve up to three times the storage density of manual operations.

SharpShooter is a robotic precision application system from Verdant Robotics (Hayward, California) whose Aim & Apply technology uses vision and AI to detect and track individual crops and weeds and fire targeted micro-shots from aimable turrets for weeding, thinning and input application. Verdant states coverage of up to 7 acres per hour and weeds from 2 mm to 24 in; the 2025 SharpShooter was unveiled for commercial launch at FIRA in October 2024.

Automatic milking robot from Dutch dairy-robotics maker Lely that succeeds the Astronaut A5, with a new operating system supporting remote assistance and over-the-air updates, a hybrid robot arm with laser and camera teat detection and an optional automatic milk filter. It was launched in 2025, with availability in the US and Canada following local validation in 2026.

Autonomous manure-collecting robot from Lely for solid and semi-closed barn floors that vacuums up manure instead of scraping it, sprays water to aid collection and follows preset routes and schedules set from a phone. Introduced in 2016, it reached 10,000 units sold worldwide in 2026.

Autonomous electric vehicle from Lely that mows grass, fertilises the field from a 200-litre liquid tank in the same pass, transports the fresh grass to the barn and distributes it along the feed fence. It navigates with GPS, stereo cameras and ultrasonic sensors at up to 4.5 km/h; introduced as a concept in 2020, it was in use on 25 farms by early 2026.

Free-navigating feed-pushing robot from Lely for large farms that plans its own routes between several barns using a pre-scanned map, a stereo camera and a laser scanner, and handles slopes up to 20%. Unveiled in 2024 with a 54 V battery and a top speed of 72 m/min, six times that of the Juno J2, it is listed among Lely's latest innovations.

Automatic livestock feeding system from Lely made up of a feed kitchen with an overhead feed grabber and a battery-powered mixing and feeding robot that mixes, transports, distributes and pushes rations for different animal groups. A feed-height sensor lets the robot decide when feed is needed; the system was introduced in 2012.

Fully autonomous mechanical weeding robot from Rotterdam-based Odd.Bot for organic arable crops such as onions, carrots, chicory and red beet, which uses cameras and AI to tell crops from weeds and pulls weeds with its Weader arms at 2 mm precision. It runs around the clock on swappable batteries, has an adjustable track width of 1.50 to 2.25 m, and the 2025 model is the first full-scale production version.

Fully electric autonomous tracked tool carrier from Naïo Technologies for vineyards, orchards and other perennial crops, offered in Compact (1.3 m) and Large (1.8 m) versions with a 3-point hitch, PTO, auxiliary hydraulics and an on-board power supply for existing implements. It uses a patented dynamic mass-balancing system, human- and obstacle-detection sensors and geofencing; unveiled in November 2026 and winner of an EIMA 2026 award, it is available for pre-order with delivery in 2027.

Electric autonomous straddle robot from Naïo Technologies for vineyard weeding and maintenance that carries interchangeable implements over the vine row, guided by RTK GNSS and able to run unsupervised with Naïo's Augmented Autonomy. Naïo states coverage of up to 6.5 ha per day and a 600 kg lifting capacity; the current version was launched in 2020 with a centre tool holder and more engine power.

Autonomous electric straddle tool carrier from Naïo Technologies for sowing and weeding vegetable crops, nurseries and young trees, with RTK guidance, a camera-guided side-shift system and track widths of 150-175 cm or 180-215 cm. Introduced at World FIRA 2021 as Naïo's fourth robot, it is no longer manufactured or sold by Naïo SAS as of June 2026.

Autonomous service robot designed in Paris and made in France by Aldebaran for restaurants, hotels and healthcare, carrying up to 30 kg on three weight-sensing shelves, with a 10.1-inch touchscreen face, LiDAR and depth sensors and navigation through aisles as narrow as 65 cm. It was unveiled in November 2022; after Aldebaran's 2025 liquidation, the Plato product line was taken over by French software group Lundi Matin.

The AGILOX ONE is an omnidirectional floor-to-floor autonomous mobile robot (AMR) pallet truck from Austrian maker AGILOX with four drive units and swarm-based fleet control. In standard configuration it lifts 1,000 kg to 500 mm with a single scissor lift, or 750 kg to 1,000 mm with a double scissor lift, and travels at up to 1.4 m/s. AGILOX brought its first AMR to market in 2017.
maxLiftHeight: 500 mm (single scissor lift); 1000 mm with 750 kg (double scissor lift)

description: The AGILOX OCF is an omnidirectional autonomous counterbalanced forklift AMR from Austrian maker AGILOX with three drive units. It is offered with 750 kg or 1,500 kg payload and lifts up to 1,600 mm (1,200 mm low-height version), reaching 1.4 m/s; AGILOX added it to its range at the start of 2021.

The AGILOX ODM (Omnidirectional Dolly Mover) is AGILOX's smallest autonomous mobile robot, built to move dollies and small load carriers with a 205 mm wide fork. It lifts 300 kg up to 250 mm, travels at 1.4 m/s and comes as ODM 600 and ODM 800 variants for different dolly sizes; it was introduced in October 2022 and won the 2023 IFOY Award.
maxLiftHeight: 250 mm

description: The AGILOX OFL (Omnidirectional Free Lifter) is a scissor-free, AI-supported omnidirectional stacker AMR from AGILOX that carries pallets and custom load carriers up to 800 kg to stations up to 1.2 m high. It uses 3D-sensor obstacle avoidance and laser distance sensors to detect free storage slots; AGILOX launched it in March 2025.

The Elios 3 is a caged, collision-tolerant indoor inspection drone from Swiss company Flyability, carrying an Ouster OS0-32 LiDAR and the FlyAware SLAM engine for 3D mapping of confined spaces such as tanks, mines and boilers. Optional payloads include ultrasonic thickness, radiation and surveying modules, and a high-capacity battery extends flight to 17 minutes; it was unveiled in May 2022.

WingtraRAY is a VTOL fixed-wing survey and mapping drone from Zurich-based Wingtra that takes off and lands vertically and swaps between RGB (61 MP), LiDAR and multispectral sensors. Wingtra lists up to 59 minutes of flight time, up to 550 ha covered per flight, 3 cm absolute accuracy with PPK and cruise speeds up to 22 m/s; it was announced in July 2025 as the successor to the WingtraOne GEN II.

The Voliro T is a contact-inspection flying robot from Zurich-based Voliro, an ETH Zurich spin-off, whose tilting-rotor design lets it press sensors against structures with up to 30 N of stable force for non-destructive testing at height. Interchangeable payloads include ultrasonic thickness (UT), EMAT, pulsed eddy current, lightning-protection testing and gas sensors; it launched with early adopters in 2022 and reached general availability in 2023.

The Wingcopter 198 is an all-electric tilt-rotor eVTOL fixed-wing drone from German maker Wingcopter, used for beyond-visual-line-of-sight medical and parcel delivery and for LiDAR surveying. The maker lists a 25 kg maximum take-off weight, 4.7 kg payload, 94 km maximum range and 90 km/h speed; a triple-drop delivery upgrade is in development. It was introduced in 2021.

The Wingcopter 262 is a modular all-electric VTOL reconnaissance drone from German maker Wingcopter, named after its 262 cm wingspan and aimed at defence and security users. It carries AI-enabled EO/IR camera systems, has a 10 kg maximum take-off weight, a 150 km tactical range and up to six hours of flight time; it was introduced in September 2026.

Jaibot is a semi-autonomous, BIM-driven ceiling-drilling robot from Hilti for mechanical, electrical, plumbing and interior-finishing installation work. It locates itself with a total station, drills holes overhead from building-model data, runs cordless for up to 8 hours between charges and has built-in dust removal; Hilti unveiled it in October 2020.

LIFTBOT is a battery-powered, remote-controlled robotic hoist from Munich-based KEWAZO that carries scaffolding parts, insulation, tools and other materials up a rail mounted on scaffolds, with KEWAZO Onsite analytics tracking loads and lift cycles. The maker lists a 42 m/min operating speed, about 6,000 kg moved per 8-hour shift by a three-person crew and operation in winds up to 72 km/h; the series system followed prototypes first shown in 2018 and was reported complete in 2021.

Dexter is a compact, mobile robotic surgery system from Swiss company Distalmotion for minimally invasive procedures in urology, gynaecology and general surgery. Its open architecture works with the hospital's own laparoscopic visualisation and instruments, the surgeon console stays in the sterile field so surgeons can switch between laparoscopic and robotic technique without redocking, and docking takes about 4 minutes. Dexter received the European CE Mark in December 2020 and later US FDA clearances.

Cirq is a lightweight, modular table-mounted robotic surgical platform from Munich-based Brainlab that assists surgeons during spine and cranial procedures. Its Cirq Robotic Alignment Module automatically aligns instruments to pre- or intraoperatively planned trajectories for pedicle-screw placement while keeping haptic feedback, and integrates with Brainlab navigation and imaging. The robotic alignment module received CE mark in summer 2020 and FDA clearance in February 2021.

Loop-X is a mobile robotic intraoperative imaging system (cone-beam CT and 2D X-ray) from Brainlab, developed with Salzburg-based partner medPhoton, whose independently moving source and 43 x 43 cm detector panels allow non-isocentric scans for spine, cranial, orthopedic, ENT and CMF surgery. It has a 1.5 m2 footprint, is controlled wirelessly from a tablet and works with Brainlab navigation; it was unveiled at NASS in September 2019 and received FDA clearance in February 2021.

The Lokomat is a treadmill-based robotic gait-training device from Swiss rehabilitation company Hocoma (part of DIH) that combines an individually adjustable leg exoskeleton with dynamic body-weight support for highly repetitive physiological walking therapy of severely impaired patients. It was developed with Balgrist University Hospital in Zurich and first sold in 2001; Hocoma celebrated its 1,000th installed Lokomat in 2020.

ArmeoPower is a robotic upper-limb exoskeleton from Hocoma for arm and hand rehabilitation of severely impaired patients, providing arm-weight support and adjustable assist-as-needed robotic support in a three-dimensional workspace with game-like exercises; the optional Manovo Power module trains hand opening and closing. Hocoma introduced it in 2011 as the first commercially available robotic arm exoskeleton with a 3D workspace.

The Andago is a mobile gait-training robot from Hocoma that follows the patient during free overground walking while providing dynamic body-weight support, bridging treadmill-based Lokomat training and unassisted walking. Hocoma introduced it to the market in 2016 as the first mobile gait robot with a body-weight support system; the current version is Andago V2.0.

The iw.hub is an autonomous mobile robot from Munich-based idealworks, a BMW Group spin-off now majority-owned by Agile Robots, that slides under and carries roller dollies and pallets of up to 1,000 kg at up to 2.2 m/s. It is built to automotive standards for three-shift operation, has a turntable for re-orienting loads while driving and works with more than 20 load-carrier types; it has been in production use at BMW Group plants since 2020.

The Pick-it-Easy Robot is an AI-supported, camera-guided piece-picking robot workstation from Austrian intralogistics company KNAPP that identifies, grips and places mixed items such as cartons, cans, bottles and polybags of up to 3.5 kg from storage containers around the clock. KNAPP presented it at LogiMAT 2017, where it was named best product.

The Open Shuttle is a free-navigating autonomous mobile robot from KNAPP for transporting containers, cartons and trays between storage, picking and production areas; the Open Shuttle 50/100 variants carry up to 120 kg and run 7 hours per charge with a 60-minute charging time. KNAPP Open Shuttles were already in operation at the Grene warehouse in Denmark by 2015.

The Open Shuttle Fork is KNAPP's autonomous forklift-type mobile robot for transporting pallets, stillages, racks and special load carriers, with a payload of up to 1,500 kg, 8 hours of runtime and a 60-minute charging time. Würth Industrie Service presented it in operation in May 2017.

ADA is an autonomous delivery robot developed by Brazilian startup Synkar in partnership with food-delivery platform iFood. It debuted in 2021 at the Iguatemi shopping mall in Ribeirão Preto, carrying orders from restaurants to courier hubs, and was later extended to call elevators on its own to deliver inside residential and office buildings.

Four-rotor agricultural drone from XAG for autonomous spraying, spreading, field mapping and sling-load transport. It carries up to 80 kg, has an 80 L liquid tank and a 115 L granule container, and flies at up to 20 m/s. Unveiled internationally at Agritechnica in November 2025.

Quad-rotor agricultural drone from XAG for spraying, spreading, transport and aerial mapping, launched at XAG's annual conference in December 2023. It has a 70 kg maximum payload, 30 L/min maximum spray flow, a 115 L granule container and a 280 kg/min maximum spread rate.

Compact agricultural drone from XAG for spraying, spreading and field mapping, launched alongside the P150 in December 2023. It carries up to 30 kg, flies at up to 13.8 m/s and has IPX6K protection so the whole airframe can be washed down.

Flagship 2026-model-year agricultural drone from XAG with a 149.9 kg maximum takeoff weight and 85 kg rated payload for spraying, spreading, sling-load transport and mapping. It uses XAG's sixth-generation RevoSpray system with up to 42 L/min flow and a 150 L granule box; unveiled at XAG's annual conference on 5 November 2025.

Tote-to-person rack-climbing robot system from Geek+ that delivers up to 6,000 totes per hour per 1,000 m², climbs at up to 1.5 m/s and allows two robots to work in the same rack column. Its Max Workstation exceeds 800 totes per hour; launched in August 2026 alongside the existing RoboShuttle Air and Flex.
throughput: 6000 totes/h per 1,000 m²

description: Four-arm laparoscopic surgical robot from MicroPort MedBot for urology, general surgery, gynecology and thoracic procedures, with 3D HD visualization and integrated telesurgery over 5G, broadband, fiber or satellite links. Approved by China's NMPA on 27 January 2022 as the first Chinese-developed four-arm laparoscopic robot; it later gained NMPA approval for commercial telesurgery (May 2025) and CE marking.

UniPath (Dudao) electronic bronchoscopy navigation robot from MicroPort MedBot for reaching small peripheral lung lesions, using an ultra-thin flexible catheter of about 4.0 mm outer diameter, image-based airway path planning and real-time respiratory-motion compensation. Approved by China's NMPA on 23 December 2025.

Single-port endoscopic surgical robot from Surgerii Robotics (Shurui) that uses patented continuum-bending nickel-titanium instruments with up to 210° cumulative bending for urologic, gynecologic, general and thoracic laparoscopic procedures. Approved by China's NMPA on 20 June 2023 as the country's first single-port laparoscopic robot, and CE marked in Europe.

Orthopedic surgical robot from Beijing Tinavi Medical Technologies whose robotic arm positions instruments and implants along planned screw trajectories in spine and trauma surgery, supporting both 2D and 3D imaging modes. The third-generation TiRobot received China CFDA registration in 2016.

Second-generation orthopedic surgical robot from Tinavi with a multi-functional robotic arm, integrated terminal arm control, real-time surgical planning, an omni-directional tracer and dual foot pedals for switching between manual and automatic modes, covering spine, trauma and TKA procedures. Launched in 2021.

Multi-port endoscopic surgical robot from Edge Medical with a suspended four-arm design, immersive low-latency 3D imaging and wristed instruments for urology, gynecology, general and thoracic surgery. NMPA-approved in December 2022 and CE certified in January 2025; it shares a surgeon console with the company's single-port robot and supports telesurgery.

Single-arm, single-port laparoscopic surgical robot from Edge Medical that completes procedures through one incision, using its AgileArm and DriveBoxFlip technologies for four-quadrant reach. NMPA-approved in November 2023, with later approvals covering gynecology, urology, general and thoracic surgery.

Robotic bronchoscopy system from Edge Medical with a dual-arm design, remote handle control, multimodal navigation and a dual-layer catheter for biopsy and treatment of peripheral lung nodules. Approved by China's NMPA in January 2025.
New-generation multi-port endoscopic surgical robot from Edge Medical, unveiled in August 2024 as the successor platform to its MP1000 series.

Multi-arm laparoscopic/endoscopic surgical robot developed by Wuhan United Imaging Zhirong Medical Technology, a surgical-innovation subsidiary of United Imaging Healthcare. Clinically validated in hepatobiliary, urologic, gastrointestinal, gynecologic and thoracic procedures at top Chinese hospitals, and approved by China's NMPA on 30 July 2026 as the group's first laparoscopic/endoscopic surgical robot.

Modular robotic surgery platform from Shanghai-based Ronovo Surgical that provides configurable robotic assistance for laparoscopic procedures in general surgery, gynecology, urology and thoracic surgery. Unveiled in February 2023 and approved by China's NMPA in March 2025; commercialized in China in collaboration with Johnson & Johnson MedTech.

Endoscopic surgical robot from Hong Kong-based Cornerstone Robotics with lightweight surgeon-side arms, tremor filtration and motion-control techniques for complex surgery in confined spaces. Approved by China's NMPA in September 2024 after clinical trials in urology, general surgery, gynecology and thoracic surgery.

Four-arm laparoscopic surgical robot from Weigao (Shandong Weigao Surgical Robot), developed with Tianjin University and consisting of an imaging system, surgeon console and bedside robotic-arm cart; its instrument tips rotate 540° and it was used for a 5G remote surgery over more than 3,000 km in 2020. Approved by China's NMPA in October 2021 as the first domestically approved laparoscopic surgical robot.

Omnidirectional autonomous pallet truck from Multiway Robotics with a 1,000 kg rated load, 1.7 m/s top speed and 360° movement that allows right-angle stacking in 1,900 mm aisles. It uses 3D SLAM navigation without reflectors or QR codes and can ride elevators between floors; launched in June 2026 and winner of a 2026 French Design Award.

Autonomous forklift from VisionNav Robotics for automated trailer and truck loading and unloading, using deep-learning-based 3D local SLAM and coordinated by a robot control fleet scheduling system. Introduced at MODEX in March 2024.

Latent (under-ride) transport AMR in Hikrobot's Mingzhi single-unit intelligence series, carrying 300 kg for line-side material delivery without a central server; deployment can take as little as 30 minutes. It passes aisles as narrow as 60 cm and was launched on 23 October 2026.

Fork-type transport AMR in Hikrobot's Mingzhi series with a 1,500 kg load capacity for pallet transport and stacking, supporting walk-through teaching of routes and server-free multi-robot coordination. Launched on 23 October 2026.

maxRuntime: 12 hours
description: Lightweight indoor delivery AMR from Standard Robots with a 150 kg rated load, about 12 hours of runtime unloaded (8 hours loaded) and automatic recharging. It maps about 1,000 m² in 10 minutes, passes 550 mm gaps and uses dual LiDAR plus cameras; launched on 10 October 2026.

Fork-type autonomous mobile robot from Jiexiang Lingyue whose maximum lift height was raised from 6.5 m to 8 m while keeping a 1.2 t load capacity over the full stroke, for higher pallet storage locations. Launched on 15 October 2026.
maxLiftHeight: 8 m

description: Compact line-side transport AMR nicknamed 'Little Turtle' from Dolphin Star, with a 920 x 400 mm body and 690 mm minimum turning radius for narrow-aisle material handling. Shown publicly for the first time in October 2026.

Point-to-point transport robot ('Jixing' V400) from Weimaier that staff configure through a visual app for points, routes and tasks, using 3D SLAM localization rather than fixed tracks; basic mapping and deployment take as little as 30 minutes. Launched on 6 August 2026.

Embodied person-following transport robot from Chengdu Ruixinxing Technology with a 300 kg maximum load and five carrying modes: automatic delivery, lifting delivery, person following, power-assisted pushing and towing. It has a touchscreen and voice interaction and was launched in August 2026.

Latent lifting transport robot from Yangzi Manufacturing that weighs 78 kg, carries a 300 kg rated load with a 50 mm lift stroke and fits passages from 70 cm wide, for moving carts, totes and small pallets between production lines. Launched on 29 July 2026.

XFL201 is a 2.0-tonne counterbalance autonomous forklift from EP Equipment (Zhejiang Zhongli Machinery), using AI-based navigation for indoor and outdoor pallet loading, unloading and material handling. It was one of several autonomous material-handling robots unveiled at the company's '629' product event on 29-30 June 2026.

XCP101 is a compact 1.0-tonne under-fork AMR from EP Equipment (Zhejiang Zhongli Machinery) for autonomous pallet transport in narrow-aisle warehouses. It was one of several autonomous material-handling robots unveiled at the company's '629' product event on 29-30 June 2026.
1.5-tonne counterbalance forklift robot from EP Equipment (Zhongli), one of several autonomous material-handling robots launched at the company's '629' product event on 29-30 June 2026.
1.0-tonne single-side-fork narrow-aisle stacker robot from EP Equipment (Zhongli), one of several autonomous material-handling robots launched at the company's '629' product event on 29-30 June 2026.
1.0-tonne double-side-fork narrow-aisle stacker robot from EP Equipment (Zhongli), one of several autonomous material-handling robots launched at the company's '629' product event on 29-30 June 2026.

Embodied-AI truck loading and unloading robot from ENGOAL designed for mixed cartons of different sizes, using dual 3D vision systems and SLAM navigation to complete loading and unloading on its own. Launched in June 2026.

Compact embodied-AI loading and unloading robot from ENGOAL running the company's OmniPredict 2.0 loading world model, with an integrated design that handles both loading and unloading. Launched on 26 October 2026.

Battery-electric tracked Auto-Navigation Forklift Robot from LEAPTING that carries 3,000 kg pallets of solar modules from laydown yards to installation rows on utility-scale PV sites. It combines GPS-RTK, laser SLAM and 3D vision for pallet detection, runs about 8 hours on a 48 V 400 Ah battery and is IP67-rated; launched in October 2026.

Bipedal entertainment robot for culture, tourism and sports venues from Chengdu Xingjin Humanoid Robot Technology, a subsidiary of the Chengdu Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, launched in July 2025 and used as a robot cheer squad at the 2025 Chengdu World Games. It is about 1 m tall and 30 kg, has a 6-DOF head carrying a 19-inch expression screen, group choreography control, multilingual guiding and AI-vision patrol functions.

Lightweight lumbar material-handling exoskeleton from Yuanshan Zhixing (远山智行), a smart-wearables brand of the China Ordnance Hangzhou Zhiyuan Research Institute, shown at the 140th Canton Fair in October 2026. A waist-assist structure offloads lumbar strain for workers doing frequent bending and lifting in warehousing, manufacturing and parcel-sorting jobs.

Boom-arm photovoltaic panel cleaning robot from Hefei-based Renjie Intelligent Technology, unveiled in November 2025 with a first batch of ten units delivered to solar plants. It uses a flexible arm that adapts to frameless modules and different rack heights and tilts, low-speed autonomous driving with cloud control, wireless charging with automatic parking, and cleans 8-14 MW of panels per day.

Explosion-proof wheeled inspection robot from Chongqing-based Qiteng Robot, launched in September 2026 for oil, gas and chemical plants. It has a modular architecture with an independently sealed compartment and quick-maintenance interfaces, and accepts interchangeable detection modules for different inspection tasks.

Embodied-AI sewing robot (艾妮) from Aitu Technology (艾图科技), a brand of sewing-equipment maker Jack Technology, launched on 28 October 2026 at a China launch price of 308,000 CNY. It identifies, picks, smooths and aligns fabric for garment workstations using a 5-billion-parameter sewing model and sensorized grippers with 0.1 mm control precision, and is used for shirt collars, cuffs, pockets, buttonholes and button attaching.

The M5F is a single-layer bin-moving mobile robot from Quicktron Robotics used in its QuickBin goods-to-person system. It has a 30 kg rated load, a 890 mm lifting height, QR-code plus inertial navigation with ±10 mm positioning accuracy and a top unloaded speed of 4.5 m/s; it was launched at CeMAT Asia 2024.
maxLiftHeight: 890 mm

description: The VNE40-66 is an autonomous counterbalance forklift (AGV/AMR) from VisionNav Robotics for stacking large, heavy containers such as automotive cages. It uses 3D SLAM navigation and 3D LiDAR perception, is rated at 6,180 lb on the product page and travels at up to 4.5 m/s forward; it was introduced at MODEX 2026.

The VNST 20 is a slim autonomous pallet mover (AGV/AMR) from VisionNav Robotics for ground-to-ground pallet transport. It carries up to 2,000 kg, drives at up to 1.8 m/s and uses a 3D laser sensor for positioning, perception and protection; VisionNav launched it in May 2023.

The Agras T25P is a compact DJI Agriculture spraying and spreading drone for small and hillside plots, with a 20 L spray tank. It weighs 33 kg with battery and has a 1,970 mm diagonal wheelbase; DJI launched it globally in July 2025 after debuting it in China the previous year.

The Agras T50 is a DJI Agriculture crop-protection drone with a 40 L spray tank, a coaxial eight-rotor layout and a 2,200 mm diagonal wheelbase. It weighs 52 kg with battery; it was released in China in 2023 and launched internationally in April 2024.

The Agras T25 is a portable DJI Agriculture spraying and spreading drone with a 20 L spray tank and a 1,925 mm diagonal wheelbase. It weighs 32 kg with battery; it was released in China in 2023 and launched internationally in April 2024.

TiRobot II (TianJi II) is an orthopedic surgical robot system from Beijing Tinavi Medical Technologies that uses a multi-functional robotic arm to guide instruments and implants in spine, trauma and total knee arthroplasty procedures. Tinavi lists 2021 as the year TiRobot II reached the market.

TiRobot (TianJi) is Tinavi's orthopedic robotic navigation and positioning system whose robotic arm provides planned screw trajectories for spine and trauma surgery in 2D and 3D imaging modes. Tinavi states that the third-generation TiRobot was approved by China's NMPA in 2016.

The Max 1500-L Slim is a low-profile lifting AMR from ForwardX Robotics for pallet and rack transport in warehouses and factories. It stands 245 mm tall, carries up to 1,500 kg, weighs 250 kg, uses laser SLAM and visual positioning with 360-degree obstacle detection and runs about 8 hours per charge; ForwardX introduced it in November 2023.
maxLiftHeight: 60 mm

description: The Apex 1400-L is an autonomous pallet-stacker forklift from ForwardX Robotics that combines laser SLAM, visual positioning, LiDAR and a 3D camera to pick and place floor pallets. It carries up to 1,400 kg, weighs 880 kg, lifts to 1,600 mm as standard and runs about 10 hours per charge; ForwardX featured it in early 2023 and launched it in the US in 2024.
maxLiftHeight: 1600 mm (3500 mm customizable)

description: The Apex C1500-L is an autonomous counterbalanced forklift from ForwardX Robotics with a 1,500 kg load capacity that fuses computer vision and laser SLAM for pallet docking and placement. ForwardX listed it alongside the Apex 1400-L in February 2023 and presented a next-generation version in February 2024.

The Flex 60-SW is a vision-based picking AMR from ForwardX Robotics with an integrated automatic weighing scale and interactive touchscreen to verify picked items. It was launched at Logistic-Tech Tokyo in September 2023.

The HaiPick A3 is a fork-lifting autonomous case-handling robot (ACR) from Hai Robotics for storing, picking and moving non-containerized goods such as tires, trays, foam boxes and PCBs. It uses SLAM navigation, reaches a picking height of up to 5.5 m and has a dust-proof, anti-static load handling device for Class 10000 cleanliness; it was unveiled at CeMAT Asia in October 2021.
