The HaiPick A42-FW is a flexible-width autonomous case-handling robot from Hai Robotics whose fork adjusts to the size of totes or cartons being picked. It has a 900 mm wide chassis and a lowest pick height of 190 mm for denser storage; it was unveiled at CeMAT Asia in October 2021.

LINGTRA (Lingyun) is HANGCHA Group's line of AI-Fork robotic forklifts built on its electric industrial vehicle platform and its LogiMind industrial embodied-AI model, which lets the trucks interpret tasks and surroundings, plan movements and adapt to occupied locations or misaligned pallets. HANGCHA unveiled a five-model LINGTRA range, including a pallet stacker and a three-wheel counterbalance forklift, at its 4th Global Dealers Conference in Hangzhou in November 2026.

The Remebot (Reme) neurosurgical navigation and positioning robot from Beijing Baihui Weikang Technology combines multimodal image fusion planning software, an optical tracking locator and a robotic operating platform for procedures such as DBS electrode placement, SEEG, biopsy and hemorrhage aspiration. The company states it received China's first NMPA Class III registration for a neurosurgical robot in 2018.

The Remebot Dental Robot (Ruiyibo) is an oral implant surgery robot from Beijing Baihui Weikang Technology. The company states it was approved in 2021 as the first NMPA-certified surgical robot in China's oral field.
The RM-50 is a cerebral hemorrhage surgical robot from Beijing Baihui Weikang Technology (Remebot). The company states that it obtained NMPA certification in 2022.

The Sinobot X1, registered as the SR1 series in some markets, is a neurosurgical robot from Sinovation (Beijing) Medical Technology that pairs Holoshot 3D structured-light markerless patient registration with a fully automatic robotic arm for stereotactic procedures. Sinovation states that the SR1 neurosurgical robot was approved for market by China's NMPA in December 2018.

The Q300 series is a miniature neurosurgical robot from Sinovation (Beijing) Medical Technology that integrates intraoperative navigation with frameless robotic stereotaxis to guide drainage tubes, biopsy needles and intracranial electrodes to planned targets. Sinovation states it was approved for the Chinese market in January 2022 as China's first miniature neurosurgical robot.

The X1000 series is a neuro-spinal surgical robot from Sinovation (Beijing) Medical Technology that combines a neurosurgery robot module, a neuronavigation module and a spine surgery robot module in one system for procedures such as DBS and SEEG electrode implantation, biopsy and spinal surgery. Sinovation states it was approved for the Chinese market in September 2024.

The D200 (Lingyang) is an intelligent operation robot from Nanjing-based YIJIAHE Technology that the company lists under its smart-power product line and describes as an embodied-intelligence operation robot. YIJIAHE's company history dates its release to 2021.

The E100 is a new-generation outdoor intelligent inspection robot from YIJIAHE Technology for power facilities. The company history records its release in 2017; it is no longer listed in YIJIAHE's current product line.

The A100 was YIJIAHE Technology's first-generation indoor inspection robot, which the company history says debuted in 2015 together with its first tunnel robot, the T100. It is no longer listed in YIJIAHE's current product line.

The Tuoshou orthopedic surgical robot is made by Tuodao Medical, a surgical-robotics company founded in 2019 within the YIJIAHE Group. YIJIAHE's company history states that the Tuoshou orthopedic surgical robot was approved for market in China in 2022.

The EA-J150 is EAVISION's flagship multifunctional agricultural drone platform combining spraying, spreading and transport with omnidirectional perception. EAVISION's company timeline dates its market launch to 2024, and it was exhibited at AGRITECHNICA in Hannover in November 2025.
The EA-J70 is an agricultural spraying drone from EAVISION marketed for single-operator missions. EAVISION's company timeline dates its market launch, together with the EA-J150, to 2024.

The EA-J100 is an agricultural crop-protection drone from EAVISION (Jimu) that the company showed alongside the J150 and J70 at AGRITECHNICA 2025. EAVISION's company timeline dates its market launch to 2023.
The EA-30XP is an agricultural spraying drone from EAVISION, marketed as a more stable and more powerful successor to the EA-30X. EAVISION's company timeline dates its market launch to 2022.
The EA-30X is an omnidirectional intelligent agricultural drone from EAVISION for crop protection. EAVISION's company timeline dates its market launch to 2021.

The MGIUS-R3 Tele-robotic Ultrasound System is a remote ultrasound robot developed by Imabot, a subsidiary of MGI Tech, that lets a clinician control an ultrasound probe on a patient-side 6-DOF robotic arm from a distant console with live imaging. It supports abdominal, urological, gynecological, superficial-organ, vascular and pulmonary exams and was publicly demonstrated by BGI in April 2019.

The Matrice 350 RTK is a DJI enterprise drone platform for inspection, mapping and public-safety payloads that uses the DJI RC Plus controller. It weighs about 6.47 kg with two TB65 batteries, has a 9.2 kg maximum takeoff weight, up to 55 minutes of flight time and IP55 protection; DJI released it in May 2023.

The Matrice 5TD is a DJI dock-based enterprise drone with thermal imaging, long-range zoom, LiDAR, millimeter-wave radar and onboard AI, designed to operate from the DJI Dock 4, which swaps its battery automatically in about 25 seconds. DJI states up to 59 minutes of flight time and speeds up to 21 m/s; it was announced in October 2026.

The Matrice 4T is the thermal variant of DJI's Matrice 4 enterprise drone series for public safety and energy inspection, combining 24 mm wide, 70 mm medium-telephoto and 168 mm telephoto cameras with a thermal camera, NIR auxiliary light and laser range finder. The series weighs 1,229 g and flies up to 49 minutes at up to 21 m/s; DJI released it in January 2025.

The Matrice 4E is the surveying and inspection variant of DJI's Matrice 4 enterprise drone series, with a 24 mm wide camera using a Micro Four Thirds sensor and mechanical shutter for mapping, plus 70 mm and 168 mm telephoto cameras and a laser range finder. The series weighs 1,229 g and flies up to 49 minutes at up to 21 m/s; DJI released it in January 2025 as the successor to the Mavic 3 Enterprise.

The Matrice 30 is a compact folding DJI enterprise drone for emergency services and energy inspection that works with the DJI RC Plus controller, FlightHub 2 and DJI Dock. It weighs 3,770 g with two batteries, flies up to 41 minutes and is rated IP55; DJI announced it in March 2022.

The J160 is an agricultural drone from EAVISION (Jimu) in China, part of the company's intelligent crop-protection lineup built around visual perception and constant-droplet mist spraying. EAVISION's official company history lists the J160 among models that launched domestically in 2025; it has no dedicated page yet on EAVISION's international English site and was not among the models (J150/J100/J70) shown at AGRITECHNICA 2025.

The EA-J110 is an agricultural spraying drone from EAVISION (Jimu) for medium-sized farms, with a 50 L spray tank, a 1–500 μm adjustable droplet range, LiDAR-radar fusion sensing and a 30 Ah CTB battery. EAVISION's company timeline lists the J110 among the models launched in 2025.

BYD's flash-charging robotic arm automatically locates an EV's charging port, opens the cover, inserts the connector and removes it after charging, using visual recognition and force-feedback control. Demonstrated in the UAE in November 2026 at a solar-plus-storage station reaching 1,000 kW, it supports several overseas connector standards and works with BYD's one-tap automated parking-and-charging function.

The 7th-generation COFE+ is a fully automated robotic coffee kiosk from Shanghai Hi-Dolphin Robot Technology, debuted at the 2026 Hongqiao International Coffee Culture Festival. In a 2.3 m² footprint it offers 197 recipes across eight drink categories including fresh-ground coffee, milk tea and 3D-printed latte art, holds extraction at 9 bar and 92.5 °C, averages about 54 seconds per cup in the maker's barista showdown and is rated for 24/7 indoor or outdoor use from -20 to 40 °C.

Baoxiaomi Max is OrionStar's flagship AI-agent reception and guide robot, first shown at WAIC 2026 and in volume delivery from July 2026. It runs OrionStar's AgentOS with 30+ built-in agent skills, has motorized arms and head for gestures, a 14-inch screen, six-microphone array, 13 MP camera and lidar, a 5 kg chest bay for card readers or printers, and calls elevators for cross-floor guiding.

Baoxiaomi Pro is a modular AI-agent reception robot from OrionStar, launched on March 27, 2026 together with the Baoxiaomi Lite. It uses a Qualcomm QCS6490 platform running AgentOS, a 14-inch screen, six-microphone array, 13 MP and wide-angle cameras and gesturing arms, and accepts add-ons such as a 21.5-inch advertising screen, elevator module and ID-card reader.

Baoxiaomi Lite is OrionStar's lower-cost AI-agent reception and guide robot for small exhibition halls and company front desks, launched on March 27, 2026. It is 1.26 m tall with a 14-inch screen, six-microphone array, gesturing arms and AgentOS with built-in agent skills, and is designed to be configured and deployed without complex setup.

Coffee Master is a robotic-arm pour-over coffee station from OrionStar that reproduces hand-brewed coffee and was selected among QbitAI's 2021 top-10 AI products at MEET2022. It brews about 300 ml per serving in roughly three minutes, cleans its filter automatically and comes in standard, custom-bar and self-service versions, the latter adding iced drinks, automatic filter papers, NFC ordering and QR payment.

Tea Master is OrionStar's fully automatic robotic tea-brewing station for oolong, black and green tea. It brews about 300 ml into a glass sharing pot in roughly three minutes, cleans its filter cup and pot automatically, uses automatic filter papers and holds three sets of tea canisters.

Baoxiaodi Slim is a slim hotel delivery robot from OrionStar with two lockable 32 L compartments (expandable to four), each carrying 10 kg. It passes corridors from 55 cm wide, navigates with lidar, depth and fisheye cameras over maps up to 50,000 m², climbs 8-degree slopes and returns to its dock automatically.

Vercari is UBTECH's cabinet delivery robot for hospitals, nursing homes and blood-collection centers, introduced with its healthcare robot line in August 2022 as the Containerized Delivery Robot. A six-degree-of-freedom arm grasps items up to 2 kg and arranges them in self-opening drawers that unlock only by RF badge or password, and the robot navigates autonomously with cloud-based scheduling and tracking.

Aucari is UBTECH's open-shelf delivery robot for nursing homes, hospitals and hotels, debuted in August 2022 as the Open Shelf Delivery Robot. It has three sensor-monitored trays carrying 10 kg each, navigates with lidar, RGBD and ultrasonic sensors, works with door-access and elevator systems, and supports 'Dining Room' and 'Room Service' modes with cloud scheduling.

AeroBot is a storage-robot system from KNAPP in which robots climb along rack structures using friction-drive technology while a SatBot satellite robot riding on top stores and retrieves containers, trays and bulk goods of up to 35 kg, feeding goods-to-person workstations. KNAPP launched it at LogiMAT 2025, where it won the Best Product award.

Chico (Chico Mendes) is an amphibious environmental robot built by Brazilian oil company Petrobras to inspect oil and gas pipelines in the Amazon. It drives on sand, mud and flooded terrain and floats on water, carrying an explosimeter for methane and flammable gases, water-quality sensors, a depth gauge, GPS and an IMU; it was presented in 2008.

Versatrax 450 TTC is a remotely operated tracked crawler for hazardous environments, originally developed by Inuktun of British Columbia and now part of Eddyfi Technologies' VersaTrax line. It carries a pan-tilt-zoom camera and a 4-DOF manipulator arm with its own camera to locate, inspect and remove dangerous materials; the standard vehicle weighs 59 kg and reaches 0.55 km/h.

Kingfisher M200 is a small unmanned surface vessel (remote survey system) that Clearpath Robotics unveiled in November 2012 for environmental monitoring, bathymetric data collection, shore-erosion and sediment mapping, flow measurement and dam inspection. It uses semi-planing hulls and electric jet thrusters for fast-moving water and accepts add-ons such as acoustic Doppler profilers; Clearpath's later Heron USV replaced the Kingfisher pages.

Arkytas MU-2.1 is a remotely operated wheeled mining robot from Chilean startup Kinamics that carries a camera on a robotic arm to capture photogrammetry of freshly blasted, unsupported tunnel faces so surveyors and geologists do not have to approach them. Codelco reported in February 2026 that it had entered operation at the Esmeralda mine of its El Teniente division, turning about 20-22 photographs per face into 3D models.

BicudoBot is an autonomous field robot from Sao Paulo startup BSV Robotics, founded by University of Sao Paulo engineers, built to fight the cotton boll weevil (bicudo-do-algodoeiro). It uses cameras and computer-vision models to detect and map infestations, collects and destroys infested plant structures and applies insecticide only where the pest is present; the company said in December 2025 it was in field trials and would offer it as a robot-as-a-service from the next season.

Anovo (formerly Hominis) is a teleoperated surgical robot made by Momentis Surgical (formerly Memic Innovative Surgery) of Israel, using flexible instruments with internally articulated, humanoid-shaped joints. It won FDA De Novo authorization in 2021 for single-site transvaginal gynecologic procedures, then gained single-port general-surgery clearance in 2024 and, in July 2026, multiport clearance, making it the first robotic platform cleared for all three minimally invasive access routes (transvaginal, single-site, and multiport).

The XACT ACE Robotic System is an image-guided robotic device made by Israeli company XACT Robotics that autonomously inserts and steers needles for percutaneous biopsy, ablation, drainage and drug-delivery procedures in organs such as the lung, liver, kidney and prostate. Its proprietary S-Drive technology lets the needle switch from a linear to a non-linear trajectory in real time to compensate for tissue and target motion, with average tip-to-target accuracy under 1.7mm. The ACE Xtend remote control unit, allowing the physician to operate the system from outside the procedure room, received FDA clearance in October 2022.

Tevel Aerobotics Technologies, an Israeli agri-robotics company, makes the Flying Autonomous Robot (FAR), a tethered multirotor drone that uses computer vision and AI to identify ripe fruit, autonomously pick it from the tree and lower it into a collection bin. Multiple FAR units work together in an orchard under one control station, and the system is used commercially to harvest apples, peaches, apricots, nectarines, plums and pears in Israel, Italy, the US and Chile.

FFRobotics, an Israeli agricultural robotics company, builds the FFRobot, a multi-armed robotic harvesting platform that uses machine vision to locate and classify fruit and emulates the human-hand picking motion for bruise-free, cost-effective harvesting. The patented multi-fruit platform is designed to be reconfigured for different crops such as apples, and the company has run commercial field trials in the US and Europe with EU Horizon 2020 funding.

MetoMotion, an Israeli greenhouse-robotics company based in Yokne'am Illit, makes the GRoW (Greenhouse Robotic Worker), an autonomous dual-arm robot that uses AI and 3D vision to identify ripe produce, harvest it from both sides of a greenhouse row, and pack it directly into boxes with an onboard boxing system. It is commercially deployed for tomato harvesting in greenhouses in Europe and North America, with partners reporting roughly 80% lower labor hours and up to 15% higher yield.

Servis Robotu V3 is a wheeled hospitality/delivery service robot made by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS, used to carry food and drinks to guests in restaurants and hotels using autonomous navigation and collision sensors. It weighs 43kg, measures 60 x 50 x 146cm, has three 30cm-diameter carrying trays each rated for 5kg, a 10.1-inch screen, and supports autonomous charging.

Fabrika Servis Robotu (Factory Service Robot) is a wheeled indoor service robot made by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS for factory and office settings, derived from the company's Servis Robotu platform to carry trays and materials between workstations with autonomous navigation and charging.

The AMR Depo Taşıma Robotu (AMR Warehouse Transport Robot) V500 is an autonomous mobile robot by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS for moving loads inside warehouses and factories. It weighs 230kg, measures 33 x 82 x 110cm, runs for about 30 hours on a lithium-ion battery, reaches 0.7 m/s, and carries up to 500kg; it supports autonomous navigation and charging with collision protection.

The AMR Depo Taşıma Robotu (AMR Warehouse Transport Robot) V1000 is the higher-payload version of AKINROBOTICS' Turkish-built warehouse AMR, sharing the same 230kg chassis, 33 x 82 x 110cm footprint, roughly 30-hour battery life and 0.7 m/s top speed as the V500 model but rated to carry up to 1000kg.

The UV-C Sterilizasyon Robotu is an autonomous UV-C disinfection robot made by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS for hospitals, offices and other indoor spaces, navigating rooms on its own to sterilize surfaces and air with ultraviolet light. The system holds CE certification under the EU's AT Declaration of Conformity (2025).

AS-PNCR-2 is a wheeled agricultural field robot built by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS as part of its early AS-PNCR research project (2011-2012). It weighed 280kg, measured 175 x 100 x 87cm, ran on a 36V lead-acid battery for about 10 hours, and moved at 2.8 km/h; only a single unit was produced.

M1 Urban is a large wheeled unmanned ground vehicle made by Dubai-based Micropolis Robotics for urban security patrol, perimeter monitoring, incident verification and aerial surveillance support. It weighs 1800kg, runs on four in-wheel motors with double and crab steering, reaches a software-limited 120km/h, carries up to 500kg of payload, and uses eight vision sensors with 360-degree obstacle detection and NVIDIA-powered L4 autonomy; it carries an integrated drone compartment. Micropolis has supplied these vehicles to Dubai Police and UAE oil company ADNOC.

M2 Urban is a smaller wheeled security robot from Dubai-based Micropolis Robotics, built for patrol of gated communities, public spaces and controlled facilities. It weighs 453kg, reaches a software-limited 25km/h, carries up to 350kg payload, runs about 10 hours per charge, and uses six vision sensors with 360-degree obstacle detection and NVIDIA-powered L4 autonomy.

M1 Expedition is an off-road unmanned ground vehicle by Dubai-based Micropolis Robotics for extended security patrol, infrastructure inspection and equipment transport in remote terrain. It weighs 2000kg, has a hybrid drivetrain with two mid-drive motors and a range extender giving about 20 hours of runtime, a 450mm ground clearance, a 25-degree maximum slope rating, carries up to 750kg payload, and integrates a drone compartment with eight vision sensors for 360-degree obstacle detection.

M2 Expedition is the lighter off-road variant of Micropolis Robotics' security UGV line, built for patrol and payload-configurable security operations across rough or hard-to-access terrain. It weighs 450kg, reaches a software-limited 25km/h, carries up to 350kg payload, and runs about 10 hours per charge with six vision sensors for 360-degree obstacle detection.

LOGX Max is a heavy-duty autonomous logistics ground vehicle by Dubai-based Micropolis Robotics for inter-warehouse transport of cargo, equipment, parts and supplies. It weighs 2.4 tons, carries up to 5 tons of payload, reaches 80km/h, runs 10 hours per charge with 1.5-hour fast charging, and uses eight cameras with 360-degree obstacle detection and NVIDIA-powered L4 autonomy.

ECO Agri is an autonomous agricultural ground vehicle from Dubai-based Micropolis Robotics for farming and environmental operations such as crop monitoring, soil preparation, spraying and material transport. It weighs 1700kg, moves at a software-limited 10km/h, carries up to 500kg payload, runs about 10 hours per charge, and supports drone and robotic-arm attachment with NVIDIA-powered L4 autonomy and 360-degree obstacle detection.

Robee is a robotic pollination system made by Israeli agtech company BloomX for blueberry crops. It mimics the buzz pollination bumblebees perform by applying controlled vibrations to flowers so the anthers release pollen, and is offered commercially as a pollination-as-a-service in Israel, Peru, Mexico and South Africa.

Yahav 2400 is a robotic pollination system made by Israeli agtech company BloomX for avocado orchards. It generates a controlled electric field with high-voltage electrodes to attract and detach pollen grains, which collect on a bee-mimicking textile before being transferred to female flowers, using AI to guide one operator over up to 3.5 hectares a day. BloomX commercially launched the system in 2026.

The MATE-XT GO is a passive, unpowered upper-body exoskeleton from Italian robotics maker Comau that supports workers' arms and shoulders during overhead and repetitive tasks. It weighs under 3 kg, offers 8 adjustable assistance levels per arm, and is certified under EU Regulation 2016/425 for personal protective equipment.

The Atlas 2030 is a pediatric robotic gait exoskeleton made by Spanish company Marsi Bionics for children with cerebral palsy and other neuromuscular conditions. It is used in clinical settings to provide robot-assisted walking training and has been the subject of published observational studies on gait improvement.

Rubion is an autonomous strawberry-harvesting robot built by Belgian company Octinion. It uses machine vision to identify ripe strawberries, picks them without bruising using a soft gripper, and sorts them into punnets by target weight for the fresh market.

Colossus is a tracked, remote-controlled firefighting robot made by French company Shark Robotics, carrying firefighting monitors, cameras and up to 500 kg of payload across more than 10 mission modules. It became internationally known after helping Paris firefighters battle the 2019 Notre-Dame Cathedral fire and has since been supplied to brigades worldwide, including to Ukraine.

HANK is a lower-limb robotic exoskeleton made by Spanish company Gogoa Mobility Robots for clinical gait rehabilitation, described as the first European exoskeleton to receive CE marking as a medical device. It has 6 motorized joints at the hip, knee and ankle, and is used in hospitals to treat stroke, spinal cord injury, Parkinson's disease and other neurological conditions.

Vitirover is a small, solar-powered, GPS-guided autonomous robot made by the French company of the same name for herbicide-free vegetation maintenance in vineyards and other agricultural land. It weighs 23 kg, moves at roughly 500 m/hour, and uses a four-wheel-drive chassis with a pendular rear axle to navigate under vine rows among thousands of posts and stakes per hectare without damaging crops.

BOBY is a goods-to-person mobile robot made by French company Scallog that lifts and transports mobile storage shelves to order-picking stations in warehouses, guided by an optical sensor following a repositionable floor strip. It carries up to 600 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s unloaded, runs up to 14 hours per charge, and is deployed at numerous European logistics sites.

K-STER C is an expendable, remotely operated underwater drone made by French defense-technology company Exail (formerly ECA Group/iXblue) for naval mine disposal. It carries dual-frequency sonar and a color camera for target identification and a patented tiltable shaped charge to neutralize sea mines from a safe standoff distance, and is used by NATO navies including the French Navy.

Le Symbo is a passive lower-back support exoskeleton made by French company Exosafe (formerly RB3D) for workers doing repetitive lifting or bending tasks. It is a one-size, unisex device that takes about 30 seconds to put on and is claimed to cut lower-back loading by up to 15%.

L'Exo Up is a passive upper-body exoskeleton made by French company Exosafe (formerly RB3D) that supports the shoulders and arms during overhead or forward-reaching work, providing up to 5 kg of lift assistance per arm to reduce shoulder fatigue.

L'Exoviti is a passive lower-back and posture-support exoskeleton made by French company Exosafe (formerly RB3D), claimed to cut lower-back loading by up to 40% for workers doing repetitive lifting tasks. It is a one-size, unisex design that takes about one minute to put on.

AutosatGTR is a shuttle robot made by Italian intralogistics company Automha (part of the Comau group) that runs within pallet racking to automatically store and retrieve goods in high-density warehouses. It is the newest model in Automha's Autosat shuttle line and is sold across Europe, the Americas and China.

The ARA1200 UHP Sprayer is a tractor-pulled, AI-powered precision sprayer made by Ecorobotix that uses six camera modules and its Plant-by-Plant AI technology to detect individual weeds and crops across a 12 m working width, firing 288 nozzles to spot-spray only targeted plants. The company reports it can cut herbicide and pesticide use by 50-95% versus blanket spraying and is sold in over 20 countries.

The AR5 is a medium-altitude, long-endurance fixed-wing uncrewed aerial system made by Portuguese company Tekever for maritime surveillance, border security and land monitoring. It spans 7.3 x 4.0 m, carries up to 50 kg of payload, cruises at 100 km/h with roughly 20 hours of endurance, and launches from unprepared airstrips; it has been selected by the UK and Portuguese militaries and used operationally in Ukraine.

Exo-H3 is a research-grade lower-limb walking exoskeleton made by Spanish company Technaid, with six actuated joints at the hip, knee and ankle that replicate a human gait pattern to assist stroke patients in neurorehabilitation research. It supports position, torque and admittance control, interfaces over Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and ROS, and fits users from 110-210 cm tall and up to 100 kg.

Alfie is an autonomous industrial mobile manipulator robot developed by RobCo GmbH of Munich, Germany, intended to move between stations and perform bimanual pick-and-place, machine loading and palletizing tasks in factories without reprogramming for each part variant. It uses RobCo physical-AI software to adapt to changing parts, containers and layouts. As of late 2026 it is being trialed with select manufacturers under pilot agreements ahead of wider commercial deployment.

Paexo Shoulder is a passive, spring-based upper-body exoskeleton made by German company Ottobock, designed to relieve shoulder and arm strain during overhead industrial work such as assembly, finishing or shipbuilding. It requires no battery or motor, using mechanical spring tension instead, and has been in series production since 2018 as part of Ottobock's Paexo exoskeleton line, used by thousands of workers worldwide.

Paexo Thumb is a lightweight passive hand exoskeleton made by German company Ottobock that supports the thumb during repetitive gripping and pinching tasks in industrial and logistics work, reducing strain on the thumb joint. It is part of Ottobock's Paexo line of passive industrial exoskeletons and is sold as model 16ES501.

The EAC 212a is an autonomous mobile robot from German material-handling company Jungheinrich, designed to automate pallet transport with an integrated lifting function at loading docks and between goods receipt, warehousing and production areas. Introduced at LogiMAT 2026, it uses onboard sensors to navigate the pre-loading zone and inside truck trailers without fixed infrastructure and can be integrated with existing warehouse management systems.

The AXL iGo is an autonomous low-lift pallet truck made by German intralogistics company STILL (part of KION Group) for automated loading and unloading of trucks at the dock, navigating the pre-loading zone and inside trailers using onboard sensors without fixed infrastructure. It has a load capacity of 1,500 kg, a rated lift of 125 mm and a travel speed of 7.2 km/h, and can load around 30 pallets in about 35 minutes when two units work in double play.

Minitractor CP is a fully autonomous agricultural mini-tractor platform developed by Russian autonomous-driving company Cognitive Pilot, built to run farm tasks around the clock without an operator. A feed-pusher variant automates pushing feed back to livestock at dairy and cattle farms, with the platform navigating via AI and computer vision and supporting FPV teleoperation up to 12 km away. It uses a series-hybrid drivetrain rated at 30 hp and can run 12-20 hours per charge.

Efarm.Pro is an autonomous-driving retrofit system made by Ukrainian company Gardarika Tres that converts standard farm tractors into remotely operated, self-driving machines for demining agricultural fields. A sensor-equipped drone first scans a field to flag suspected mine locations, after which the armor-plated autonomous tractor runs a mine-clearing attachment over the area alongside certified deminers, continuing to operate even after a detonation. The brand launched in 2023 to help clear farmland left mined after Russia's invasion.

THeMIS is a modular tracked unmanned ground vehicle made by Estonian company Milrem Robotics, built on a hybrid-electric chassis that can be fitted with different mission modules for cargo transport, casualty evacuation, explosive-ordnance disposal, route clearance and reconnaissance. It has a 750 kg rated payload, a top speed of 20 km/h, and can run up to 1.5 hours on battery alone or about 15 hours in hybrid mode. It has been acquired by over 20 countries including 8 NATO members and used operationally in Ukraine and Mali.

Promobot Thermocontrol is a standalone kiosk-style robot from Russian maker Promobot that performs contactless body-temperature screening, launched during the COVID-19 pandemic. It measures temperature in under 5 seconds with 0.2 degC accuracy, can screen over 600 people per hour, and uses facial recognition to log each visitor's photo, name and reading while alerting staff if a reading is abnormal. It is deployed in schools, offices, airports, hospitals and other public buildings.

Promobot Cyber Cafe is a self-service robotic kiosk from Russian maker Promobot that automates the sale of coffee, soft-serve ice cream and soft drinks. A humanoid robot cashier greets and takes orders at a payment terminal, while a robotic arm and built-in coffee, ice-cream and drink machines prepare and dispense items through a pickup window, offering 10 coffee types, 3 ice-cream types and 3 drink types at up to 36 coffees, 50 ice-creams and 100 drinks per hour.

Promobot Scanner is a self-service hardware-and-software kiosk from Russian maker Promobot that scans ID documents, extracts the data with optical character recognition, and automatically enters it into a facility's information systems (including 1C, InfoKlinika and MedMIS) within 4 seconds. It is used at clinics, HR departments and multi-service government centers (MFC) to replace manual check-in data entry, and the company reports deployments in more than 30 countries.

Yandex Rover is a six-wheeled autonomous sidewalk delivery robot built by Russian internet company Yandex, in service since 2019 for food and grocery delivery via Yandex Eats and Yandex Lavka. A fourth-generation version, announced in late October 2025 as the company's first serial-production model, adds a partitioned 61-liter compartment that can carry two separate orders up to 25 kg at once, travels at an average 4 km/h with up to 70 km of range per charge, and uses lidar with 100 m range that works in fog, rain and snow. It operates in Moscow, St. Petersburg, Innopolis and Murino, with the new generation launching in Kazan in December 2025 and Yandex targeting a fleet of about 20,000 rovers by the end of 2027.

SymBot is Symbotic's autonomous mobile robot that operates within an automated storage and retrieval system (ASRS) inside a steel rack structure, storing, retrieving and sequencing cases and totes for warehouse order fulfillment. It carries payloads up to 60 lb (27.2 kg) with a max payload size of 24 x 24 x 16.2 in (61 x 61 x 41.2 cm), holds power for 10+ hours per charge with auto-charging for continuous operation, and more than 22,000 units have been deployed across customers including Walmart and Target.

size: palletizing height up to 98 in; pallet size 48 x 40 in
description: DepalOne is Plus One Robotics' portable robotic work cell for automated palletizing and depalletizing of boxes, cartons, bags, and food and beverage items in warehouses. It combines a cobot or industrial robot arm with the company's PickOne vision software and Yonder remote human-assist system, handling 48 x 40 in pallets up to 98 in tall at up to 9 cycles per minute with 99% accuracy. Pricing starts at 155000 USD.

InductOne is Plus One Robotics' dual-arm parcel induction system that automatically picks and sorts polybags, boxes, envelopes, and mailers onto warehouse sortation conveyors. It handles parcels up to 15 lb and 27 x 19 x 17 in at a peak rate of 2,200 to 3,300 picks per hour with a 99% quality rate, using a compact design for space-constrained mezzanine deployments.

CivDot+ is Civ Robotics' four-wheel-drive autonomous layout robot for construction sites, using dual RTK GNSS positioning, tilt compensation, and a robotic laser pointer to mark up to 1,200 points per day at 3/100 ft (8 mm) accuracy for piling, pre-drilling, and foundation layout. It runs CivPlan planning software and can be remote-operated from up to 100 feet away.

CivDot Mini is Civ Robotics' compact two-wheel-drive layout robot that uses dual RTK positioning and spray paint to mark points, lines, dashes, and curves from digital designs for road striping, parking lot marking, and airport work. It can mark up to 17 miles of lines per day at sub-inch (2 cm) accuracy and supports remote operation up to 100 feet away.

The EG7 is Okibo's compact autonomous construction robot for residential and office interiors, performing wall painting, sanding, and drywall finishing. At 27 in wide it fits through standard doorways, runs on standard 5 kWh cart batteries, and operates without Wi-Fi or site preparation using omnidirectional swerve drive and quick-change toolheads.

The EG7+ is Okibo's heavy-duty autonomous construction robot for commercial sites such as data centers and manufacturing facilities, reaching up to 24 ft to paint, sand, and apply Level 4-5 drywall finishing on drywall, concrete, and brick. It runs on a 15 kWh lithium-ion battery for about 10 hours and uses omnidirectional swerve drive.

Burro is an autonomous ground robot that follows workers or drives set routes to carry and tow loads in orchards, vineyards, and nurseries, using computer vision, RTK GPS, and LiDAR for navigation. It weighs 420 lb (190 kg), carries up to 500 lb on flat surfaces, reaches 5 mph, and runs on field-swappable 2.56 kWh LFP batteries for up to 10 miles per charge.

The Grande 15 is Burro's mid-size autonomous work platform for agriculture and industrial sites, using 360-degree 3D LiDAR, 12 cameras, RTK GPS, and Pop-Up Autonomy to carry or tow loads with 4-wheel drive. It weighs 1,081 lb (490 kg), carries up to 1,000 lb (454 kg), tows up to 5,000 lb on flat paved surfaces, and reaches 5.8 mph on a 48V 10 kWh battery pack.

The Grande 44 is Burro's most powerful autonomous work platform, delivering 44 hp peak (18 hp continuous) for heavy-duty agricultural and industrial hauling. It carries up to 1,500 lb, tows up to 6,000 lb, reaches 5 mph, and uses independent 4-wheel drive with 4 stereo cameras, 360-degree 3D LiDAR, and RTK GNSS; it can apply herbicide only where weeds are detected with up to 75% less chemical use via the Sprayito attachment.

Vulcan is FarmWise's AI-guided precision weeding implement for specialty crops, using a high-frame-rate machine-vision system and fast actuators to identify and mechanically remove intra-row weeds in fractions of a second. It covers up to 3 acres per hour, is sold through a partnership with RDO Equipment Co., and is built on a modular, self-calibrating architecture with over-the-air software updates.

Dispatch is Berkshire Grey's compact small-parcel sorting system for e-commerce warehouses, using the company's patented Hyperscanner to identify polybags, mailers, cartons, and irregular packages for dynamic, real-time destination routing. It supports both manual and automated induction and is designed to increase sortation throughput and accuracy without expanding a facility's footprint.

Stride is Berkshire Grey's robotic shuttle sortation system for warehouses, using a parallel-shuttle architecture with configurable 8, 10, or 14 m sort beams to route rolling, unbagged, and irregular merchandise to totes or boxes. It scales from 4,000 to over 60,000 units per hour at over 99% accuracy while cutting sortation footprint by about 50% on average.

Dogtooth Technologies' Gen 5 is a vision-guided autonomous robot that harvests strawberries in UK and Australian tabletop glasshouse and polytunnel farms, extracting 80-90% of ripe fruit with under 2.5% machine-made waste. It navigates crop rows autonomously, inspects and grades berries on-board to eliminate separate QC, and runs on a swappable battery rated for about 200 kg of fruit picked per day.

AV1 is a telepresence robot made by Norwegian company No Isolation that lets a child who cannot attend school in person join lessons remotely, controlled from a smartphone or tablet app with a camera, microphone, speaker and light indicators for raising a hand. Marketed as an attendance and reintegration solution for pupils with long-term illness, school anxiety or SEND, it is CE certified, ISO 27001 compliant and manufactured in Norway. No Isolation reports over 5,000 AV1 units deployed across 20 European countries, including UK schools.

Heavy Picker is an AI-guided waste-sorting robot from Finnish company ZenRobotics (now a Terex brand) built for bulky construction and demolition waste. It uses a heavy-duty robotic arm paired with the ZenBrAIn/ZenVision recognition software to identify and pick recyclable fractions with high purity from mixed waste streams. ZenRobotics launched Heavy Picker commercially in 2015, following its earlier ZenRobotics Recycler that began waste sorting in Helsinki in 2010.

Fast Picker is a high-speed AI waste-sorting robot from Finnish company ZenRobotics (now a Terex brand), designed for lightweight recyclables and marketed as achieving roughly double the pick rate of a human sorter with customisable precision. It shares the ZenBrAIn/ZenVision machine-vision and AI stack used across ZenRobotics' sorting line and was launched commercially in 2018.

Q-Bot is a London-based company whose small tracked, remotely operated robot enters the void beneath suspended timber ground floors to survey and spray-apply insulation foam without lifting floorboards. It is offered as a 'Robot as a Service' to accredited installation partners, landlords and homeowners in the UK, and the company reports insulating thousands of homes to date. Q-Bot also sells SWARM, a companion compliance-management software platform for retrofit projects.

The DeLaval VMS V300 is a voluntary (robotic) milking system from Swedish dairy-equipment maker DeLaval that lets cows be milked automatically, on their own schedule, without a human operator attaching the milking cluster. DeLaval markets the V300 series as its most flexible milking-robot line and continues to add features to it, including a 2025 update bundling previously optional functions as standard. It is used on dairy farms across the UK, Ireland, the Nordics and elsewhere worldwide.

HUGIN Superior is a 6.6 m, 2,200 kg autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) from Norwegian company Kongsberg Maritime, rated to 6,000 m depth and carrying a HISAS 1032 synthetic-aperture sonar, EM2040 Mk2 multibeam echosounder, camera, laser profiler, sub-bottom profiler, magnetometer and gas sensors for seabed survey and mapping. It has an endurance of about 72 hours at 3 knots and is used commercially for offshore survey as well as by navies, including a 2022 French Navy (DGA) deployment for deep-sea exploration from the vessel Beautemps-Beaupre.

HUGIN Endurance is a long-range autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) from Norwegian company Kongsberg Maritime, unveiled in 2021 as the next generation of the HUGIN AUV family. It extends mission duration to about 15 days and can map up to 1,100 square kilometres in a single mission without a mothership, carrying a KONGSBERG HiSAS synthetic-aperture sonar, multibeam echosounder, sub-bottom profiler, magnetometer and a Maritime Broadband Radio link, and is used for offshore-wind and seabed survey as well as naval mine-hunting.

Solix is an autonomous, solar-powered ground robot made by Brazilian ag-tech company Solinftec for real-time field scouting and site-specific pest and weed treatment in row crops, sugarcane, coffee, forestry, and citrus. The robot is in commercial deployment across Brazil and the United States, with Solinftec reporting over 100 autonomous Solix robots deployed in the U.S. and a 243% expansion of its U.S. footprint by early 2026.

ST ("Standard") is a teleoperated firefighting ground robot originally developed by Brazilian startup Unidroid Robotica do Brasil, now part of Ambipar Robotics. It was the company's first firefighting robot, unveiled in 2018, and is used to fight large fires at close range without exposing firefighters to danger.

STW ("Standard Wide") is a larger teleoperated firefighting ground robot made by Brazilian manufacturer Ambipar Robotics (formerly Unidroid Robotica do Brasil), built for refinery-scale fires. An explosion-resistant STW-Ex variant was developed for Petrobras oil and gas facilities, and a current STW Response version has been exported and used operationally, including at a 2026 solvent-plant fire in Itaquaquecetuba, Brazil.

T.A.R.S. (Tatico Apoio de Resposta e Servico) is a multi-function teleoperated unmanned ground vehicle made by Brazilian manufacturer Ambipar Robotics, weighing about 250 kg with a 150 kg payload capacity. An EOD (explosive ordnance disposal) version was delivered to the Brazilian Army's engineering department in July 2026 after the company won a Brazilian Army contract for bomb-disposal robots.

m-FLEX is a portable, cable-driven robotic exoskeleton for upper-limb neuromotor rehabilitation, developed from patented research at the Universidade Federal do Espirito Santo (Ufes) and commercialized by the Brazilian startup Symbios. Designed to let patients continue arm-rehabilitation exercises outside traditional clinics, it was selected as the only robotics finalist from the Americas at Medica 2026 in Germany.

Kachaka is a small, low-cost autonomous mobile robot made by Preferred Robotics, a spinoff of Japanese AI company Preferred Networks, that follows users around the home or office and can fetch and carry furniture-mounted shelves or items on voice command. It launched in Japan in 2023 and is also marketed as a simple business AMR platform.

TX SCARA is a SCARA-type robot arm from Telexistence that autonomously restocks beverage refrigerators in Japanese convenience stores, running on Nvidia Jetson edge AI with Microsoft Azure cloud support. It operates autonomously about 98% of the time, with remote human operators stepping in via VR headset for the rest, and was deployed to roughly 300 FamilyMart stores starting in 2022.

T-54ENRYU is tmsuk's disaster-response rescue robot in its POWER-ROID line: a tracked, remotely operated machine up to 5.4 m long, 1.4 m wide and 1.7 m tall, weighing up to 3.5 tonnes, with dual synchronized hydraulic arms and 7 onboard cameras for wireless teleoperation. It is used by Japanese fire and disaster-response agencies, including joint training exercises with police in 2025.

RODEM is tmsuk's rear-entry personal mobility robot that lets a seated rider transfer directly from a bed or chair without being lifted, with adjustable seat height for eye-level travel alongside pedestrians. It has been trialed as a sightseeing mobility device on public street tours in Tokyo's Yaesu-Nihombashi area.

PATORO is an autonomous security patrol robot made by ROBO-HI (formerly ZMP, renamed April 2025), which patrols indoor and outdoor facilities at walking pace using autonomous driving, uses a 360-degree camera plus an infrared camera for nighttime/thermal intruder detection, and can dock to charge. It detects abnormal sounds and fire, and can report incidents to police or security firms via its communication link; it shares its compact chassis with ZMP/ROBO-HI's DeliRo delivery robot.

DeliRo is ROBO-HI's (formerly ZMP, renamed April 2025) autonomous last-mile delivery robot, trialed on Japanese public roads with Japan Post and in pilots with partners such as ENEOS; it can carry up to 100 kg (50 kg on public roads) at up to 6 km/h for about 4 hours per charge. Variant body styles include DeliRo Care and DeliRo Truck, which swap the delivery lockers for an open cargo bed, and DeliRo Tractor for hospital goods transport.

The MK-V was Monarch Tractor's fully electric, driver-optional autonomous tractor for vineyards, orchards, dairy, and open-field farms, offering 40-70 hp, up to 14 hours of runtime, and WingspanAI fleet-management and row-follow autonomy with 360-degree collision-avoidance cameras. It shipped in Standard, Dairy, and Utility trim variants; Monarch Tractor shut down in April 2026 and sold its assets to Caterpillar, discontinuing the product.

BetterPick is Advanced Farm Technologies' autonomous strawberry-harvesting machine, using real-time stereo vision to spot ripe fruit, food-safe soft grippers to pick it, a hybrid-electric drive to navigate rows without a driver, and onboard tray stacking to hold harvested fruit. The company reported a pick rate around 100 lb/hour per machine (about 5x a human harvester) before folding in mid-2025 after CNH Industrial acquired its IP and assets.

The Apple Harvester is Advanced Farm Technologies' robotic orchard machine that autonomously drives down rows (Autodrive), uses stereo cameras to find apples meeting color and size specs, and removes them with soft twist-and-pull grippers before conveying them into standard bins, passing full and empty bins through without disrupting harvest. It was marketed to reduce field headcount by more than 50% and was commercially deployed in Washington state orchards before the company folded in mid-2025.

Lio is a mobile service robot from Swiss manufacturer F&P Robotics that combines a collaborative arm, voice interaction with ChatGPT-based conversational AI, and autonomous indoor navigation. It is deployed in healthcare and elderly-care settings such as Switzerland's Rehabilitation Clinic Zihlschlacht for internal deliveries, front-desk services and assistance tasks.

Path Robotics' Intelligent Welding Cell is an AI-powered robotic welding cell for high-mix production that needs no manual programming of weld paths. The company's Obsidian AI is stated to deliver up to 17x faster throughput and 97%+ first-pass yield versus manual welding, offered via a no-capex robotics-as-a-service model. Path Robotics is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio.

Rove is Path Robotics' mobile welding robot, pairing its Obsidian AI with a legged, walking platform so autonomous welding capability can be brought directly to large workpieces on the shop floor, built for large-scale fabrication.

The Vecna APT is an autonomous pallet truck for long-haul warehouse and distribution-center transport. It handles double-stacked pallets up to 8,000 lb, carries a maximum payload of 7,936 lb (about 3,600 kg), and reaches a top speed of 6.7 mph.

The Vecna CPJ (Co-bot Pallet Jack) is a collaborative robot for short-haul moves in tight spaces; an operator manually spears the payload and programs its drop-off destination, moving pallets, carts, racks and bins up to 3,300 lb (1,500 kg) at up to 2.8 mph.

The Vecna ATG is a fork-free autonomous tugger for high-capacity, high-throughput pallet-train moves in manufacturing and warehousing, hauling trains of nearly 10,000 lb (9,920 lb / 4,500 kg) at up to 6.0 mph.

The Vecna AFL is a driverless, counterbalanced autonomous forklift moving a wide range of payloads and pallet types, from ground-to-ground workflows to conveyor and rack put-away, reaching up to 60 in (1.5 m) lift height with a payload of up to 3,000 lb (1,360 kg) at up to 6.7 mph.

Orchard GUSS is GUSS Automation's flagship autonomous, GPS-guided orchard sprayer; a single operator can remotely supervise a fleet of up to 8 GUSS sprayers at once from a pickup truck, and the system integrates with the John Deere Operations Center. GUSS Automation (Kingsburg, California) was acquired by John Deere in 2025.

Mini GUSS is GUSS Automation's smaller autonomous orchard/vineyard sprayer, built about 25% smaller than the flagship Orchard GUSS while offering the same precision and efficiency, for tighter row spacing.
Herbicide GUSS is GUSS Automation's autonomous sprayer variant built specifically for herbicide application in orchards.

Amiga Flex is Bonsai Robotics' versatile, cost-effective autonomous platform for research and light-duty applications in specialty crops, supporting tasks such as weeding, spraying, towing and mowing. Bonsai Robotics (San Jose, California) builds on the farm-ng Amiga base platform after acquiring farm-ng in 2025.
Amiga Max is Bonsai Robotics' compact diesel-hybrid autonomous platform for heavier-duty spraying, weeding and mowing in specialty-crop orchards and vineyards.

Raptor is Gecko Robotics' next-generation industrial inspection robot for pipelines, storage tanks and other steel infrastructure, collecting structural-condition data 3-5x faster than the company's prior systems. It was unveiled at ADIPEC 2026 with UAE energy company ADNOC as its first customer. Gecko Robotics is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

Komodo is a Gecko Robotics crawling robot that assesses non-skid deck coating on U.S. Navy ship flight decks, using electromagnetic acoustic conduction to create an ultrasonic waveform that penetrates to the base metal and detects corrosion without stripping the coating; it lets the Navy assess deck condition six to 12 months before a ship enters maintenance.

Corvus One is an autonomous inventory-counting drone for warehouses that flies scheduled cycle-count missions without pilots, reflectors or navigation beacons, using 14 onboard cameras for omnidirectional collision avoidance to scan barcodes, locate empty slots and count cases, including fully lights-out at night. It is designed, manufactured and tested by Corvus Robotics in Mountain View, California, and is used by companies including ASICS America, GNC and Southern Glazer's Wine & Spirits.

The Wing 8000 Series is Alphabet subsidiary Wing's current package-delivery drone, carrying payloads up to 5 lb (2.3 kg) at speeds up to about 60 mph and a range up to 12 miles at a cruise altitude of about 150 ft, using separate vertical-lift and forward-cruise motors. Wing operates delivery service with retailers including Walmart across multiple U.S. metro areas.

The Wing 7000 Series is an earlier-generation package-delivery drone from Alphabet's Wing, using the same dual-propulsion design as later Wing drones, with separate vertical-lift motors for takeoff/landing and forward cruise motors for efficient flight.

HP SitePrint is an autonomous three-wheeled robot that prints 2D construction layouts (lines, arcs and text) directly onto a job-site floor, guided by a Robotic Total Station (e.g., Leica or Topcon systems) for precise positioning. HP states it lays out work up to 10x faster than manual methods; it ships with two swappable batteries each rated for about four hours of continuous layout work, and has been used on projects such as the LIRR Train Hall renovation at New York's Penn Station.

Titan is ICON's current-generation large-scale 3D construction printer, capable of printing a 2,500 sq ft home's wall system in under seven days at a stated cost of about $20/sq ft, more than 40% below the U.S. national average, paired with ICON's BuildOS software platform for remote monitoring and fleet operation. ICON is based in Austin, Texas, and Titan supersedes the company's earlier Vulcan printer.

The Optimus System is American Robotics' fully automated drone-in-a-box platform for 24/7 on-demand aerial data operations, automatically swapping among up to 9 payloads and 11 batteries for continuous missions. Each flight lasts up to 40 minutes with a range of 5 to 10 miles, and the system is rated IP52 rain resistant / IP54 in a climate-controlled configuration. American Robotics is based in Sparks, Maryland.

The Iron Drone Raider System is American Robotics' autonomous counter-UAS (counter-drone) platform for airspace security, using radar and sensor arrays to detect, track and intercept unauthorized drones over public events, critical infrastructure and other sensitive sites with minimal human intervention.

LUCY is an autonomous mobile robot made by Austrian manufacturer DS Automotion for in-plant logistics, carrying roll containers, racks, shelves and pallets up to 500 kg at up to 1.6 m/s. It uses SLAM-based laser navigation, 360-degree personnel protection and automatic charging, with a modular frame that can be customized with different load-handling attachments.

AMADEUS is an autonomous driverless high-lift forklift from Austrian manufacturer DS Automotion, built to transport Euro pallets, industrial pallets, boxes and containers up to 2.0 tonnes at speeds up to 1.8 m/s. It is sold in mono/duplex, wide, low and counterbalanced variants with lift heights from 85 mm up to 2.8 m, using SLAM/laser navigation, 360-degree safety and automatic charging.

ARNY is an autonomous counterbalanced reach truck from Austrian manufacturer DS Automotion for narrow-aisle, high-bay warehouse logistics. The Mono, Duplex and Triplex variants carry up to 1.5 tonnes at up to 1.5 m/s, with lift heights ranging from 1.5 m up to 7.45 m depending on variant, and an ARNY HD Triplex version reaches lift heights of 10.8 m at up to 1.0 tonne payload.

AMY is a compact autonomous mobile robot from Austrian manufacturer DS Automotion for small-parts transport and production-line station concatenation, carrying up to 35 kg at up to 1.8 m/s. It uses laser scanners and time-of-flight cameras for 360-degree personnel protection, SLAM navigation, automatic lithium-battery charging, and is offered in deck, lift and flap configurations.

OSCAR is a low-profile autonomous mobile robot from Austrian manufacturer DS Automotion for driving under load carriers and dollies, carrying up to 1000 kg at up to 1.6 m/s with lift heights from 80-160 mm depending on the spin 180, spin 360 or omnidirectional Omni/Omni XL variant. The Omni XL variant carries up to 1250 kg with full omnidirectional mobility.

SALLY is DS Automotion's smallest autonomous mobile robot, a welded-steel platform for industrial and public environments carrying up to 100 kg at up to 1.6 m/s using contour-based laser navigation. A SALLY Courier variant, carrying up to 50 kg at up to 1.0 m/s with 3D-camera obstacle avoidance, is built for hospitals to transport sterile goods, documents, lab samples, instruments and medications.

LiftSuit 2 is a lightweight occupational exosuit from Swiss manufacturer Auxivo, an ETH Zurich spin-off founded in 2019, that supports the back and hip muscles during lifting and forward-leaning work tasks.
CarrySuit is an upper-body occupational exoskeleton from Swiss manufacturer Auxivo that relieves the arms, shoulders and upper body when carrying or holding heavy payloads.
DeltaSuit is an occupational exoskeleton from Swiss manufacturer Auxivo that supports workers performing frequent overhead and above-shoulder-level tasks.
OmniSuit is a multitask occupational exoskeleton from Swiss manufacturer Auxivo combining support for overhead work, lifting and forward-leaning activities in one wearable system.

ACH iGo is a compact autonomous mobile robot from German forklift maker STILL, built for short-to-medium distance intralogistics with on-the-spot carrier rotation for tight spaces. It carries 1000-1500 kg at up to 1.2-2.0 m/s using QR-code navigation and needs only a 1.4 m minimum aisle width.

AXH iGo is an autonomous mobile robot from German forklift maker STILL for long-distance intralogistics transport, carrying 1000 kg at up to 2.2 m/s. It uses SLAM navigation with obstacle circumnavigation and a 3D camera for precise handling of trolleys and pallets in standard-width aisles (2.8 m minimum).

EXV-CB iGo is an automated counterbalance high-lift truck from German forklift maker STILL, carrying 1400 kg up to a 3.8 m lift height at up to 7.2 km/h. It has cantilever forks for pallets, mesh boxes and special carriers, dual automatic/manual operation modes, a 360-degree laser scanner and ISO 3691-4 safety compliance.

LTX 50 iGo is an automated tugger train from German forklift maker STILL for cycle-controlled production-line supply and disposal, towing up to 5 tonnes at up to 1.7 m/s with 360-degree personnel protection and optional dual manual/automatic operation.

KMP 3000P omni is an omnidirectional top-loading autonomous mobile robot platform from KUKA for transporting large, heavy products such as EV battery modules across production and logistics floors, carrying up to 3000 kg. Its omnidirectional drive allows sideways movement, on-the-spot rotation and smooth curve navigation in congested factory and warehouse layouts.

KMP 1500P diffDrive is a differential-drive autonomous mobile robot platform from KUKA engineered to move pallets and other load carriers up to 1500 kg through narrow aisles in manufacturing and warehouse settings.

KMR iiwa is a mobile manipulator from KUKA that pairs a sensitive LBR iiwa lightweight arm with an autonomously navigating mobile platform, moving itself precisely and safely to where it is needed in flexible manufacturing environments.

KMR iisy is an autonomous mobile cobot platform from KUKA combining the entry-level LBR iisy collaborative arm with a self-navigating base, used for collaborative assembly, intralogistics and service-robot tasks.

RunPick (Robotic Universal Picker) is an automated case-picking and palletizing robot system from Austrian intralogistics maker Knapp, placing up to 6 pack units per cycle onto pallets or roll containers for dry, fresh and frozen goods. It integrates machine-vision quality checks, KiSoft Pack Master packing-pattern software, and typically pairs with Knapp's Evo Shuttle storage system.

VELUM is an AI-driven robotic system from Munich-based sewts for automating textile handling in industrial laundries, such as folding towels and processing garments. It uses real-time perception to predict how easily deformable fabrics will behave when grasped, a task traditionally too unpredictable for standard robotic automation.

Vmax 160 is a next-generation automated medication-dispensing and storage robot from BD Rowa (Becton Dickinson's German pharmacy-automation unit, Rowa Automatisierungssysteme), built for high-volume centralized outpatient pharmacies handling specialty and refrigerated medicines. It loads totes in about 3 seconds per tote at 99.8% accuracy, supports 2-8C cold-chain storage, automatically flags and blocks expired medications, and is widely deployed across Europe with its first U.S. installation at Fairview Health Services in 2026.

FM-X iGo is an automated reach truck from German forklift maker STILL for narrow-aisle warehouses under 3 m wide, carrying up to 2330 kg to lift heights up to 10.47 m at up to 7.2 km/h. It uses cantilever forks with a Pallet-Positioning-System, 360-degree laser scanning to ISO 3691-4, lithium-ion batteries and the STILL iGo easy automation interface.

EXV iGo is an autonomous high-lift pallet truck from German forklift maker STILL for production logistics and staging areas, carrying up to 1600 kg to a 3.8 m lift height at up to 7.2 km/h. It offers dual automatic/manual operation, 360-degree pedestrian-protection scanners, and lithium-ion or lead-acid battery options via the STILL iGo easy interface.

KMF 1500P-CB is an autonomous counterbalance forklift from KUKA carrying up to 1500 kg to a 3 m lift height, built for long transport routes, closed pallets and transfer stations where pallets cannot be accessed from below.

C-MATIC HP is an autonomous mobile robot from German forklift maker Linde Material Handling that carries loads up to 1000 kg over medium and long distances using laser-based natural-feature navigation with no floor infrastructure, suited to mixed manual/automated operation in production plants and 3PL warehouses.
L-MATIC AC is an automated counterbalanced stacker truck from German forklift maker Linde Material Handling, automating storage and retrieval with lift heights up to 4.2 metres.
R-MATIC is an automated reach truck from German forklift maker Linde Material Handling for storage and retrieval at heights up to 11 metres, carrying loads up to 1600 kg.
K-MATIC is an automated very-narrow-aisle (VNA) truck from German forklift maker Linde Material Handling, built for high-bay warehouse storage and retrieval at lift heights up to 14 metres.

TX2-60L MedX Ready is a 6-axis precision robot from Swiss manufacturer Staubli built as a medical and surgical assistant for orthopedics, neurosurgery, cancer surgery and diagnostics. It is developed under an ISO 13485:2016-compatible quality system, has a hygienic disinfectant-resistant surface, and offers an optional MedXguiding force-sensor hand-guiding mode for intuitive manual positioning.

MATE-XB is a battery-free, passive lumbar-support exoskeleton from Italian robotics maker Comau that stores human energy in a spring-based Torque Generating Box to assist workers lifting and bending. It provides adjustable assistance up to 25 kg across 5 levels and uses a passive kinematic chain that allows free trunk movement without hindering walking.

RB-VULCANO is a customizable collaborative mobile manipulator from Spanish robotics maker Robotnik, combining an omnidirectional AMR base with a lift column and a Universal Robots UR5e, UR10e or UR16e arm. It carries up to 1,750 kg of payload, has a tableboard that supports objects up to 300 kg, an arm reach from 750 mm to 1,500 mm (up to 3,000 mm working height), and uses integrated safety lasers to share workspace with people.

RB-ROBOUT XL is a heavy-payload autonomous mobile robot from Spanish maker Robotnik, a customized version of the RB-ROBOUT optimized for indoor factories and warehouses with flat floors. It carries up to 2,000 kg, uses an omnidirectional low-profile steel chassis, safety lasers for collaborative obstacle avoidance, and a ROS-based architecture with up to 18 hours of autonomy.

RB-ELI is an autonomous smart shopping-cart robot from Spanish maker Robotnik that follows shoppers around a store, guides them to products, and supports onboard-screen product selection and automatic payment via barcode scanning. It uses voice-recognition sensors and obstacle avoidance to track and navigate after a customer, and can also help locate a parked car or verify purchase details.

RB-VOGUI XL is an all-terrain autonomous mobile robot from Spanish maker Robotnik, an increased-payload version of the RB-VOGUI platform aimed at outdoor transport tasks such as last-mile delivery, agriculture and logistics R&D. It carries up to 200 kg, has steerable wheels supporting omnidirectional and double-Ackermann drive modes, IP53 weatherproofing, and climbs slopes up to 47%.

Vertex One is a modular autonomous drone platform from Dutch robotics maker Avular, built around an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX for real-time autonomous navigation. It carries up to 2 kg of payload with a quick-lock, tool-free payload interface, flies up to 30 minutes per charge, and is programmable through an SDK supporting ROS 2 and C++ for inspection, agriculture/forestry mapping and research swarming applications.

JO is an ultra-compact autonomous crawler robot from French agri-robotics maker Naio Technologies, designed for in-row and inter-row work in narrow vineyards, tree nurseries and conifer plots. It navigates autonomously with GNSS RTK, lifts implements up to 250 kg, runs up to 10 hours per charge, and supports tools such as mechanical and electric intervine weeders, a vibrotiller and a vine shoot remover; as of June 2026 it is no longer manufactured or sold by Naio.

The ARA900 is an ultra-high-precision (UHP) tractor-mounted sprayer from Swiss agri-tech maker Ecorobotix that uses its Plant-by-Plant AI to apply crop-protection products and non-selective herbicides only where weeds are detected. It has an adjustable working width up to 9 m with 216 high-precision spray nozzles, covers up to 6 ha/hour, and reduces plant-protection product use by up to 95%.

The AR3-EVO is a modular unmanned aerial system from Portuguese drone maker Tekever, launchable by catapult, VTOL or parachute and operable in GPS- and comms-denied environments. It has a maximum take-off weight of 25-30 kg, up to 22 hours of fixed-wing endurance (14 hours in VTOL mode), a 6 kg payload capacity, a 46-knot cruise speed and a communications range up to 230 km, supporting interchangeable ISR, communications-relay and electronic-warfare payloads.

VEENY is an autonomous very-narrow-aisle (VNA) turret truck AGV/AMR from French warehouse robotics maker Balyo, built on a standard OEM VNA forklift chassis. It operates in aisles as narrow as 1.8 m, lifts pallets up to 17 m high with a 1,500 kg load capacity, and uses Balyo's infrastructure-free navigation with 3D pallet detection and a 360-degree safety system.

REACHY is an autonomous reach-truck AGV/AMR from French warehouse robotics maker Balyo, built on an industrial reach forklift chassis for high-bay pallet storage. It works in aisles as narrow as 2.9 m, lifts up to 11 m with a 1,400-1,600 kg load capacity, and uses Balyo's infrastructure-free navigation with 3D pallet detection for pick-and-drop operations.

LOWY is an autonomous stacker AGV/AMR from French warehouse robotics maker Balyo, built on a standard OEM forklift chassis for horizontal pallet movement in warehouses and manufacturing. It has a 1,600 kg load capacity, lifts up to 2.9 m, works in aisles from 2.9 m, and uses Balyo's infrastructure-free navigation with 3D pallet detection to interface with conveyors, stretch wrappers and palletizers.

Rhyno Protect is a compact, fully electric firefighting robot from French maker Shark Robotics, designed to access confined spaces and support first responders. It delivers a 1,900 L/min water or foam cannon, runs up to 5 hours per charge, is remote-controlled up to 1,000 m away, measures 78 cm wide, and carries modular payloads for reconnaissance, CBRN detection and casualty evacuation.

Barakuda is a rugged all-terrain mule robot from French maker Shark Robotics built to transport equipment for defense, security and emergency-response teams. It carries up to 500 kg and tows up to 1 ton, climbs slopes up to 40 degrees, clears 30 cm obstacles, runs up to 10 hours on Shark Energy batteries, and is remote-controlled up to 1 km with a mesh relay option.

Atrax is a compact explosive-ordnance-disposal (EOD) and counter-IED robot from French maker Shark Robotics for bomb-disposal, CBRN-detection and demining operations. It has patented dual-function flippers for stairs and wire-crossing, a 5-axis arm with a 200 mm clamp, up to 6 hours of autonomy, a 1,000 m line-of-sight control range via mesh relay, and a compact 115 x 48 x 39 cm footprint.

EffiBOT is a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AGV/AMR) from French logistics robotics maker Effidence that acts as a handling assistant in factories and warehouses. It carries up to 300 kg or tows up to 500 kg, offers a Follow-Me mode to trail a picking operator or full autonomous navigation using natural-environment recognition, drives up to 7 km/h with IP54 protection, and runs up to 8 hours per charge.

Aera is a long-range VTOL fixed-wing drone from Dutch manufacturer Avy that takes off and lands vertically on four rotors before transitioning to efficient fixed-wing cruise flight. It covers up to 150 km of range (100 minutes of flight time) with a 3 kg payload capacity, cruises at 23 m/s, launches from Avy's own docking station for repeatable autonomous missions, and is rated to fly in winds up to 30 knots for emergency response, inspection and perimeter-security use.

The Lely Astronaut Max is a centralised support unit for automatic milking robots on large dairy farms, serving two Astronaut robots from a single Central Unit. It delivers filtered, cooled milk over long distances to the milk tank and supplies centralised cleaning detergents, vacuum, hot-water cleaning and udder-care utilities to boost milking-robot efficiency, hygiene and uptime, with Horizon software for centralised monitoring.

The Lely Calm is an automatic calf feeder from Dutch agri-robotics maker Lely that gives calves unlimited milk for their first 35 days before gradually reducing volume to promote roughage intake. It uses a HygieneBox with an automated two-step cleaning process that rinses the teat with fresh water after every feed and cleans the system interior with water and detergent up to four times a day, with full lifecycle tracking through Lely Horizon.

ADAPTO BAGSTORE is a shuttle-based automated baggage storage system from Dutch logistics automation maker Vanderlande (part of Toyota Automated Logistics Group) for airports. Multidirectional shuttle robots move along an integrated track within a racking structure to store and retrieve bags on demand, use RF-tagged carriers for tracking, and the modular design lets operators add racking and shuttles to scale throughput.

VarioStore Flex is an early-bag-storage system from Dutch logistics automation maker Vanderlande that uses automated guided vehicles (AGVs) to move mobile luggage racks to predefined locations and reintegrate bags into the main conveyor line. It gives direct access to single bags for improved efficiency and is designed for flexible, space-saving extension at airports.

The Symani Surgical System is a robotic microsurgery and supermicrosurgery platform from Italian medical robotics maker Medical Microinstruments (MMI), based in Pisa. It uses NanoWrist instruments with the world's smallest robotic wrist to replicate natural hand movements for delicate tasks such as vessel anastomosis and dissection, and is used clinically in lymphedema treatment, breast reconstruction, head-and-neck cancer and trauma surgery.

Skelex 360 is a passive, unpowered shoulder-and-arm support exoskeleton from Dutch wearable-robotics maker Skelex, designed for overhead and mid-range lifting tasks. It offloads strain from the shoulders and arms with adjustable force support and armcup positioning, and is used by welders, installers, painters, maintenance engineers and dairy farmers.

Skelex Ironhand is a powered hand-and-finger grip-assistance glove from Dutch wearable-robotics maker Skelex that boosts a worker's grip strength by up to 80 N (about 16 N per finger) to reduce hand and forearm fatigue during repetitive or precise tasks. It adapts to natural hand movements with configurable force, sensitivity and locking settings, aiming to prevent work-related musculoskeletal disorders such as carpal tunnel syndrome.

ANAFI Ai is a 4G-connected professional robotic UAV from French drone maker Parrot, built for extended-range beyond-line-of-sight operation over cellular networks. It supports autonomous photogrammetry for large-scale mapping, is open to developers through Parrot's SDK, and is positioned for enterprise inspection and surveying work.

ANAFI USA is a professional drone from French maker Parrot designed and manufactured in the United States for first responders and enterprise users, and listed on the U.S. DoD's Blue sUAS approved program. It carries a 32x zoom camera alongside a thermal imager that detects centimetric hot spots from altitudes up to 40 m, and is NDAA and TAA compliant for government use.

Goyo is a solar-powered strawberry aid-harvester robot from Spanish agri-robotics maker Agrobot (Badajoz) that assists field workers by following crop rows with LIDAR-guided autonomous navigation and automatically stopping at row ends. Its stainless-steel and military-grade-aluminum frame carries a conveyor that moves fruit trays to the edge for faster unloading, runs on stored solar energy even at night, and can add UV-C treatment for chemical-free mildew control.

Kiko is an ultra-compact autonomous utility robot from Spanish agri-robotics maker Agrobot for high-precision crop treatment in tight rows, requiring no programming or GPS setup before starting work. It has a 42 hp electric powertrain, up to 20 hours of battery runtime, a stainless-steel chassis, and tows chemical-free UV-C treatment or electrostatic sprayer trailer modules for pest and disease control.

Curro is an autonomous insect-vacuum robot from Spanish agri-robotics maker Agrobot that extracts light-bodied pests such as Lygus bugs, whiteflies and flea beetles from row crops like strawberries, melons and leafy greens. It uses reactive navigation that tracks bed furrows and autonomously turns at row ends, is available in electric or diesel powertrains (diesel variant runs up to 40 hours), and captures roughly twice as many insects as traditional tractor-mounted vacuum attachments.

KOMPAI delivery is a range of autonomous mobile robots from French maker Kompai Robotics for hospital logistics, transporting medicines, chemotherapy bags and medical equipment through corridors, lifts and wards. The range includes a cabinet-equipped Top Module with modular removable cells, a Tractor for towing carts, and Container/Transfer variants with lifting tables and roller conveyors for automated loading and unloading, all navigating autonomously while avoiding obstacles.

R-One+ is a CE-marked robotic system from French medical robotics maker Robocath (a Stereotaxis subsidiary) for interventional cardiology and neurointervention. It gives physicians millimetric, joystick-controlled motorized control of guidewires, balloon catheters and stents from a shielded control room, is compatible with most leading interventional devices, and a published R-EVOLUTION study found it reduced physician radiation exposure by 84%.

DriX is a series of uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) from French maritime-robotics maker Exail for hydrography, oceanography, scientific monitoring and AUV/ROV subsea-positioning support. The vessels operate in remote-controlled or supervised-autonomous mode using the CortiX autonomy solution (first deployed on the DriX H-8), support line-of-sight and over-the-horizon operation via a multi-channel communication system, and have logged more than 300,000 hours at sea and 1 million nautical miles of autonomous navigation.

Explorer MB is a personal-use pediatric gait-assistance exoskeleton from Spanish bionics maker Marsi Bionics, built on the company's ARES variable-stiffness active-joint technology, for children with neurodevelopmental disorders. It lets children walk independently in everyday environments such as parks, streets and schools, and is designed to grow with the user across an age range of roughly 2 to 17 years.

Trey is Gideon's autonomous forklift robot for fully automated trailer loading and unloading of palletized goods, using 3D vision and on-board AI to navigate loading bays without a human operator unloading the first pallets. It ships in Medium-Duty (1,600 kg) and Heavy-Duty (2,200 kg) chassis and integrates with warehouse WMS/WES/MES systems. Gideon is a Croatian robotics company backed by Toyota.

The MV-4 is DOK-ING's light-category remote-controlled mine-clearance and EOD robot, resistant to anti-personnel mine detonations and able to sustain anti-tank mine blasts. Fitted with interchangeable front tools (flail, tiller, dozer blade) and a manipulator arm rated for 400 kg, it clears a path up to 1,800 mm wide at up to 1,800 m2/h. DOK-ING, a Croatian unmanned-ground-vehicle maker founded in 1992 and majority-acquired by Rheinmetall in 2026, has supplied the MV-4 to militaries and demining operators worldwide, including Ukraine.

The MV-10 is DOK-ING's heavy-duty remote-controlled demining and EOD robot, the only system in its class combining a front flail with a rear tiller tool, clearing a 2,450 mm-wide path at up to 4,000 m2/h. It is powered by a 571 kW Caterpillar C18 engine and has been verified in real combat demining operations. DOK-ING is a Croatian unmanned-ground-vehicle manufacturer founded in 1992.

The MVF-5 is DOK-ING's heavy-duty remote-controlled emergency-response robot for fire extinguishing and clearing or pushing debris in extreme conditions too dangerous for human first responders. It carries a 2,500-litre water tank plus a 500-litre foam-concentrate tank and a segmented hydraulic arm with a 2,000 kg lifting capacity, and its dozer blade can push loads of up to 10 tonnes. DOK-ING is a Croatian robotics manufacturer specializing in demining and emergency-response unmanned ground vehicles.

Komodo (MVC8) is DOK-ING's unmanned ground system built to operate in extreme chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) conditions hazardous to human intervention teams, equipped with a CBRN mission module plus a gripper and manipulator arm. Co-financed by the EU's European Structural and Investment Fund as a dual-use civil/defence asset, it has a 17,000 kg gross vehicle weight and a speed limited to 30 km/h. DOK-ING is a Croatian unmanned-ground-vehicle manufacturer.

Vepr is a Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicle built by Partner-VS for front-line logistics resupply, evacuation of up to two casualties, and remote mine clearance. It weighs around 400 kg, carries up to 250 kg of cargo, is driven by two 1,500 W electric motors giving over 50 km of range at speeds above 12 km/h, and communicates over six channels including LTE and Starlink. It has been used on the Ukrainian front line since 2024 and was formally codified by Ukraine's Ministry of Defence in 2026.

NEO is a wheeled, remotely operated ground robot from Ukrainian company Contra-Drone, built as a counter-UAS (C-UAS) platform to protect military positions from hostile drones. It carries a 10-channel electronic-warfare suite with omnidirectional and directional jamming antennas, is primarily controlled over Starlink with 5 km backup radio control, rotates 360 degrees, and rides on mine-blast-resistant tubeless tyres. It can carry up to 300 kg and travel up to 30 km per charge at speeds up to 15 km/h.
