Slon is an interactive helper robot from Sber's Robotics Center that understands spoken commands, moves objects, and can answer questions in conversation. It was unveiled together with the Topa, Kuba and Krab robots at Sber's AI Journey 2024 conference as part of a family of AI-driven assistant robots.

The One 150 is a fixed-wing unmanned aircraft from Czech manufacturer Primoco UAV used for both civilian surveillance (such as border and infrastructure monitoring) and military reconnaissance, including supply to Ukraine for operational use. It has an integrated autopilot for fully automatic takeoff, landing and flight-plan execution, up to 15 hours of endurance, a 30 kg payload, a cruising speed of 100-150 km/h and a service ceiling of 3,300 m. Primoco UAV began serial production of the One 150 in 2016 and is building a new factory in Pisek, Czech Republic, to scale output.

The M40 is a heavy-duty multirotor drone from Hungarian manufacturer ABZ Innovation built for construction and heavy-lifting tasks, with a 40 kg load capacity, about 22 minutes of hovering time, and IP54 weather protection. It runs open-source flight software with ABZ's own battery-management system.

The L10 V2 is an agricultural spray drone from Hungarian manufacturer ABZ Innovation, built on open-source ArduPilot software with Controlled Droplet Application spraying technology that uses up to 80% less water and 50% less pesticide than conventional spraying. It can optionally be fitted with a trichogramma-wasp spreader for biological pest control (an 8-litre tank holding 800-1,200 pellets, treating 8-12 hectares per flight and up to 36 hectares per hour), as well as seed or granule spreaders.

The Bramor ppX is a fixed-wing mapping and surveying drone from Slovenian manufacturer C-Astral, carrying a 42-megapixel RGB camera with GNSS PPK post-processing for precise orthophotos, with under 3 hours of flight time, up to 150 km of range, and about 30 km2 of coverage per flight.

The SQA is a hybrid fixed-wing eVTOL unmanned aircraft from Slovenian manufacturer C-Astral that takes off and lands vertically while cruising like a fixed-wing plane, offering up to 3 hours of flight time and 160 km of range with interchangeable EO, infrared or lidar payloads and a failsafe parachute system.

TX GHOST is an AI-powered shelf-stocking robot developed by Telexistence that operates inside convenience-store walk-in coolers around the clock, restocking roughly 1,800 beverage items per day by analyzing sales data to prioritize best-sellers, with teleoperation as a fallback for edge cases. It is paired with Telexistence's Smart Shelf digital inventory system and follows earlier pilots at 7-Eleven and Lawson stores. Telexistence announced full-scale nationwide rollout across FamilyMart convenience stores starting January 2027.

The Agri Robo Tractor M5 is Kubota's autonomous farm tractor based on the 100hp M5002 diesel tractor platform, fitted with a continuously variable transmission, GPS guidance, cameras and obstacle-detection sensors. It supports four operating modes - manual driving, remote control, fully autonomous operation, and a master-slave mode letting one operator supervise multiple driverless units in the field - and extends Kubota's AgriRobo line of unmanned tractors first sold commercially in Japan from 2017. It was shown with a hoe attachment for orchard and vegetable growers at Agritechnica 2023 and remained Japan-only as of that date.
driveMode: Manual, remote control, fully autonomous, and master-slave (one operator supervising multiple units)

description: Honda Avatar Robot is a teleoperated dual-arm robot developed by Honda as part of its post-ASIMO robotics portfolio, using technology derived from Honda's bipedal-robot hand and arm research to let a remote operator perform dexterous tasks such as opening a canned drink. Honda has shown it publicly since 2021, including at the 2022 International Robot Exhibition, as a platform for remote physical work rather than a commercial product with a fixed release date.

Raicho 2 (雷鳥²号) is an electric, multi-function agricultural robot from tmsuk's WORKROID rice-farming lineup, built with a bird-like body styled after the Thunderbird 2 rescue vehicle and designed to swap attachments for tilling and harvesting work in paddy fields. It was developed as part of tmsuk's push to use swarms of small farm robots to offset Japan's agricultural labor shortage, and was unveiled in December 2023.

Raicho 1 (雷鳥¹号) is tmsuk's small bird-shaped agricultural robot built for Japanese rice paddies as part of the WORKROID farm-robot lineup, sold in a weed-suppression model and, from April 2024, a seeding-capable model, both designed to work in coordinated groups across a field. It was field-tested suppressing weeds in paddies in Shimane Prefecture in 2024 as part of tmsuk's swarm-robotics approach to easing Japan's farm labor shortage.

Inchworm is a space-walking robot developed by the Japanese space-robotics company GITAI, built to crawl along a spacecraft's exterior using its own gripping end-effectors to perform maintenance, assembly and inspection tasks in place of human astronaut spacewalks. A technology-demonstration unit was mounted on a commercial module of the International Space Station, where GITAI conducted multiple external operations in 2024, part of the company's broader plan to automate construction and maintenance of satellites, lunar bases and future Mars settlements.

Muscle Suit Every is a lightweight, 3.8 kg wearable exoskeleton from Innophys that uses pneumatic artificial muscles rather than electric motors to reduce the physical burden of lifting, carrying and sustained squatting. It needs no electricity, works in wet conditions, and is marketed for nursing care, manufacturing, distribution, construction, agriculture, domestic chores, gardening and snow removal at a retail price of 136,000 JPY. It launched in Japan on November 1, 2019 and in February 2020 became the first pneumatic-muscle exoskeleton certified to the ISO 13482 personal-care-robot safety standard.

The PW200R is a ride-on, fully automatic vegetable transplanter from Yanmar Agribusiness fitted with a straight-line steering assist function that keeps planting rows accurate and reduces operator workload and transplant loss. Yanmar released the PW200R series in March 2025, and it has since been adopted by Japanese vegetable growers moving away from conventional manual transplanting toward smart-agriculture workflows.

Aigamo Robo 2 (model IGAM2) is a solar-powered floating robot from Iseki that autonomously patrols flooded rice paddies and stirs up the water to block sunlight, suppressing weed germination without herbicides, following the same principle as traditional Aigamo duck-assisted rice farming. It weighs 6 kg, measures 900 x 810 x 253 mm, is built from expanded polypropylene with a lithium iron phosphate battery, learns the field's shape from GPS and bump data to cover it automatically, and is controlled via a smartphone app that sets run schedules, no-entry zones and reports battery level; it retails for 275,000 JPY.

Sanae Japan PRJ8-R (model PRJ8DR) is Iseki's 8-row autonomous rice-transplanting robot, built on patented technology from Japan's National Agriculture and Food Research Organization (NARO). An operator first plants three edges of the paddy manually so the machine learns the field's shape, after which it automatically plants the field in reciprocating passes and an inner loop, decelerating and stopping itself near the paddy banks, with a color remote control usable up to about 300 m away, auto differential lock and forced four-wheel drive for traction. Iseki markets it to ease rice-planting labor shortages and let less-experienced operators plant with expert-level precision.

RakuRo is a single-seat, walking-speed autonomous personal mobility robot from ZMP (now marketed by its ROBO-HI unit) that drives itself to an app-selected destination on public sidewalks, steering with its two front wheels and using a front LED 'face' panel to signal its intentions to pedestrians. It runs about 4 hours per 1-hour charge, is certified by Japan's Robot Delivery Association for sidewalk operation, and supports a 'group walk' mode letting one caregiver supervise up to four RakuRo units at once, used for example to take elderly care-home residents on supervised walks and in attraction experiences such as the Night Safari XR ride.

Kachaka Pro is Preferred Robotics' business-oriented autonomous mobile robot (AMR), launched for corporate customers on February 19, 2024 as a distinct product line from the company's home-use Kachaka shelf-carrying robot, and deployed in factories, healthcare facilities, restaurants and offices. It uses Preferred Robotics' own SLAM and navigation technology together with a deep-learning perception model developed with sister company Preferred Networks to choose collision-free routes for transporting goods, and has become the top-selling AMR by unit share in Japan's domestic market.

ugo mini G2 is the next-generation version of Mira Robotics' compact, camera-equipped telepresence robot for remote inspection and security patrol, built with an extending, tilting 4K camera for quiet operation in facilities such as data centers, offices and stations. It succeeds the original ugo mini in Mira Robotics' ugo robot lineup, which also includes the dual-arm ugo Pro and the budget-oriented ugo Ex, all managed through the cloud-based ugo Platform for remote control, no-code automation and reporting. Mira Robotics announced ugo mini G2 in October 2026, with production delegated to Canon Electronics.

size: 1 - 17.5 m wide x 2.0 m tall x 0.7 m deep
description: The Cleveron 302 is a modular indoor smart parcel locker for click-and-collect retail, holding between 15 and 402 parcels depending on configuration. Made by Estonian company Cleveron, it lets shoppers pick up online orders without staff assistance and is deployed by retailers across Europe.

size: 1 - 22 m wide x 2.2 - 2.4 m tall x 1.5 - 3.4 m deep
description: The Cleveron 355 is an outdoor parcel locker built for oversized click-and-collect deliveries such as TVs or furniture, with a capacity of 4 to 193 parcels and a weatherproofed housing rated for extreme temperatures. It is made by Estonian company Cleveron for retailers across Europe.

size: 3.7 - 13.7 m wide x 3.1 - 4.75 m tall x 2.1 m deep
description: The Cleveron 402 is a modular robotic parcel locker that uses an internal robot to store and retrieve up to about 3,400 parcels depending on installation size, and can be installed behind a wall with only a console exposed to customers. Made by Estonian company Cleveron, it won a Bronze 2017 Edison Award and was a 2023 DesignEuropa Awards finalist.

size: 4 m wide x 2 m tall x 1.5 m deep
description: The Cleveron 403 is a fixed-size robotic parcel locker holding roughly 75 to 567 parcels, designed to be installed behind a wall or as a standalone unit with a smaller footprint than earlier Cleveron models. A 2025 software update improved loading time and the internal robot's horizontal and vertical movement speed.

Tom is an autonomous crop-scouting robot built by UK startup Small Robot Company to scan arable fields and build per-plant crop maps for weed and disease detection. The 2022 'Tom V4' update captured images at a 0.28 mm/pixel ground sample distance using 8 x 6-megapixel cameras, weighed 350.6 kg and reached a forward speed of 1.5 m/s; the company ceased trading in February 2024.

Dick is a precision weeding robot from UK startup Small Robot Company that uses an 8,000-volt electrode to kill individual broad-leaved weeds identified by onboard AI from data gathered by its sister robot Tom. It began field trials in October 2021, running on Tesla battery packs, before Small Robot Company ceased trading in February 2024.

Harry is a 1.8-metre-square, spider-shaped digital drilling robot unveiled by UK startup Small Robot Company at the REAP 2018 conference, designed to fold compactly and punch-plant seeds at a uniform depth with minimal soil disturbance while logging each seed's exact location. It remained a prototype, with only its sister robots Tom and Dick reaching field trials, when Small Robot Company ceased trading in February 2024.

The 600 Series is Ocado's newest grid-based fulfilment bot, which travels across the top of its warehouse 'Hive' grids to retrieve totes stacked up to 21 bins deep for order picking. Announced in November 2024, it is built with an 'additive-first' 3D-printing process (with HP, Onshape and nTop) that makes it about three times lighter than its predecessor, enabling lighter, faster-to-install warehouse grids.

Robotti is a diesel-powered, RTK-GPS-guided autonomous field robot from Danish company AgroIntelli, used with standard three-point-hitch farm implements for seeding, weeding and other row-crop tasks. It weighs under 3,000 kg, lifts up to 1,250 kg, can spin on the spot for narrow headland turns, and the long-range version runs roughly 60 hours on a 300-litre diesel tank; distributed across ten European countries including via Kubota before AgroIntelli's 2026 bankruptcy and sale.

Thorvald is a modular, electric autonomous field-robot platform from Norwegian company Saga Robotics, used in strawberry polytunnels and vineyards for tasks such as UV-C fungicide-free powdery-mildew treatment and crop monitoring. Its lightweight design with a swappable Dual-axis Drive module reduces soil compaction versus heavy machinery, and in 2026 it was named to TIME's Best Inventions list.

Falcon is a compact, five-thruster electric observation-class ROV made by Saab Seaeye in Fareham, UK, used for inspection work across oil and gas, renewables, aquaculture and scientific missions. It is 1 metre long, weighs 60 kg in air, carries a 14 kg payload, and is rated to a 300 m depth (1000 m in its Falcon-DR variant).

Panther-XT Plus is a heavy work-class electric ROV from Saab Seaeye in Fareham, UK, built for drill support, pipeline survey, inspection/repair/maintenance (IRM) and salvage work. It runs ten thrusters for 3.5-knot speeds, can mount two Schilling manipulator arms, weighs 800 kg in air with a 150 kg payload, and is rated to an 800 m depth.

The Einride Pod (originally the T-pod) is a cabless autonomous electric freight truck from Swedish company Einride, first revealed in 2017 and combining self-driving software with remote human teleoperation for difficult situations. It has about 200 km of range per charge and has hauled freight on public roads for customers including DB Schenker, Lidl, GE Appliances and Maersk.

The Eelume S3 is a small, portable autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) from Norwegian company Eelume, built for rapid deployment and agile operations in defense, infrastructure-inspection and mine-countermeasure missions. It is rated to 300 m or 600 m depth, runs up to 11 hours or 62 km per mission, and carries sonar and 4K still-camera payloads.

The Eelume S6 is a medium-class autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) from Norwegian company Eelume, built for maximized data quality, advanced navigation and multi-day mission endurance. It is rated to 600 m depth and carries Synthetic Aperture Sonar plus a 4K still camera for defense, security and underwater infrastructure inspection.

Rooster is a hybrid ground/air robot made by Israeli company Robotican that rolls like a wheeled robot and flies like a drone, designed for indoor and underground ISR (intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance) and search-and-rescue missions in tunnels, caves and buildings. It weighs 1.62 kg, carries up to 300 g of payload, streams day/low-light/NIR video, uses a self-healing mesh radio link between units for communication-denied environments, and has been fielded by the Israeli military and other security forces.

Bennu is a multipurpose mobile robotic platform developed in-house by Egrobots, an Egyptian deep-technology company with operations in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Built by Egyptian engineers as, according to the company, the Arab world's first autonomous agricultural harvesting robot, it uses computer vision and autonomous navigation with up to four robotic arms to identify ripe crops and harvest them at about 160 kg/hour; its first deployment is tomato harvesting inside a commercial greenhouse for Saudi operator Mahasil, and the same platform has also been demonstrated for street traffic-violation monitoring in Egypt.

Duma is a modular, mass-producible tracked unmanned ground vehicle built by Nigerian autonomous-systems company Terra Industries (formerly Terrahaptix) for ground surveillance, site protection and cargo operations at mines, oil and gas pipelines, farmland and defense sites across Africa. It runs on Terra's ArtemisOS to autonomously handle mission planning and threat detection, weighs 350 kg, carries up to 600 kg of payload, reaches 45 km/h, and operates continuously for at least 24 hours with an AES-256 encrypted control link over a 10 km range.

Ironhide Forklift is an autonomous forklift made by Key Intelligent Technology (KIT), a robotics startup incubated at Technopark Casablanca, Morocco. It uses laser SLAM navigation to lift and position loads of up to two tonnes with millimetric precision for industrial and logistics customers.

Fly Boat is an autonomous mobile robot (AGV/AMR) made by Key Intelligent Technology (KIT), a robotics startup incubated at Technopark Casablanca, Morocco, for material handling in factories and warehouses. It carries up to 300 kg of payload and runs for about ten hours per charge. KIT, founded in late 2023, completed fifteen projects in 2025 and built international partnerships across Asia, Europe and the United States.

RASID is a jet-ski-style unmanned surface vessel (USV) developed in Qatar by Barzan Holdings for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) missions, supporting maritime surveillance and information-gathering without an onboard crew. It was shown among 12 new locally developed security and defense products at Milipol Qatar 2026 in Doha.

ISR VTOL-400 is a vertical take-off and landing drone made by Qatari company Barzan Holdings for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions. It carries up to 4 kg of payload, has a datalink range of about 40 km, flies up to 10,000 ft altitude and reaches speeds of up to 110 km/h.

Solix X1 is the solar-electric entry in Solinftec's expanded Solix autonomous agricultural robot lineup, which spans four power configurations (solar-electric, battery-electric, diesel-hybrid and hybrid-electric) with tank capacities from 50 to 1,200 gallons for spraying and crop scouting. Solinftec, a Brazilian agtech founded in Araçatuba, announced the expanded model range in 2026 to let farms match machine size and power source to their operation.

Solix XT is the battery-electric variant in Solinftec's expanded Solix autonomous agricultural robot lineup, alongside solar-electric, diesel-hybrid and hybrid-electric siblings covering 50 to 1,200 gallon tank capacities for autonomous spraying and field scouting. Solinftec, a Brazilian agtech, announced the expanded lineup in 2026 so farms can pick the power source that fits their operation.

Solix XR is a diesel-hybrid variant in Solinftec's expanded Solix autonomous agricultural robot lineup, using a diesel engine for propulsion and to charge onboard batteries, aimed at larger farm operations in regions such as Canada and Texas. The XR prototype completed field testing in 2026, with broader commercial deployment planned for the 2027 growing season by Solinftec, a Brazilian agtech.

Solix XC is the hybrid-electric variant in Solinftec's expanded Solix autonomous agricultural robot lineup, which spans solar-electric, battery-electric, diesel-hybrid and hybrid-electric configurations with 50 to 1,200 gallon tank capacities for autonomous spraying and scouting. Solinftec, a Brazilian agtech, announced the expanded model range in 2026 to match machine power source to farm size.

IRBin is an AI-powered interactive recycling kiosk robot made by Peruvian startup Cirsys that accepts PET plastic bottles up to 2.5 liters and stores up to 400 bottles for sorting. Two units operate around the clock at Lima's Jorge Chavez International Airport, engaging passengers with raffle incentives as part of the airport's waste-reduction program. Deployed in 2026.

Vantage is an autonomous underwater vehicle built by Pelagos, a Waterloo, Ontario startup founded by Carleton University graduates Samuel Scrivens and Shrey Naphade, aimed at port security, underwater infrastructure inspection and marine biodiversity monitoring. Designed to be backpack-portable and rapidly deployable, the saltwater-tested prototype has completed about an hour of untethered autonomous operation, with underwater docking and recharging still in development. Pelagos secured its first commercial customer, US ocean-technology firm Tekmara, in 2026.

Keeogo is a powered leg-brace exoskeleton ("Dermoskeleton") made by B-Temia of Quebec, Canada, that adds motorized support at the knee joints to help users with stroke recovery, spinal cord injury, Parkinson's disease and general leg weakness walk and stand. It is used both in clinical rehabilitation settings and for daily personal mobility, and is approved for sale and rental in Canada.

Maize Runner is a solar-powered autonomous robot from Waterloo, Ontario startup Upside Robotics that applies precisely dosed liquid fertilizer between 30-inch corn rows, using onboard sensors to time applications and cut nitrogen use by up to 70%. It is 22 inches wide, carries a 50-liter tank, runs about 10 hours per charge with a 60-minute solar recharge at its base station, and covers roughly 1 acre per hour. The company announced a $7.5 million seed round in February 2026 and was operating across about 3,000 corn acres in Ontario, Canada.

The SG-12 is an ultra-low-profile autonomous robot from Chilean mining-robotics startup Smart Plus Robotics that navigates beneath active conveyor belts to continuously extract spilled heavy material, recovering 6.7 tons of ore per day per robot without requiring a plant shutdown. It has been trialed in underground copper mine infrastructure in Chile, including Codelco operations, and reduces worker exposure to hazardous areas.

SG-SCAN is a heavy-duty electric 4x4 autonomous robot in development by Chilean startup Smart Plus Robotics for data collection and preventive maintenance analysis in underground mining environments where GPS and Wi-Fi signals are denied. It is designed to operate alongside the company's SG-12 ore-recovery robot in Andean copper mines.

Milano ISR is the observation branch of Milano's modular VTOL fixed-wing drone platform, designed and built in Buenos Aires, Argentina, adding a stabilized EO/IR (visible and thermal) payload for security, infrastructure-monitoring and emergency-support missions; Milano's own site states this ISR configuration is still under development and integration. The shared airframe takes off and lands vertically on three rotors before transitioning to fixed-wing cruise, with 2026-prototype target specs of 85-minute endurance, 6 kg MTOW, 65 km/h cruise speed and a 2.5 m wingspan. Milano (Milano.Aero), founded in Argentina in 2009, publicly presented the platform at the 2026 Congreso Internacional de Drones.

The Explorer AUV is a modular autonomous underwater vehicle from International Submarine Engineering (ISE) of Port Coquitlam, BC, available in 1,000 m, 3,000 m and 6,000 m depth-rated versions with a swappable payload bay for side-scan sonar, multibeam echosounders, sub-bottom profilers, CTD instruments, cameras and chemical sensors. It is used for hydrographic surveying, pipeline and cable inspection, environmental monitoring and long-range under-ice Arctic surveys, with high-precision terrain-following navigation.

Theseus is an autonomous underwater vehicle built by International Submarine Engineering (ISE) of Port Coquitlam, BC, best known for the Canada-US Spinnaker project in which it laid multiple 220 km fibre-optic cables beneath a 2.5 m thick Arctic ice pack in water up to 600 m deep, completing over 60 hours of continuous under-ice operation. Owned by Canada's Department of National Defence and maintained by ISE, it has a configurable pressure hull, modular payload bay and variable ballast system, and remains available for charter for research, technology demonstration and subsea operations.

Dorado is a semi-submersible unmanned vehicle from International Submarine Engineering (ISE) that tows a sonar towfish for seabed imaging while running at up to 12 knots and operating to 200 m depth, with a surface-piercing mast providing continuous radio and differential GPS links up to 10 km from its host vessel. Its low-drag semi-submersible hull gives it steadier performance than surface drones in rough seas, for mine-countermeasure surveys, seismic surveys and marine science operations.

HYSUB is a work-class remotely operated vehicle (ROV) line from International Submarine Engineering (ISE), depth-rated to 6,000 m and built on a modular, configurable subsea platform with electro-hydraulic actuation for scientific, commercial and subsea-construction missions. It supports a wide range of mission payloads and comes with proprietary control software, operator training and lifecycle support.

DataXplorer Enviro is a solar-powered, self-righting uncrewed surface vessel from Victoria, BC's Open Ocean Robotics, built for long-endurance ocean environmental monitoring in water as shallow as 0.5 m. It carries modular sensor payloads such as weather stations, CTD and ADCP water-quality instruments, thermal cameras, eDNA samplers and AIS/satellite communications, with onboard battery capacity configurable from 3.5 to 17.5 kWh. It is part of Open Ocean Robotics' DataXplorer line, which also includes Protect, Listen, Survey and METOC mission variants of the same solar USV platform.

KATFISH is an actively stabilized, towed synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) towfish from Kraken Robotics of St. John's, Newfoundland, that can be towed at up to 10 knots for high-speed, high-resolution underwater imaging and simultaneous bathymetric mapping. It is used for seabed survey, mine-countermeasure and offshore-infrastructure inspection missions, integrating with unmanned surface and underwater vehicles.

Tenniix is a portable AI tennis-ball machine shown at CES 2026 with a 4K+1080p dual-camera vision system that tracks the player and adapts each serve's speed, spin, placement and tempo in real time. It offers voice control, app control, over 1,000 built-in drills and OTA software updates.

Tenniix S is a model in Tenniix's AI tennis-ball-machine lineup, sharing the brand's dual-camera vision tracking, voice and app control and adaptive serve generation (speed, spin, placement, tempo) with over 1,000 drills.

TransCar is an autonomous guided vehicle made by Singapore's OTSAW Digital for intra-logistics material transport in hospitals and healthcare facilities, carrying up to 500 kg of trolleys via a lifting mechanism to reduce floor contact. It is offered under a Robot-as-a-Service model and has been deployed at Singapore hospitals including Singapore General Hospital and KK Women's and Children's Hospital.

Camello+ is OTSAW's autonomous multi-purpose mobile robot for combined delivery and security-patrol applications, successor to the earlier Camello delivery robot. It carries lockable, swappable compartments accessed by RFID or QR code, and uses an upgraded LiDAR and sensor suite for 360-degree obstacle detection indoors and outdoors.

O-R3 is OTSAW's autonomous outdoor surveillance robot that patrols streets, pathways and open spaces using patented 3D SLAM navigation, avoiding obstacles and returning to base to recharge. It streams HD video and 360-degree computer-vision sensor data for real-time security monitoring and anomaly alerts.

Hadrian X is FBR's truck-mounted construction robot that autonomously lays concrete blocks to build a house's structural walls, using Dynamic Stabilisation Technology to cancel vibration on its 32 m telescopic boom. It lays up to 360 blocks per hour and can complete a standard double-brick house's internal and external walls in a single day, operated by a two-person crew.

SwarmBot 5 is SwarmFarm Robotics' autonomous, driverless field robot for broadacre crop spraying, carrying an 18-27 m boom with WEED-IT optical spot-spray cameras to selectively apply herbicide and reduce chemical use. It runs at up to 9.5 km/h with a 3,000-litre tank, covering roughly 13 hectares per hour and 100-200 hectares per day, and has racked up thousands of operating hours on Australian farms.

Hydrus is Advanced Navigation's micro hovering autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) for affordable underwater surveying and inspection. It integrates DVL, USBL, an inertial navigation system and acoustic/optical modems with a 4K 60fps camera and sonar for fully autonomous subsea missions, obstacle avoidance and 3D point-cloud mapping, and has been used for shipwreck and reef surveys in Australian waters.

Prospr is Robotics Plus's autonomous, multi-use hybrid ground vehicle for orchard and vineyard tasks such as spraying, using an all-electric drive system backed by a Tier 4 diesel generator for extended range. It has independent wheel motors for all-wheel drive and a 7.1 m turning radius for working rows as narrow as 1.85 m, and became commercially available in 2023 with swappable Q4/Q6/Q8 sprayer attachments; the company was acquired by Yamaha Motor in 2025 to form Yamaha Agriculture.

Mobile Log Scaler is a robotic measurement system by New Zealand's Robotics Plus that automatically scales (measures and grades) logs at timber ports, replacing slow and hazardous manual log-scaling work. It is offered as either a fixed installation or a mobile unit and was introduced at New Zealand ports as a world-first automated log-scaling solution.
throughput: up to 20 trucks per hour

description: Taurus is ST Engineering's electric, remote-operated four-wheel-drive unmanned ground vehicle for surveillance, casualty evacuation, logistics transport and material handling, unveiled at Singapore Airshow 2024. It weighs about 1,600 kg, runs roughly 19 miles (30 km) per charge in full-electric mode, and can carry ST Engineering's DrN-15 multirotor drone for beyond-visual-line-of-sight surveillance missions.

Dolphin1 is ZBHA's portable, throwable AI water-rescue robot that autonomously detects drowning victims via connected CCTV and sensor feeds and launches to reach them without waiting for an operator command. It reaches up to 7 m/s and can carry loads up to 1,000 kg, and was piloted with Thai security firm Super Guard at Phuket's Cherng Talay police station in 2026.

Dolphin3 is ZBHA's water-rescue robot variant that connects to the company's full AI monitoring platform for networked, autonomous drowning detection and response, as a counterpart to the portable, stand-alone Dolphin1. It reaches up to 7 m/s and can carry loads up to 1,000 kg, and was piloted with Thai security firm Super Guard at Phuket's Cherng Talay police station in 2026.

Dinsaw Pro4 OPD is a hospital outpatient-department kiosk robot from Thailand's CT Asia Robotics, used in hundreds of Thai hospitals to check NHSO insurance coverage and appointments, take AI-assisted symptom histories by touchscreen and voice, record vital signs from connected devices, and route patients to the right clinic. The company says it supports more than 80% of outpatient registration and screening workload, integrating with hospital information systems.

SwagBot is a four-wheeled, battery-powered autonomous robot developed by the University of Sydney's Australian Centre for Field Robotics (led by Professor Salah Sukkarieh) to herd and monitor cattle without fences. It assesses pasture health and density, tracks livestock condition, and moves animals toward better grazing areas to prevent overgrazing and soil degradation on rugged terrain; first demonstrated in 2016, it remains a research platform under continued development.

Ohmio LIFT is a high-capacity, modular autonomous electric shuttle bus from New Zealand's Ohmio Automation, designed for zero-emission passenger transport at airports, university campuses and smart-city precincts. It uses LiDAR, cameras and AI-based obstacle detection for self-driving and route-learning operation, with step-free low-floor boarding and wheelchair accessibility, and has been deployed at sites including JFK and Amsterdam Schiphol airports.

Phenikaa-X's autonomous shuttle bus is a Vietnamese-developed SAE Level 4 self-driving minibus that carries up to 5 passengers on fixed short routes in campuses, tech parks and urban districts. It measures 3.2 x 1.7 x 2.4 m, runs a 38.64 kWh battery for about 6-hour charging, reaches a maximum 20 km/h, and navigates using LiDAR, camera and radar with GPS/IMU/3D-map localization and 5G teleoperation support; first unveiled in March 2021, it has been trialed at Ecopark and Binh Duong before a 2026 Hanoi sandbox program.

MooBus is Singapore developer MooVita's autonomous passenger shuttle, intended as a green first- and last-mile transport solution for cities, built on the company's modular autonomous-vehicle driving stack. It has been under road testing in Singapore since 2021 and was proposed by ride-hailing operator Ryde and MooVita for a driverless shuttle service in Punggol.

V1800 is Invert Robotics' vacuum-adhesion climbing inspection robot for non-ferrous and non-magnetic industrial surfaces such as stainless-steel tanks, reactors and food/beverage vessels. It is remotely operated, is portable enough for air freight, and can be set up inside an asset in under 30 minutes, carrying NDT payloads such as a 30x-zoom remote visual inspection camera to detect defects without confined-space entry.

RangerBot is a briefcase-sized autonomous underwater robot developed by Queensland University of Technology to protect the Great Barrier Reef by detecting and injecting poison into coral-eating crown-of-thorns starfish. It uses an onboard computer-vision system for underwater navigation and obstacle avoidance, identifies the starfish with about 99.4% accuracy, builds 3D reef-health maps, and can operate underwater far longer than human divers.

LarvalBot is an underwater coral-restoration robot adapted by QUT's Matthew Dunbabin from the RangerBot reef-protection platform, designed to gently disperse coral larvae onto damaged Great Barrier Reef areas so they settle and grow into new coral. Each unit can carry roughly 200,000 to 1.2 million larvae and cover about 1,500 square metres of reef per hour on a preset underwater path, operating semi-autonomously with remote-triggered release; it was completed and first deployed in November 2018 to coincide with the reef's annual coral spawning.

ARTEV1000 is Jevons Robotics' battery-electric, 1-tonne modular mining robot that automates pre-split explosives loading on highwalls, autonomously locating and aligning blast holes while being remotely operated from a control room so personnel no longer need to enter hazardous blasting areas. The modular platform can also be reconfigured for hole-dipping and blast-hole quality assurance, and was first deployed globally at Newmont's Boddington mine in Australia.

CORI is a compact, handheld image-free robotics-assisted surgery platform made by Smith+Nephew for partial and total knee and shoulder arthroplasty. Instead of a large robotic arm, it uses a hand-held robotic sculpting tool with real-time 3D surface mapping and haptic boundaries. The next-generation CORI XT platform, which extends the system to additional joint procedures, began its first clinical cases in 2026.

hinotori is Japan's first domestically developed robotic-assisted surgery system, built by Medicaroid, a joint venture of Kawasaki Heavy Industries and Sysmex. It is a teleoperated multi-arm platform used for laparoscopic urological, gynecological and general surgery and received CE marking for the European market in 2026.

Revo-i is South Korea's first domestically developed robotic-assisted surgical system, made by Meerecompany and approved by Korea's MFDS in 2017 for laparoscopic procedures. It has surpassed 500 cancer surgeries at a single institution and has been exported to markets including Paraguay.

LUNA was Asensus Surgical's next-generation digital laparoscopic surgery platform, unveiled in 2023 as a smaller, modular successor to the company's Senhance system. After Karl Storz completed its acquisition of Asensus in 2024, Karl Storz announced in June 2026 that it would fully integrate Asensus and discontinue both the Senhance and LUNA robots, laying off over 100 employees.

The SSi Mantra 3 is a multi-arm, teleoperated surgical robot made by SS Innovations International for minimally invasive general, urological and cardiac procedures. It has been used in thousands of surgeries in India, including the first robotic beating-heart bypass surgery and the world's longest-distance robotic telesurgery, and the company has submitted the system to the FDA for US clearance.

The EndoQuest Flexible Robotic Surgical System (also marketed as the Endoluminal Surgical System) is a flexible, teleoperated robotic endoscopy platform made by Houston-based EndoQuest Robotics for natural-orifice and single-incision procedures such as endoscopic submucosal dissection, using instruments with up to 7 degrees of freedom. It remains an investigational device under FDA review, not yet FDA-cleared, and is being evaluated in the multi-site PARADIGM clinical trial, including completed procedures at Mayo Clinic and Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center.

JASPER is a robotic-assisted surgery platform developed by ForSight Robotics for cataract surgery, designed to combine microsurgical precision with AI-based guidance. The company raised $125M in 2025 to trial the system and announced the first robot-assisted human cataract surgery with the JASPER platform in 2026.

Epione is a robotic platform made by French company Quantum Surgical for image-guided percutaneous ablation of liver, kidney and lung tumors. It combines CT-based planning software with a robotic arm for needle placement and made its first US surgical robot sale in 2023.

neuromate is a stereotactic surgical robot made by UK-based Renishaw for neurosurgical procedures such as deep brain stimulation electrode placement, stereo-EEG and biopsies. It is one of the longest-serving commercial neurosurgical robots still in clinical use at hospitals internationally.

NaoTrac is a surgical navigation robot made by Taiwan's Brain Navi Biotechnology for frameless, image-guided neurosurgical procedures such as biopsies and electrode placement. It received FDA approval in 2025 and is marketed in Europe and the US as an alternative to traditional stereotactic frames.

ROSA Brain is a robotic guidance system made by Zimmer Biomet for stereotactic neurosurgical procedures including biopsies, electrode and catheter placement, and epilepsy surgery planning. It is part of Zimmer Biomet's ROSA robotics family alongside ROSA Knee, and has been in clinical use for over a decade.

The PRECEYES Surgical System is a robotic micromanipulator made by Dutch company Preceyes B.V. (acquired by Carl Zeiss Meditec in 2022) for high-precision vitreoretinal eye surgery, filtering out hand tremor to achieve under 20 micrometers of positioning precision with 4 degrees of freedom. It was the first market-cleared (CE marked) robot for retina surgery, used in the world's first robot-assisted retinal surgeries, and continues to be studied clinically, including first-in-human robotic subretinal drug delivery.

The Flex Robotic System was a flexible, snake-like surgical robot made by Medrobotics for transoral and transanal minimally invasive procedures, FDA-cleared in 2015. The company put its surgical robotics intellectual property up for sale in 2024, ending commercial support for the platform.

The Magellan Robotic System was a teleoperated robotic catheter platform made by Hansen Medical for endovascular and peripheral vascular interventions. Hansen Medical was acquired by Auris Health in 2016 (later J&J MedTech), after which the Magellan system was discontinued in favor of newer platforms.

Pulse is an all-in-one spine surgery platform, originally launched by NuVasive and now marketed by Globus Medical following the companies' 2023 merger, integrating imaging, navigation, neuromonitoring and robotics-assisted instrument guidance into a single system for spine procedures. It received FDA clearance and CE mark in 2021 and has been rolled out globally.

CUVIS-joint is an open-platform orthopedic surgical robot made by South Korea's Curexo for total knee, unicompartmental knee and total hip arthroplasty. It supports a range of third-party implants and features navigation-based active bone cutting with real-time gap checking; Curexo supplied dozens of these systems worldwide in recent years and entered Japan's joint-surgery robot market with Kyocera.

CUVIS-spine is an open-platform, navigation-based robotic system made by Curexo for spine surgery, including treatment of lumbar disc disease and spinal stenosis. It supports diverse implant systems and uses 2D-3D registration for pedicle screw placement guidance.

MORNINGWALK is a robotic gait-rehabilitation device made by Curexo that combines a motorized lower-limb trainer with VR software and bio-signal monitoring to provide personalized, real-time-feedback therapy for patients recovering from stroke or orthopedic surgery.

ORTHBOT is a spine-surgery robot developed by Shenzhen-based Xeek (Xinjunte Intelligent Medical Device) for pedicle-screw placement guidance in orthopedic procedures. The company, which raised a multi-hundred-million-yuan Series B in 2021, became the first Chinese firm to obtain EU market access for a domestically developed spine surgery robot in 2023.

Amadeo is a robotic hand-rehabilitation device made by Austrian company Tyromotion that provides individual finger actuation and sensory training for patients recovering hand function after stroke or injury. It is used in clinical rehabilitation settings and has been studied in peer-reviewed clinical research.

Trexo Theo is a pediatric robotic lower-limb exoskeleton made by Canadian company Trexo Robotics, designed to help children with cerebral palsy and other mobility impairments practice walking. It received FDA clearance and launched in 2026 as the first pediatric robotic exoskeleton cleared for home use.

ReStore is a soft, powered lower-limb exosuit made by Lifeward (formerly ReWalk Robotics), developed with Harvard's Wyss Institute, for gait rehabilitation after stroke. Unlike the rigid ReWalk exoskeleton, it uses lightweight cable-driven actuation at the ankle, and clinical studies have shown it improves walking ability versus traditional therapy alone.

The ABLE Exoskeleton is a robotic lower-limb exoskeleton made by Barcelona-based Able Human Motion for people with spinal cord injury and other mobility impairments, enabling independent standing and walking in clinical and home settings. It has been clinically validated in neurorehabilitation hospitals in Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and Spain, with results published in peer-reviewed journals.

ExoAtlet II is a medical rehabilitation exoskeleton made by ExoAtlet for clinical use, helping patients with spinal cord injury, stroke or other neurological conditions stand and walk under therapist supervision. ExoAtlet's parent, Cosmo Robotics, completed an IPO and began trading on South Korea's KOSDAQ exchange in 2026.

Erigo is a robotic tilt-table system made by Swiss company Hocoma that combines verticalization with automated cyclical leg movement, used for early mobilization and circulatory training of patients in intensive care and early neurorehabilitation who cannot yet stand on their own.

The X-ble Shoulder is a wearable powered exoskeleton developed by Hyundai Motor Group to reduce shoulder and arm strain for workers performing overhead tasks in automotive manufacturing and other industries. Hyundai has been expanding its wearable-robot lineup for sale to industrial customers.

The X-ble Knee is a wearable powered lower-limb exoskeleton developed by Hyundai Motor Group to reduce knee and back strain for workers in physically demanding roles such as sanitation work. A Seoul district government deployed the suits to its sanitation workers in 2025.

Laevo FLEX is a passive back-support exoskeleton made by Dutch company Laevo for industrial and logistics workers who perform repeated bending and lifting. The FLEX 3.0 generation became the first exoskeleton to be certified as personal protective equipment under the EU PPE CE mark.

The IX Back Volton is a powered back-support exoskeleton launched in 2025 under Ottobock's SUITX brand (formed after Ottobock's 2021 acquisition of US Bionics/suitX), marketed as one of the lightest motorized back exoskeletons for industrial ergonomics.

SafeLift is a soft, powered back-support exosuit made by Harvard spinout Verve Motion to reduce lifting injuries for warehouse and logistics workers. The company raised $20M in 2023 to scale production of the wearable robotics system.

EXO-S is a passive shoulder-support exoskeleton made by Hilti for construction workers performing overhead tasks such as drilling and installing ceiling fixtures, reducing shoulder and arm fatigue. Hilti released an improved version of the exoskeleton in 2023.

WalkON Suit F1 is a powered lower-limb exoskeleton made by South Korea's Angel Robotics for people with complete paraplegia, featuring a front-loading, self-donning design and autonomous balance control that lets users walk without crutches. A pilot wearing the suit won the exoskeleton race at the 2024 Cybathlon.

HSR (Human Support Robot) is a mobile-manipulator assistance robot developed by Toyota to help people with limited mobility, including elderly and disabled users, with everyday tasks such as picking up and fetching objects. It is used both as a home-care assistance platform and as an open research platform at universities worldwide.

Robear is a bear-shaped nursing-care robot developed by Japan's RIKEN research institute, designed to lift and transfer elderly patients between a bed and a wheelchair using soft, force-sensing arms. It was unveiled as a named prototype to demonstrate safe human-robot physical interaction for Japan's aging-care workforce.

WIM is a lightweight, hip-worn walking-assist exosuit made by South Korea's WIRobotics, designed to support mobility for elderly users and people recovering from injury during everyday walking. It was shown publicly at CES 2026 and the company has partnered with Ottobock to expand distribution of its wearable robots across North America.

Resyone Plus is a transforming care robot made by Panasonic that splits apart to convert between an electric care bed and a powered wheelchair, letting caregivers move bedridden or elderly patients without manually lifting them. It is deployed in Japanese nursing-care facilities to reduce caregiver physical strain.

Enos (formerly developed as the SPORT Surgical System) was a single-port, teleoperated robotic surgery platform developed by Canadian company Titan Medical for minimally invasive laparoscopic procedures, featuring miniaturized dual articulating instruments and a 3D camera through one incision. The company built and showed next-generation prototypes but never achieved FDA clearance or commercial sales before winding down.

The Vicarious Surgical System was a single-port robotic surgery platform developed by Massachusetts-based Vicarious Surgical, using miniaturized, human-like dual robotic arms delivered through one incision and controlled via a virtual-reality surgeon console. After repeated delays in its FDA submission, the company's board voted in 2026 to wind down operations before the system reached commercial sale.

FIFISH V-EVO is an underwater ROV made by QYSEA with a 4K/60fps camera, 166-degree field of view and 360-degree omnidirectional thrusters. It is rated to 100 m depth with up to 4 hours of dive time and AI Vision Lock tracking for divers and marine subjects.

FIFISH E-GO is a modular industrial underwater ROV from QYSEA rated to 100 m depth (200 m optional) with a six-thruster vector layout, hot-swappable dual batteries and up to six accessory mounting ports for inspection and survey payloads.

CHASING M2 S is a compact industrial-grade underwater ROV with a butterfly-wing hull, eight-thruster omnidirectional layout, a 4K camera and a 100 m depth rating. It launched in 2023 as a single-person-deployable inspection drone.

EVO Max 4T is an enterprise inspection and public-safety drone from Autel Robotics carrying wide, zoom, thermal and laser-rangefinder cameras with 720-degree obstacle detection. It supports coordinated multi-drone operation via Autel A-Mesh and is IP43 rated for light rain.

Matternet M3 is the next-generation autonomous delivery drone from Matternet, unveiled in 2026 for BVLOS medical and retail delivery from rooftop micro-hubs. It carries up to 5 kg over a 16 km service radius at a 72 km/h cruise speed and completes four or more deliveries per hour.

Manna 2 is the current all-electric delivery drone operated by Irish drone-delivery company Manna, used for fast food, grocery and pharmacy deliveries across Ireland, the UK and (from 2026) the United States.

DJI Dock 3 is an automated drone-in-a-box hangar that houses and recharges a compatible Matrice drone for unattended, remote-piloted BVLOS inspection and public-safety missions, with weatherproofing for 24/7 field deployment.

DJI Dock 4 is DJI's drone-in-a-box hangar launched in 2026 with automatic battery swapping in 25 seconds for continuous 24/7 operation, paired with the Matrice 5TD drone carrying wide-angle and infrared cameras, mmWave radar and LiDAR.

Hull Skater is a magnetic-wheeled, remotely operated hull-grooming robot developed by Jotun with Kongsberg that drives over a docked ship's underwater hull to remove biofilm with a motorized brush, documenting fouling via onboard cameras without drydocking.

XOcean X-16 is a 4.5 m wave-piercing catamaran uncrewed surface vessel used for bathymetric surveys, environmental monitoring and fisheries enforcement. It runs on a hybrid battery-diesel-solar system, cruises at 4 knots and can stay on mission for up to 18 days with satellite-linked remote piloting.

DriX H-8 is a 7.7 m hydrographic uncrewed surface vessel made by Exail (formerly iXblue), the first USV certified by both Bureau Veritas and Lloyd's Register. It carries a 38 hp diesel engine for up to 10 days of autonomous survey endurance at 14-knot top speed.

DataXplorer is a solar-powered, self-righting uncrewed surface vehicle from Open Ocean Robotics used for hydrographic survey, habitat mapping, maritime security and environmental monitoring, capable of multi-day zero-emission missions with mission-specific sensor payloads (Survey, Enviro, Listen, METOC, Protect).

BIKI is a bio-inspired, fish-shaped underwater drone made by Robosea with a 4K camera, obstacle avoidance and return-to-base functionality, rated to 60 m depth. It launched via Kickstarter in 2017 as one of the first consumer tailed-swimming underwater drones.

Hullbot is an autonomous underwater robot from the Australian startup of the same name that performs frequent, on-demand hull cleaning and inspection for boats and ships, removing biofouling without drydocking and navigating niche areas such as propellers.

EverClean is a hull-cleaning and in-water inspection robot from Greensea IQ (formerly Armach Robotics), built on the company's underwater autonomy technology to provide proactive hull grooming for commercial and cruise vessels.

Astro is an industrial multirotor drone from Freefly Systems carrying payloads up to 35 lbs, including a 61MP interchangeable-lens camera, thermal imaging and laser rangefinder options. It offers 28 minutes of flight time, RTK positioning and LTE cloud connectivity, and is NDAA-compliant and Blue UAS listed.

eBee X is a fixed-wing mapping drone from AgEagle (via its senseFly line) built for infrastructure inspection and large-area surveying. It is hand-launched, flies up to 90 minutes per battery, covers up to 500 hectares per flight and achieves 1.5 cm absolute accuracy with RTK/PPK.

UX11 is a hand-launched, fixed-wing inspection drone from Toulouse-based Delair, deployable in under five minutes for linear infrastructure, safety and topography missions. In 2023 it became the first enterprise UAV to receive EU C6 category certification, enabling BVLOS flight without prior approval.

Sabertooth is a hybrid AUV/ROV from Saab offering tether-free autonomous operation or tethered teleoperation with six degrees of freedom and 360-degree hovering, used for subsea inspection, maintenance and repair. The single-hull variant reaches 1,200 m depth and the double-hull variant 3,000 m.
depthRating: 1200 m (single-hull, 650 kg, 5 kts); 3000 m (double-hull, 1300 kg, 4 kts)

description: Matrice 5T is a compact enterprise drone from DJI launched in November 2026, combining LiDAR, mmWave radar and visual sensors with 1K thermal imaging and IP55 sealing for emergency response, inspection and surveying work. It offers up to 59 minutes of flight time and relay modes for extended range.

HullWiper is a remotely operated underwater vehicle that removes ship hull fouling using adjustable seawater jets under variable pressure rather than brushes or abrasives, avoiding damage to anti-fouling coatings. The UAE-based company operates its patented ROV cleaning service at ports worldwide, including a 2024 Singapore expansion.

Sentaero 6 is a fixed-wing uncrewed aerial system from Censys Technologies built for over-the-horizon BVLOS inspection of power grids and infrastructure. It offers two-hour flight endurance, a 90-mile command-and-control range, onboard AI processing via CensWise software and an ASTM-certified parachute.

Gladius Mini S is a compact five-thruster underwater ROV from CHASING (Chasing Innovation) built for underwater photography and inspection, rated to 100 m depth with a 4K/30fps camera and a standard 328-foot tether.

Optimus 1-EX (Optimus) is a drone-in-a-box platform from Airobotics (an Ondas Holdings company) with an integrated airbase for autonomous takeoff, landing, battery exchange and payload swapping between 2D/3D mapping, LiDAR and dual EO/IR cameras. In 2023 it became the first non-air-carrier UAS to receive a full FAA airworthiness Type Certificate, after prior commercial deployment in UAE smart-city and public-safety operations.

Bee is a small autonomous security drone from Sunflower Labs that docks and recharges at a companion Hive base station, flying automated property patrols triggered by ground sensors. It weighs 1.56 kg, flies about 15 minutes per charge and recharges at the Hive in under 15 minutes, forming the Beehive 24/7 surveillance system for homes and estates.

Probot 1.0 is an autonomous underwater robot from Norwegian company Probotic that continuously inspects and cleans fish-farm net pens at sea, improving fish welfare and catching net wear or damage early. Probotic was acquired by Scale Aquaculture in 2025.

Gavia is a compact, modular autonomous underwater vehicle from Teledyne Gavia (part of Teledyne Marine) used for seabed mapping, surveillance and survey missions to 500 m depth. It measures 1.8 m long, reaches 5.5 knots, runs up to eight hours per swappable battery module and can be deployed by two people.

Armada 78 is a class of 78 m uncrewed surface vessels operated by Ocean Infinity as motherships that launch and recover AUVs and ROVs for subsea survey and inspection work. Built by Vard Vung Tau, each vessel has two moonpools, DP2 positioning, 1,000-tonne cargo capacity and diesel-electric hybrid propulsion reaching 14 knots.

SOTEN is a made-in-Japan industrial drone from ACSL (Autonomous Control Systems Laboratory) built with secured communications, flight data and imagery for disaster response, infrastructure inspection and survey work, positioned as a domestic alternative to Chinese-made enterprise drones. It carries hot-swappable EO/IR, multispectral or zoom cameras and is IP43 rated.

NearthWIND Pro is an autonomous wind-turbine blade inspection drone from Nearthlab that performs single-button autonomous flights, compressing roughly six hours of manual rope-access inspection into about 15 minutes per turbine. Paired with the Zoomable AI data platform, it has inspected over 100,000 blades across 40-plus countries at 0.3 mm defect-detection resolution.

EZ Lite+ is a portable, tethered drone-in-a-box system from Brooklyn-based Easy Aerial, packed in a transport case for rapid deployment of automated aerial surveillance and inspection at remote or temporary sites such as military bases and ports.

Orion 2 is a tethered hexacopter drone from French manufacturer Elistair built for continuous round-the-clock surveillance and industrial monitoring. It flies indefinitely via a 330 ft micro-tether supplying power and data, carries up to 2 kg of payload at an 8.5 kg max takeoff weight, and can be deployed by a single operator in minutes.

MegaDock is a robotic drone-in-a-box hangar unveiled by Skydio at Ascend 2026 to support its F10 Lightrunner fixed-wing drone. It houses up to five aircraft for concurrent missions from one location and uses a suction-based robotic gripper to launch and land aircraft without ground crew; customer deployments begin in 2027.

DoorDash Air is a purpose-built autonomous delivery aircraft launched by DoorDash in October 2026, using a winch system to lower and collect orders without landing. It began piloting in Northern California with restaurant partners including Chipotle, Popeyes and Momo N Curry, coordinated through DoorDash's autonomous delivery platform.

Eureka is an autonomous seabed robot from Impossible Metals that selectively harvests polymetallic nodules using machine-vision selection and positive buoyancy to rise with its payload instead of riser pumps. In November 2026 it completed a field trial collecting nodules at roughly 4,000 m depth.

Harvest 100 is a heavy-lift autonomous agricultural spray drone from Rantizo built with 70%+ US or allied parts and NDAA compliance as an American-made alternative to imported spray drones. It is designed to treat up to 500 acres per day with terrain mapping, obstacle avoidance and modular payload tanks.

AYRE CX is an American-designed and manufactured agricultural spray-and-spread drone from Michigan-based Exedy Drones, offering a 13.2-gallon spray tank and 18.5-gallon spread hopper on one airframe with RTK terrain-following navigation, obstacle detection and autonomous takeoff-to-landing operation. It launched via reservation in late 2026 amid a push for domestically built alternatives to Chinese spray drones.

Sibiu Pro is a modular underwater ROV from Spanish maker Nido Robotics rated to 300 m depth, built for inspection and research with a 1080p camera, four 1,500-lumen lights and swappable payload modules.

Oli is an autonomous robotic coffee-bar kiosk from San Francisco-based Oli Robotics that grinds beans, pulls espresso, textures milk and dispenses up to 40 syrups to make espresso drinks, iced coffee and smoothies without a human barista. The company advertises roughly 40 drinks per hour from a 17-square-foot (1.6 m2) footprint and 24/7 unattended operation. Units are sold for 59,000 USD or leased at 4,990 USD per month, with a reference deployment at Frontier Tower in San Francisco.

RoboBurger is a fully automated burger-vending kiosk from a Brooklyn, New York startup that cooks and assembles a fresh burger on demand inside a roughly 10-square-foot unit, popularized on Shark Tank. The Gen 3 version, open for pre-order at 27,500 USD with a 5,000 USD deposit (limited to 200 units), is described by the maker as its first version built for mass production and plug-in installation without special power or plumbing. Earlier generations have been deployed in New Jersey and other U.S. locations since 2022.

Zume (founded 2015 as Zume Pizza in Camarillo, California) built delivery vans fitted with 56 GPS-equipped automated ovens that finished baking pizzas en route and a self-cleaning robotic cutter that sliced pies on arrival. SoftBank's Vision Fund invested 375 million USD in November 2018 at a 2.25 billion USD valuation, but Zume shelved the pizza-robot concept by 2020 over food-quality complaints and pivoted to compostable packaging before shutting down in June 2023.

Auto-S was a four-wheeled shelf-scanning retail robot from Pittsburgh-founded, San Francisco-based Bossa Nova Robotics that used 2D/3D cameras and lidar to roam store aisles and flag out-of-stock items, pricing errors and other shelf irregularities. Walmart piloted the robots from 2017, expanding to roughly 350 stores by 2019, but ended the partnership in late 2020 after deciding the robots were not effective enough for its unstructured retail floors, a decision that led to major layoffs at the company.

Chippy is a robotic-arm kitchen assistant from Pasadena, California-based Miso Robotics, maker of the Flippy fry-station robot, built to fry and season tortilla chips. It was piloted at a Chipotle location starting March 2022 (widely reported by CNBC, TechCrunch, Forbes and others) alongside Miso's other food-prep robots. Miso's current lineup page lists only Flippy, and Chippy's old product URL now returns a 404 error, indicating the unit has been discontinued.

Sippy is a drink-dispensing kitchen robot from Pasadena, California-based Miso Robotics, tested alongside the Flippy 2 fry robot at Jack in the Box locations starting April 2022 (reported by TechCrunch, Forbes, Restaurant Dive and others) and later featured together with Flippy on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. Miso's current products page lists only Flippy among its active lineup, and Sippy's former product URL now returns a 404 error, indicating the unit is no longer an active offering.

Artly (Artly AI, also branded Artly Robot Coffee) is a Seattle-founded startup whose Barista Bot uses a robotic arm with computer vision and deep-learning-based path planning and physical reasoning to grind, brew, texture milk and pour latte art for customized coffee drinks. The company operates and franchises staffed-by-robot cafe kiosks across the Seattle area and other US cities, offering purchase, lease and franchise packages that bundle the barista module, tech support, marketing and supplies.

Caper Cart is an AI-powered smart shopping cart, originally developed by Caper AI before Instacart acquired the company for 350 million USD in 2021, that uses a built-in camera, weight sensors and a touchscreen to recognize items as shoppers add them and enable walk-out contactless checkout. It has been deployed at more than ten retailers including ShopRite, Bristol Farms, Geissler's and Coles (Australia). Instacart announced in October 2026 that it is winding down the Caper Cart business through 2027.

SSN-UJA is a top-discharge nigiri-sushi rice ball forming robot from Japanese sushi-equipment maker Suzumo. It shapes up to 3,200 vinegared-rice balls per hour in 16, 18, 20 or 22 gram portions, dispensing them vertically onto a conveyor so chefs can add toppings and hand-press each piece, letting the machine run compactly inside sushi-restaurant serving counters. It draws a maximum 150 W from a standard AC100V outlet and holds about 5.5 kg of rice in its hopper.
throughput: 3200 pieces/hour

description: BotristaPro is a countertop beverage-automation machine from San Francisco-based Botrista Technologies that crafts a drink in under 12 seconds using 14 anti-cross-contamination dispensing nozzles, 8 refrigerated ingredient bag-in-box containers and 4 ambient-storage units, with a self-cleaning cycle and a honeycomb blender that simulates shaken or foamed texture. The company reports the machine is deployed with enterprise restaurant and retail clients at more than 6,000 locations across 42 US states, sold as a drink-as-a-service subscription rather than outright purchase.

Hyper Robotics builds a fully autonomous fast-food kitchen packaged inside a standard 40-foot shipping container, letting operators run a staffless restaurant that can prepare pizza, burgers, bowls, salads, baked goods and ice cream. The company, founded in Israel in 2019, deployed its first unit with Pizza Hut Israel, opening what was reported as the first automated Pizza Hut location in 2022.

PadBot W2 is an autonomous hotel-delivery robot from Guangzhou-based PadBot Robotics that carries items from the lobby to guest room doors, using autonomous navigation with elevator and access-gate integration, secure dual compartments and automatic return-to-dock charging. PadBot markets it alongside a related restaurant-oriented Food Delivery Robot W3s as part of a wider service-robot lineup that also includes reception, security, cleaning and telepresence robots.

PadBot X3 is a dual-screen reception and greeting robot from Guangzhou-based PadBot Robotics, built for welcoming and guiding visitors in offices, hotels, showrooms and other public spaces. It is part of PadBot's broader commercial service-robot lineup that also includes the W2 hotel delivery robot, P2 telepresence robot and S2/S5 security patrol robots.

Octochef (also called Robot-Chef) is Yo-Kai Express's autonomous cooking kiosk that prepares ramen, udon, dim sum, pasta, rice bowls and dessert items from a menu of more than 30 recipes, cooking each bowl in about 90 seconds using the company's proprietary Step Cooking process and an AI platform for dynamic pricing and inventory management. The California-based company has shown the robot at CES and deployed units with partners such as South Korea's Pulmuone, operating the kiosks for unattended, 24/7 service.

SEMBLR was a modular, robotic-arm-based meal-assembly system from UK food-robotics startup Karakuri (founded 2018 by Barney Wragg), designed to build bowls, salads and other multi-ingredient meals for restaurants and supermarkets. Ocado invested about 4.75 million GBP for a near-20-percent stake in 2019, but Karakuri was unable to secure further funding or an acquirer -- including failed talks with fryer maker Henny Penny -- and shut down in June 2023.

FRYR was an automated fry-line system from UK food-robotics startup Karakuri that controlled frying time, temperature and quantity for restaurant kitchens, developed alongside the company's SEMBLR meal-assembly robot. After Ocado's 2019 investment and failed later-stage funding or acquisition talks (including with fryer maker Henny Penny), Karakuri shut down in June 2023 before bringing FRYR to market at scale.

R1 was Nuro's first-generation, fully driverless delivery vehicle, just over 6 feet tall and about half the width of a sedan, carrying only cargo such as up to 12 grocery bags with no room for passengers. Nuro launched R1 with Kroger in Scottsdale, Arizona in August 2018 and announced a Domino's Pizza delivery partnership in Houston in 2019, before retiring the design in favor of the driverless R2.

R2 was Nuro's second-generation autonomous delivery vehicle, the first version built with no steering wheel, pedals or side mirrors. Testing began in Houston in February 2020, and the R2 was used to ferry medical supplies between California healthcare facilities and to deliver prescriptions for CVS Pharmacy starting in May 2020, ahead of the later R3 generation.

GO Bot (formerly branded Clevon 1) is a lightweight, Level 4 autonomous electric delivery robot from Tartu, Estonia-based indiGO Europe (rebranded from Clevon, under U.S. parent indiGOtech), built to drive on public roads for grocery, retail, parcel and hospital deliveries with one remote operator able to supervise multiple units. Clients cited by the company include DHL, REWE Group, DPD and Colruyt Group, and the company reports over four years of public-road operation in Europe without a reported safety incident.

M-Drone 4 is the fourth-generation food and parcel delivery drone from Chinese delivery platform Meituan, built for heavier payloads and smoother low-altitude flight than earlier generations; a longer-range M-Drone 4L variant followed in December 2025. Meituan's drones, dispatched through its M-Port transfer hubs and M-DaaS cloud scheduling system, completed their first user delivery in Shenzhen in January 2021 and received Civil Aviation Authority of China certification for commercial operation in February 2023, with coverage reported across Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing and Hong Kong exceeding 680 square kilometers by September 2026.

STEAMA is a steam-powered automated ramen cooking station from Bear Robotics, developed with SoftBank Robotics Corp, that cooks noodles and broth in about 90 seconds with minimal human intervention to replicate the taste of Japanese ramen restaurants. Bear Robotics, known for its Servi serving robots, demonstrated STEAMA live at the National Restaurant Association Show 2026 at McCormick Place in Chicago as part of a broader push into kitchen automation alongside its new FLAMA cooking robot.

FLAMA is a stir-fry and high-volume cooking robot from Bear Robotics, developed with SoftBank Robotics Corp, that uses intelligent heat control to cook a variety of pre-prepped ingredients through complex recipes at scale. It was demonstrated alongside Bear's STEAMA ramen station at the National Restaurant Association Show 2026 at McCormick Place in Chicago, extending the company's Servi-based hospitality robot lineup into kitchen cooking automation.

MobED (Mobile Eccentric Droid) Basic is a controller-operated mobile robot platform developed by Hyundai Motor Group's Robotics LAB, built on proprietary Drive-and-Lift (DnL) suspension for stable movement over uneven surfaces, inclines and curbs. It won the Best of Innovation Award in Robotics at CES 2026, with mass production of the modular platform for logistics, broadcasting, guidance and digital-signage uses starting in early 2026.

MobED (Mobile Eccentric Droid) Pro is the autonomous variant of Hyundai Motor Group Robotics LAB's modular mobility platform, adding integrated LiDAR-camera fusion sensors for self-navigation versus the controller-operated Basic model. Built on the same Drive-and-Lift (DnL) suspension for uneven terrain, it won CES 2026's Best of Innovation Award in Robotics and entered mass production in early 2026 for logistics, delivery, broadcasting and guidance applications.

Scan & Go is an AI-powered autonomous robotic solution from Doosan Robotics, co-developed with Canada's Maple Advanced Robotics (MARI), that uses physics-based intelligence and laser-based 3D vision to read complex geometries from point-cloud data and generate robotic tool paths without CAD modeling or manual programming. Mounted on a self-driving forklift, it autonomously navigates to and performs sanding, grinding and inspection on large composite structures such as aircraft fuselages, wind turbine blades and building facades. It won two CES 2026 Innovation Awards, including Best of Innovation in the AI category.

Bambini Kids is a pediatric overground walking exoskeleton from Cosmo Robotics (parent of ExoAtlet), named a CES 2026 Innovation Award honoree as one of the first child exoskeletons with powered ankle motion. It is designed specifically for children ages 2.5-7 with congenital or acquired neurological disorders, offering both active and passive gait-training modes for pediatric rehabilitation.

Bambini Teens is the larger-size companion to Cosmo Robotics' (ExoAtlet) Bambini Kids pediatric exoskeleton, named a CES 2026 Innovation Award honoree as one of the first overground walking exoskeletons with powered ankle motion for children and teens with congenital or acquired neurological disorders.

CMR is ROKAE's composite mobile-manipulator line, pairing an omnidirectional AMR chassis with ROKAE's SR or CR collaborative arms for material handling and automated tasks. The CMR-S lightweight variant can pass through 800 mm aisles and supports 20 kg or 100 kg payloads, with specific models such as CMR-S-V4SD1 (150 kg chassis weight, 7 kg arm payload, 988 mm working range) and CMR-S-V4SD3 (300 kg chassis weight, 12 kg arm payload, 1434 mm working range), both reaching 1.4 m/s with dual-laser SLAM navigation and about 12 hours of runtime per charge.

XCD101 is a 1.0-tonne backpack-style autonomous mobile robot (AMR) from EP Equipment, built on a dual-wheel differential drive for smooth forward, reverse and in-place turning in warehouse aisles. It has a 235 kg service weight, travels at 6.48 km/h laden (7.20 km/h unladen), and runs on a 48V Li-Ion battery pack weighing 20 kg.
XP15 is a 1.5-tonne automatic electric pallet truck from EP Equipment, positioned as a cost-effective entry into autonomous intralogistics. It runs on a 24V Li-Ion battery pack weighing 14 kg.

XPA152 is a 1.5-tonne AI-guided electric pallet truck from EP Equipment for automated intralogistics. It travels at 1/1.5 km/h laden/unladen with a 5-10% max gradeability, and runs on a 24V, 100Ah Li-Ion battery pack weighing 30 kg.

RANGER is a high-payload omnidirectional mobile robot platform from AgileX Robotics with four-wheel steering supporting Ackermann steering, lateral movement and in-place rotation. It provides up to a 150 kg payload and large top integration area for cargo modules, robotic arms and industrial computers, reaches 2.6 m/s, climbs 20-degree grades at full load, and runs about 2 hours per charge, with a modular UPS for low-downtime operation.

HaiPick A42-E6S is a grappling-hook Autonomous Case-handling Robot (ACR) from Hai Robotics, designed to retrieve totes from single- to triple-deep storage racks. It carries up to a 300 kg payload, reduces required horizontal case spacing to 30 mm, supports up to three-deep tote storage, and includes LiDAR-based collision avoidance.

HaiPick A42T is a telescopic-lift Autonomous Case-handling Robot (ACR) from Hai Robotics, described as the world's first telescopic ACR able to pick and store plastic totes and carton boxes at heights up to 12 m. It carries 30 kg payloads, holds up to nine totes on multiple storage trays at once, and is CE and NRTL certified.

MobED (Mobile Eccentric Droid) is a four-wheeled autonomous mobility robot platform from Hyundai Motor Group, with independently steerable, height-adjustable wheels that let it traverse uneven terrain and climb steps up to about 20 cm. It was shown as a production-ready commercial platform at iREX 2025 and CES 2026, with a modular top rail so partner firms can attach payloads for patrol, delivery, waste collection or dual-arm manipulation tasks; Hyundai has since formed a MobED Alliance with Korean robotics firms (Gaon Robotics, Wego Robotics, Roas) to build applications on it.

The R4 Electric Power is an autonomous, fully electric specialty-crop robot from New Holland (a CNH Industrial brand) built for narrow vineyards with 1.0-1.5 m row spacing. It is 1.38 m tall, 0.7 m wide, weighs about 1 tonne, runs on a 40 kWh battery, and uses GPS, lidar and vision cameras for autonomous inter-row mowing, tillage and spraying; it was unveiled at Agritechnica 2025.

The R4 Hybrid Power is an autonomous specialty-crop robot from New Holland (CNH Industrial) built for orchards and fruit rows of 1.5 m or wider spacing. It is 1.2 m wide, weighs about 1,400 kg, combines a 59 hp/44 kW diesel engine (able to run on vegetable-oil-based fuel) with two 4 kWh battery packs for electric-only operation, and uses GPS, lidar and vision for autonomous mowing, tillage and intelligent spraying; it was unveiled at Agritechnica 2025.

RACK is an autonomy retrofit kit from Zurich-based Gravis Robotics (spun out of ETH Zurich, founded 2022) that converts excavators and wheel loaders into self-driving earthmoving machines, adding LiDAR/camera sensing, edge compute and a tablet (Slate) control interface. In August 2026 Gravis raised a $200 million Series A led by SoftBank, reported as the largest Series A in construction-robotics history.

The MyMR-300 is the smallest model in Comau's MyMR family of autonomous mobile robots, carrying payloads up to 300 kg for production-line supply, kitting and warehouse material transport. It combines hybrid AMR/AGV navigation with real-time obstacle avoidance and fleet management, and can be fitted with lifters, conveyors or shelving attachments; the family was unveiled at Automatica 2025.

The MyMR-500 is the mid-capacity model in Comau's MyMR family of autonomous mobile robots, carrying payloads up to 500 kg for production-line supply, kitting and warehouse material transport. It combines hybrid AMR/AGV navigation with real-time obstacle avoidance and fleet management, and can be fitted with lifters, conveyors or shelving attachments; the family was unveiled at Automatica 2025.

The MyMR-1500 is the heavy-duty model in Comau's MyMR family of autonomous mobile robots, carrying payloads up to 1,500 kg for warehouse automation and heavy intralogistics transport. It combines hybrid AMR/AGV navigation with real-time obstacle avoidance and fleet management, and can be fitted with lifters, conveyors or shelving attachments; the family was unveiled at Automatica 2025.

PalletizHD+ is an AI-powered palletizing cobot system from Doosan Robotics built on the company's PalletizOS software and SwiftMove motion-optimization technology. It can stack up to 11 boxes per minute, handling multiple boxes at once, and automatically generates stacking patterns from box and pallet dimensions through a smartphone-like interface with no extensive programming; it was shown at Automate 2026 in Chicago.

The SSi Mantra 3 is a multi-arm surgical robotic system from India's SS Innovations, used for minimally invasive procedures in cardiac, thoracic, urological, gynecological, general, gastrointestinal and head-and-neck surgery. It supports dual-console telesurgery and has been used in long-distance robotic telesurgery demonstrations spanning thousands of kilometers; the company holds Indian CDSCO manufacturing approval and submitted the system to the US FDA for clearance in December 2025.

Sculptor is a logistics operations robot from Shenyi Robotics (a Tsinghua University-linked startup, now backed by strategic investor Geek+) built on the company's self-developed SE-1 embodied foundation model. It identifies mixed boxes of different sizes, materials and random placements, then autonomously adjusts its grasping and placement strategy to continuously sort and stack them into stable, multi-layer pallets in logistics warehouses. It was unveiled at the 2026 China International Industry Fair (CIIF) in October 2026.

The AgBot T2 is an autonomous tracked tractor from Dutch manufacturer AgXeed, powered by a 230 hp Deutz four-cylinder diesel engine with 170 l/min hydraulics and a 9-tonne rear-linkage lifting capacity. It weighs about 8 tonnes, runs on 900 mm or 610 mm tracks for low 30 kPa soil pressure, uses four cameras for autonomous field operation monitored via the AgXeed platform, and was launched at Agritechnica 2025 starting at 295,000 EUR.

Naiture Beam is a laser-weeding machine developed by Naiture, part of Germany's Westhof Bio Group, built with a vegetable farmer to kill weeds in crop rows with targeted lasers instead of herbicide. Naiture planned to manufacture five units in 2026 as it moves the AI-assisted weeder from prototype to limited production.
